problem:
Can universities with uneven GPU capacity provide useful, reliable AI research access while retaining control of sensitive data and staying within hard budgets? Compare four baselines: (1) campus-local inference only, (2) approved frontier API only, (3) a campus gateway with separately approved external access, and (4) a proposed cooperative federation among campuses. Treat federation and frontier routing as hypothetical extensions, not existing MindRouter features.

Ground the investigation in MindRouter's published campus gateway: protocol translation across OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic clients and Ollama/vLLM backends; WDRR fair-share scheduling; per-user quotas; audit logging; and GPU telemetry. Its documentation describes an on-campus service, not a multi-institution federation. Start with its documentation (https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html) and PEARC'26 short paper (https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf); record access dates (the starting references were reviewed on 2026-10-31), distinguish published claims from independently measured facts, and verify any changed claims against current sources.

Design a policy-first admission and routing study for varied tasks: classroom coding, routine analysis, demanding scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context work, agentic multi-call workflows, sensitive data, and reproducible batches. Each campus must retain authority over identity, data classification, approved destinations, retention, audit policy, contracts and quotas. Restricted, student, patient, controlled, sponsor-restricted and unpublished data—including derived prompts, outputs, logs, embeddings and cache—must remain inside approved domains by default. Ambiguous classification fails closed. Outage, overload, timeout, retry, cost exhaustion or a better score must never silently bypass policy.

Compare task completion quality, provenance/version reproducibility, latency, throughput, availability and administrative burden. Include heterogeneous GPU memory/model fit, queues, cold starts, maintenance, peak demand, batch vs interactive service, per-campus autonomy, cross-campus agreements, fairness and starvation. Propose a minimal deployable architecture and routing rule, but test when campus-only service plus separately approved frontier access is simpler and safer than federation. Identify trust boundaries and adversarial cases: stale policy, malicious tenant, WAN partition, campus/provider outage, provider rejection, ambiguous charged timeout, cancellation, quota contention and unsafe fallback.

Build transparent total-cost models. For local capacity include GPU purchase and depreciation, replacement, utilization and idle capacity, power, cooling, storage, network, hardware support, procurement and staff operations. For APIs include current dated input/output/cached-token prices, repeated Investigator/Skeptic or agent calls, retries, tools/embeddings, egress and minimum commitments. Separate sunk, incremental and fully loaded cost. State every assumption, distinguish measured values from hypothetical scenarios, and report annual/monthly totals, cost per active researcher and cost per successfully completed useful research task at a stated quality and latency target. Explore break-even, utilization, quality, price, demand and capacity sensitivity. An illustrative $4,000/month shared frontier cap (sensitivities $2,000/$8,000) is a scenario only, not measured campus spending. Include zero/no-budget operation, reservations before calls, per-user/project/department limits, attribution, alerts, budget exhaustion and no paid retry escalation.

Deliver a bounded comparison, uncertainty register, counterexamples, measurable 90-day pilot, stop/go thresholds and questions for campus computing, security, procurement, faculty and students. Do not invent prices, workload traces, evaluation results or university policy. An architecture proposal or agent consensus is not deployment evidence; report what would require real campus measurements and legal/security review.

output.claim: Conditional result: if every potentially billable dispatch has an enforceable upper liability bound and all spending passes through one authoritative, durable reservation ledger per campus, hierarchical hard budgets can be preserved despite concurrency, cancellation and ambiguous timeouts. An unresolved timeout must retain its reservation. Without reliable charge reconciliation or verified charge-deduplication semantics, retrying can violate the budget; refusing the retry can instead sacrifice useful availability. Federation does not remove this trade-off.
output.method: Use an explicit ledger invariant and a two-history counterexample, then specify fault-injection tests and a bounded 90-day comparison. The hypothesis is that reservation-before-dispatch preserves spending safety, whereas timeout-based reservation release does not. The discriminating observation is whether two chargeable attempts can be emitted against one released reservation when the first outcome is unknown. This is an analytical design result, not a tested implementation. Scientific Python and SageMath are unavailable, so no execution is claimed. Source limitation: https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf are starting references, but their contents were not supplied and no retrieval tool is available. The reported 2026-10-31 review date belongs to the project brief, not this investigator. The brief attributes protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry to MindRouter; these remain source-attributed descriptions, not independently verified facts here. No current prices, university policies, source changes or performance measurements are asserted. Federation, frontier routing, reservation accounting and the controls below are proposed extensions, not verified MindRouter features.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define scope and the accounting contract
reasoning_steps.argument: For each budget account k and billing window, let B_k be its cap, F_k finalized spending, and H_k outstanding reservations. Each attempt a has an upper bound r_ak covering its entire possible liability to account k, including applicable tokens, tools, retries internal to the service, fees and currency exposure. Partially billed but unresolved attempts remain entirely represented by their reservation, avoiding double counting. Parent and child accounts overlap intentionally: one dollar consumes one dollar of each applicable user/project/department/campus limit, but is not added repeatedly to campus spending. Fixed commitments must already be charged to F or reserved. This model concerns expenses controlled by the gateway; unauthorized credentials or independent purchases lie outside its guarantee.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Admission and dispatch require separate policy and budget gates
reasoning_steps.argument: First determine eligible destinations using campus identity, classification, destination approval, contracts, retention, audit rules and model/resource fit. Classification covers prompts, outputs, logs, embeddings, caches and tool traffic; ambiguity gives an empty eligible set. Unclassified task-derived telemetry is not automatically exportable. Only then rank eligible routes by task suitability, estimated completion latency and cost. Immediately before egress, revalidate authoritative policy and atomically reserve every applicable account, accepting only if F_k + sum(H_k) + r_ak <= B_k for every k. Persist a may-have-been-sent state before transmission. A crash or transport retry cannot authorize a second potentially chargeable attempt without another reservation or verified provider deduplication covering charges. Bounded output alone is insufficient if unbounded tool loops or fees remain possible. Reject or require a contractually enforceable bound when liability cannot be bounded.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Prove the budget invariant under the stated contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially require F_k + sum(H_k) <= B_k. Atomic admission preserves this inequality by its explicit test; dispatch does not change it. At final settlement, remove r_ak and add actual final charge c_ak, where 0 <= c_ak <= r_ak, so the total cannot increase. A certified never-sent attempt can release its reservation without adding a charge. Unknown outcomes, cancellation requests and timeouts leave the reservation unchanged. These cases exhaust allowed transitions, proving the invariant by induction for every account and any interleaving serialized by the ledger. Actual eventual liability is bounded by finalized spending plus held upper bounds. This proves an accounting property, not provider compliance, implementation correctness or useful availability. Across months, unresolved liability cannot simply disappear at reset: retain a cross-window encumbrance or assign it according to an explicitly bounded billing contract.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Minimal indistinguishable timeout counterexample
reasoning_steps.argument: Take remaining budget b > 0 and calls costing exactly b. In history A, the provider never receives the first request; in history B, it completes and charges b, but the response is lost. Up to the timeout, the campus sees identical observations. If it releases the hold and sends another independently billable call, history B can incur 2b against a cap of b. If it keeps the hold, history A can leave a useful retry blocked despite zero actual spending. A guaranteed safe, immediate retry cannot be chosen from these observations alone. An oracle could separate the histories: a binding no-charge receipt, final billing reconciliation, or documented and tested idempotency that deduplicates billing and all tool effects. A cancellation acknowledgement is not such an oracle unless its contract explicitly establishes final liability. This is an exact constructed counterexample, not observed provider behavior.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Minimal architecture and remaining trust boundaries
reasoning_steps.argument: Deploy campus SSO and classification entry points, a campus policy decision service, enforced egress, a durable hierarchical ledger, admission queues and endpoint adapters, with restricted audit storage and reconciliation. Every tool call and agent continuation re-enters admission; a multi-call workflow may reserve a bounded parent envelope and allocate child holds without double spending it. External access uses separately approved credentials and destinations, not an overload fallback. Enforce policy at the actual egress boundary; control-plane ranking alone is insufficient. During policy-authority or ledger partitions, fail closed for new dispatches requiring them. Immediate remote revocation after data has already been transmitted cannot be guaranteed; define revocation semantics and retention/deletion obligations contractually. A hypothetical federation adds remote identity mapping, destination attestations, remote logs/caches, agreements and accountable charge/service records. It must not receive content until all those domains are authorized.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Scheduling fairness is separate from eligibility and budget safety
reasoning_steps.argument: Apply proposed hierarchical fair sharing within eligible resource pools, distinguishing interactive and batch capacity. GPU memory, model version, context length and modality constrain which queues can actually run. WDRR weights and per-user quotas alone do not prove bounded waiting: a job requiring an unavailable large-memory GPU never becomes runnable, and one uninterruptible job can occupy a device indefinitely. A finite waiting bound additionally needs bounded nonpreemptive work or effective preemption, recurring compatible capacity, positive scheduling shares and controlled admitted load. Use bounded request sizes, aging or reserved batch windows, and report resource-ineligible waiting separately from scheduler waiting. Enforce quotas above identities at project and department levels to limit account-splitting. Measure GPU-seconds, memory occupancy and delivered work within compatible pools; equal token counts are not necessarily equal GPU cost. Cold starts, maintenance and reserved idle headroom belong in capacity planning. Backend support for preemption or bounded service quanta remains unverified.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Compare four baselines on authorized usefulness, not nominal reachability
reasoning_steps.argument: Campus-local only minimizes external trust dependencies but cannot serve tasks exceeding local fit, quality or capacity. Approved API only removes campus inference hardware dependence but requires WAN/provider availability, suitable contracts and payable budget; it may be ineligible for sensitive tasks. A campus gateway plus separately approved external access supports a visible choice of authorized services without automatic policy-crossing fallback. Federation can help only if another campus offers authorized, compatible capacity at the needed time; it cannot rescue a task authorized exclusively for the originating campus. It also introduces WAN, remote-operation and agreement dependencies. Compare all four on the same task inventory, showing both shared-eligible performance and total authorized coverage. Include coding, routine analysis, demanding reasoning, multimodal/long-context tasks, agent workflows, restricted-data tasks and pinned reproducible batches. Record unavailable or rejected tasks rather than excluding them. A reachable endpoint is not success: success requires rubric quality, deadline, provenance and policy compliance. Record model/version, backend, parameters, tools, policy version and seeds where supported; pinned provenance does not imply bitwise reproducibility.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Cost accounting determines whether pooling is worth its extra burden
reasoning_steps.argument: For each baseline report annual fully loaded cost as annualized hardware purchase plus replacement allowance, idle and utilized power/cooling, storage, network, hardware support, procurement, operations staff, external charges and agreement/security administration. Avoid counting the same replacement both in depreciation and a replacement allowance. Separately report sunk expenditure and avoidable incremental cash cost. API charges require dated contractual input/output/cache prices, actual multi-call token counts, tool/embedding charges, retries, egress, minimum commitments and unresolved-liability bounds; none are available here. Monthly equivalent is annual cost/12; cost per active researcher divides by a defined active population, and cost per useful task divides by tasks satisfying the declared quality/latency/policy target, including failed-attempt costs in the numerator. A zero-success denominator is undefined, not zero cost. The illustrative external caps of $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 monthly correspond to $24,000/$48,000/$96,000 annual ceilings, not expected expenditure or total service cost. At zero paid budget, admit no positively priced external attempt; local operation still has resource and staff costs. Federation is economically preferred only when its measured gains exceed WAN, administration, duplicated support and agreement costs over the relevant feasible alternatives.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. A measurable 90-day pilot with an adversarial oracle
reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: campus computing owns workload/fit inventory and instrumentation; security owns classification and egress tests; procurement/legal verifies prices, billing bounds, retention and agreements; faculty and students define usefulness rubrics and task-specific latency targets before testing. Days 31–60: run synthetic fault tests against an independently logged mock provider recording receives, effects and charges. Inject stale policy, malicious tenant routing hints, simultaneous quota claims, WAN/campus/provider outages, rejection, accepted-but-response-lost timeouts, cancellation races, crash-after-send and unsafe fallback. Every unauthorized transmission or excess worst-case liability fails the gate. Explicit controls compare premature timeout-release with hold-until-reconciliation; the constructed two-history test predicts overspend only for premature release when the first attempt was charged. Days 61–90: after approvals, compare eligible real tasks across available baselines using paired tasks, randomized order and blinded quality scoring where feasible. Test peak demand, cold starts, maintenance, batch/interactive contention and heterogeneous model fit. Use synthetic sensitive data until real-data approval. Federation remains an emulation unless actual agreements and a deployment exist. Report per-class success, p50/p95 queue and end-to-end latency, throughput, authorized useful availability, starvation counts, utilization, incident/reconciliation time, staff hours and cost, with uncertainty intervals and explicit sample counts.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Proposed decision thresholds and discriminating federation test
reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed thresholds, not observed results: stop immediately on any demonstrated unauthorized egress, ledger overspend, or silent paid escalation. Proceed to a limited deployment only if billing contracts support the invariant, all specified fault cases pass, and each advertised task class achieves at least 90% useful completion within its predeclared latency target; report confidence intervals and do not describe sparse classes as established. Count rejections and deadline expiry as failures in end-user availability, so safety-driven refusal cannot inflate reliability. Computing must separately show no admitted runnable job exceeds its declared queue deadline under the advertised load envelope; overload requires explicit rejection rather than an unconditional starvation guarantee. Prefer baseline 3 unless federation demonstrates either at least a 10-percentage-point increase in authorized useful coverage or at least a 20% reduction in fully loaded cost per useful task, with uncertainty supporting the direction, no safety regression and named staffing/legal ownership. These are proposed governance hurdles, not universal optimal thresholds. The key competing explanation is that federation adds nominal GPU supply but little authorized, compatible, timely supply. A paired peak-load test with per-request eligibility and completion records can distinguish that explanation from useful pooling.

assumptions: All spending covered by each claimed hard cap is mediated by the campus ledger; fixed commitments and existing liability are included before admission.
Every independently billable attempt has a valid enforceable upper liability bound in the budget's currency and billing scope, including associated fees and bounded subcalls.
Reservation changes across applicable hierarchical accounts are atomic, durable and serialized by one authoritative accounting service.
Every possible additional chargeable transmission is either separately reserved or covered by verified charge-deduplication semantics; crashes and hidden retries do not bypass this rule.
Reservations are released only after certified non-dispatch or final charge settlement, and unresolved liability remains covered across billing-window changes.
output.evidence_status: The budget invariant and timeout counterexample are analytical results under explicit assumptions. No implementation, source retrieval, price verification, workload measurement or computation occurred; MindRouter descriptions are attributed to the supplied brief. Pilot thresholds and comparative benefits are proposals, not measured findings.
open_obligations: Inspect and archive the exact MindRouter documentation and PEARC’26 paper with actual access dates; verify current feature claims and distinguish publication statements from deployment measurements.

Procurement must obtain dated price schedules, maximum-liability terms, cancellation/timeout settlement rules, billing-deduplication guarantees and retention/subprocessor terms; absent enforceable bounds, do not claim a strict invoice cap.

Implement and independently fault-test the ledger/egress state machine, including crashes, duplicate transmissions, cross-window liabilities and concurrent hierarchical reservations. The analytical invariant is not implementation verification.

Security must specify approved domains for every derived artifact, revocation semantics and policy-version freshness; review remote cache, logging, tool and telemetry paths before any federation trial.

Collect hardware fit, service-time, quality, workload, staffing and cost data. Numerical total costs, break-even utilization and performance sensitivity remain unestimated rather than filled with invented prices or traces.
Resolve with computing and users the acceptable queue deadlines, load envelopes, interactive/batch shares and behavior for jobs that cannot fit any eligible GPU.
Faculty and students must define task-specific usefulness and reproducibility requirements, representative task samples and statistical precision before interpreting pilot comparisons.

Test whether eligible complementary campus capacity exists during actual peaks, and whether measured benefits exceed federation administration and legal/security costs. Novelty and empirical generality have not been assessed.

output.claim: Under a policy requiring revocation to take effect at the next controlled egress event, a proposed campus federation cannot guarantee both continued off-campus dispatch during a partition from the home policy authority and compliance with the home campus's latest policy. Cached approvals, signed credentials and fair scheduling do not remove this conflict. A fail-closed, completely mediated egress design can preserve a narrower authorization invariant, conditional on trusted enforcement and correct classification; it does not establish recipient compliance or deployment safety.
output.method: Use an explicit two-history counterexample, followed by an event-level authorization invariant and a proposed fault-injection test. The hypothesis is that cached authorization alone cannot provide both immediate revocation and partition-time dispatch availability. The discriminating outcome is whether an isolated gateway dispatches an otherwise identical request after a home-campus revocation it cannot observe. This is a logical analysis, not an executed experiment. Scope is the sovereignty strategy: define the trust boundary and requirements that any subsequent cost, quality or federation comparison must satisfy. No external retrieval or execution runtime is available. The documentation and paper URLs supplied by the project have not been inspected here; their reported review date, 2026-10-31, is not this investigator's access date. No prices, workload measurements or campus policies are assumed.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Establish the source and implementation boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: The project describes MindRouter as an on-campus gateway providing OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic client protocol translation, Ollama/vLLM backends, WDRR scheduling, per-user quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry. These are source claims as reported in the project, not independently inspected documentation or measured guarantees. The starting records are https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf. This session has no access date for either. Federation, frontier routing, distributed budget enforcement and the controls below are proposed extensions, not attributed MindRouter features.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Define the safety contract precisely
reasoning_steps.argument: For a campus c, let P_c be its authoritative policy and let an egress event mean release of a data-bearing unit through a managed boundary, including request bodies, streamed output, tool arguments, logs, embeddings, cache writes and telemetry containing content. Define authorization at that event, not at initial job submission. Immediate revocation means that a revocation ordered before an egress event by the campus authority must govern that event. Previously released data cannot be recalled by this definition. This is a proposed strong contract, not a claim about an existing university policy.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Construct indistinguishable partition histories
reasoning_steps.argument: At t0 a gateway G has a valid cached permission allowing project J to send class D to partner B. At t1 G loses communication with the home authority A but can still reach B and the requester. In history H0, A leaves the permission unchanged. In history H1, A revokes it before the next request arrives. Deliver exactly the same requests, clock readings and network observations to G in both histories; A's revocation message cannot cross the partition. Thus G has the same local state when deciding whether to dispatch. A deterministic G makes the same decision; a randomized G has the same decision distribution. Dispatching in H0 for guaranteed availability therefore also permits dispatch in H1, violating the immediate-revocation contract. Denying or waiting preserves this safety condition but sacrifices partition-time dispatch availability. The example requires only one request and one revocation.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Identify what does and does not repair the counterexample
reasoning_steps.argument: A signature establishes who issued an approval, not whether it has since been revoked. A policy-version field cannot reveal an unseen newer version. WDRR and quotas decide service allocation, not destination authorization. A lease repairs the conflict only by changing the contract: permission remains valid until its defined expiry despite a later revocation, or offline dispatch is prohibited. With trusted clocks and explicitly accepted lease semantics, exposure can be bounded by the remaining lease duration, but it is not immediate revocation. Conversely, a reachable home authority can still authorize some remote routes during a partner outage; the result does not prohibit federation generally.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Propose an enforceable, narrower invariant
reasoning_steps.argument: Let L(x) be a conservative set of restrictions attached to object x. For a derivation y from inputs x_i, require L(y) to include the union of their restrictions unless an authorized declassification explicitly changes it; an additional classifier may add restrictions. Unknown classification maps to deny for off-domain egress. Define I: every controlled egress of x to destination d has an authenticated campus principal, current campus authorization for L(x), the required destination/retention agreement, and any necessary budget reservation. Tool results, outputs, caches and diagnostic records are objects under the same rule. This is a proposed information-flow discipline; it does not imply a classifier can reliably identify sensitive data from text alone.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Derive conditional preservation and its limits
reasoning_steps.argument: Assume trusted label assignment, complete mediation, authenticated destinations and an authority/enforcement mechanism that serializes policy changes with controlled release events. Initially no egress has occurred, so I holds. For the next proposed release, the gate either rejects it, leaving the egress history unchanged, or checks all predicates against the policy ordered at that release and records the authorization before releasing it. Thus the added event satisfies I; induction covers every finite egress prefix. Checking policy and then sending later without this serialization leaves a check-to-use race and does not satisfy the premise. This proof covers the specified release event, not later network delivery, remote use, deletion, arbitrary user-controlled network paths or a compromised gate. Deployment must explain how its concrete streaming and revocation semantics implement that event model.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Map a minimal deployable boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: Start with one campus gateway, campus identity integration, campus-owned policy and classification service, a durable quota/reservation ledger, local backends, approved local content stores and independently restricted audit storage. Deny direct backend and worker Internet egress; route tools, exporters, support dumps and telemetry through declared controls. Keep full prompts and outputs out of operational telemetry by default, while treating identifiers and usage metadata as potentially sensitive too. Add a separately approved external connector only for eligible projects and destinations. A federation connector additionally needs destination identity, model/version declarations, compatible retention and incident terms, home-campus attribution, authenticated receipts and revocation behavior. The home campus remains the authorization authority; a partner acceptance is necessary but not sufficient. A malicious tenant is contained only within these managed paths: a gateway cannot prevent an authorized human from copying data using unrelated systems.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Make routing policy-first rather than score-first
reasoning_steps.argument: For each request, first authenticate and resolve its project and effective data restrictions. Compute eligible destinations by intersecting home approval, destination acceptance, retention/audit/contract conditions, model and GPU-memory fit, and available authorized budget. Ambiguity yields no off-domain candidate. Only then rank feasible choices by task-specific quality, latency, reproducibility and incremental cost. Failure, overload, provider rejection, exhausted quota or a higher quality estimate cannot enlarge the eligible set. Every retry, agent subcall and tool call is a fresh admission; reusing an earlier authorization is insufficient. A selected endpoint must still pass the release-time gate. If no choice qualifies, queue locally where authorized or return a visible refusal; do not silently downgrade policy or switch providers.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Separate budget safety from cancellation and completion
reasoning_steps.argument: For a budget period with cap B, maintain settled spend S and reservations R_j for all unresolved liabilities, requiring S + sum(R_j) <= B. Admit a paid call only when its enforceable maximum liability fits the remaining cap and all user/project/department limits. Settlement replaces a reservation with a charge no larger than it; this preserves the inequality. An ambiguous charged timeout retains its reservation until authoritative reconciliation. Cancellation is not proof of no charge, and an idempotency key is not proof of provider deduplication without a contract. If a provider cannot bound token, tool and other charges, strict cap safety cannot be derived from this model; disallow that route under a hard-cap policy. Zero paid budget disables paid dispatch and paid retries, not necessarily already funded local service. The $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 monthly caps are scenarios only.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Compare the four baselines without assuming quality or availability
reasoning_steps.argument: Campus-local only has the fewest off-campus content boundaries but still needs controls for logs, caches, tools and administrators; it can fail model-fit, peak-demand or quality requirements. Approved API only needs explicit permission for each data class and an acceptable remote processing contract; without them, sensitive tasks are infeasible regardless of model capability. A campus gateway plus separately approved external access preserves local service and limits external authority to explicit connectors, but does not itself guarantee that researchers cannot bypass the gateway. Federation adds partner administrators, WAN failure modes, capacity commitments, accounting and policy synchronization; usable capacity is only capacity authorized for that task and fitting its model. If no required task gains an authorized quality/latency capability, or external processing already meets those requirements more cheaply, federation has no demonstrated compensating benefit for its additional trust obligations. These are architectural comparisons, not measured performance rankings.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Specify adversarial tests and observable oracles
reasoning_steps.argument: Use synthetic canary content, not real restricted data. Exercise the two partition histories above, revocation between enqueue and dispatch, revocation during streaming, tenant-supplied false labels, a tool exfiltration attempt, diagnostic logging to an unapproved sink, provider rejection, duplicate retries, ambiguous timeout, cancellation and concurrent quota reservations. Collect trusted boundary captures plus authority sequence records and ledger transactions; a gateway's own success log alone cannot establish absence of bypass. Expected safe behavior is no unapproved egress, no automatic external escalation, and no released reservation without settlement evidence. Test campus-authority loss separately from partner loss. For identical isolated-gateway observations, the immediate-revocation design must decline off-campus dispatch in both partition histories. Offline dispatch in H0 and refusal in H1 requires an additional observable authority channel; otherwise the claimed distinction is invalid. None of these tests has been run here.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Define a bounded 90-day decision rather than presume federation
reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: inspect and archive the two starting sources with actual access dates, obtain campus policy/contract decisions, inventory all egress paths, and agree task rubrics and latency targets. Days 31–60: implement the proposed gate in a synthetic-data sandbox and run the adversarial schedules before any sensitive pilot. Days 61–90: compare the four baselines on the same approved task strata: classroom coding, routine analysis, scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context, agentic workflows, sensitive tasks and reproducible batches. Record exact model/version where available, prompts under approved retention, tool versions, seeds/settings, completion quality, queue/cold-start/service latency, throughput, failed tasks, staff hours and costs. Include memory-fit failures, maintenance, peak demand and interactive versus batch queues; report per-campus/per-project tails and longest waits, not only averages. Proposed safety stop threshold is any observed unauthorized egress or reservation-invariant violation. Performance go thresholds must be numerically preregistered by the campuses before measurement; no universal target is invented here. Federation proceeds only if it adds a material authorized task benefit over baseline 3, meets those targets, and its incremental cost and agreements are acceptable. Passing finite tests is not proof against every schedule.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Preserve cost and useful-task denominators
reasoning_steps.argument: For each baseline report annual fully loaded cost as annualized hardware acquisition/replacement without double counting, plus power/cooling, storage, network, support, procurement, staff, API/tool/embedding/egress charges and commitments. Report sunk and incremental views separately; idle capacity remains in fully loaded cost. Monthly average is annual cost/12, not a substitute for peak monthly cash-flow analysis. Cost per active researcher is cost divided by a declared active-user count; cost per useful task is cost divided by tasks meeting both the quality and latency rubric, with zero successes reported as undefined rather than zero cost. Repeated Investigator/Skeptic calls, agent branches, failed attempts and paid retries belong in the numerator. Actual API input/output/cache rates, billing units and commitments require dated provider records that are unavailable here. No numerical break-even or institutional spending claim follows from this analysis.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Separate the existing gateway description from this proposal
reasoning_steps.argument: The project reports MindRouter protocol translation for OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic clients and Ollama/vLLM backends, WDRR scheduling, per-user quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry. No inspected source establishes that it implements the broker below. Federation, frontier routing, release serialization and a financial reservation ledger are proposed extensions. The missing source records are https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf. Their supplied prior review date is 2026-10-31; this investigator has no access date and cannot verify changed claims.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Locate the authority and narrow the release contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Propose one home-campus broker B as both the policy-commit authority for managed releases and the sole owner of their outbound sockets. Authenticated campus administrators submit updates to B; a separate administrative database or cached policy service cannot independently make a policy effective. An update takes effect when B durably commits it under its exclusive mutex M, and acknowledgment follows that commit. This defines the authoritative order, not an administrator's click time or message arrival time. Define release as successful acceptance of a positive byte count by the OS outbound transport through B. It is not enqueueing an application job, committing an authorization record, calling an asynchronously buffered client, NIC transmission or recipient delivery. The proposed contract forbids any new submission denied by a revocation committed earlier. It gives no bounded revocation-response time and does not recall prior submissions.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. State the minimal enforcement boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: B uses one serialized execution path for policy updates and content submissions. Only it holds destination credentials and owns managed outbound connections; workers and tenants have no alternative managed egress. Its transport adapter exposes synchronous nonblocking submission without an independently flushing application/TLS content queue. Encryption may prepare immutable bytes inside the trusted broker, but all submissions to sockets still pass through B. Each immutable data unit binds its bytes, conservative label, authenticated principal/project, destination identity, connection, retention/contract requirements and reservation identifier. Changing any binding requires revalidation. Logs, embeddings, tool calls, caches, streamed outputs and content-bearing telemetry require equivalent mediation when crossing their approved boundaries. Unknown classification denies release to a domain not explicitly approved for that uncertainty. A malicious tenant cannot lower a trusted label. Compromise of B, the OS enforcement boundary or label assignment is outside the conditional guarantee; unrelated human copying is also outside it.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Define durable state and admission transitions
reasoning_steps.argument: Durable global state contains policy P with version v, a monotone operation identifier, broker recovery epoch, an audit journal and hierarchical budget accounts. An attempt has immutable request bindings, a reservation r and phase READY, HELD, ARMED, OPEN, UNCERTAIN or CLOSED. READY means locally queued and confers no release permission. A preliminary CHECK may estimate eligibility but creates no reusable capability. RESERVE atomically checks every applicable campus/department/project/user limit and durably changes READY→HELD, reserving an enforceable upper bound for the entire billable attempt. It creates no permission to send. With no paid headroom, no paid attempt is admitted; already funded local service may remain eligible. Retries and agent subcalls are separate attempts unless already covered by an explicit enforceable aggregate bound. Provider/SDK automatic application retries are disabled unless separately covered. If no reliable liability bound exists, the paid route is ineligible under a strict hard-cap requirement.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Make FINAL_SUBMIT, not CHECK or ARM, the gate
reasoning_steps.argument: For each bounded data unit, FINAL_SUBMIT acquires M and re-evaluates its immutable bindings against current P, destination authentication, contract/retention requirements, cancellation state and sufficient pinned reservation coverage. Denial makes no transport call. On approval, B durably appends an ARMED intent identifying the unit and policy version, while retaining M. It then immediately performs one nonblocking transport submission under the same M. A positive result n means exactly that prefix was submitted; B records the returned count and marks the attempt OPEN before releasing M. A partial remainder is a new unit requiring another FINAL_SUBMIT. Errors or lost outcome records are handled conservatively; an error never proves that earlier units of the same attempt were not released. No other thread may commit policy or release reservation coverage during this critical section. REVOKE also acquires M, durably updates P and v, then releases M and acknowledges. ARMED is a write-ahead record, not an independently executable send permit. There is deliberately no detached authorized outbox worker.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Derive the submission invariant
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially no units have been submitted. Consider the next positive transport acceptance. Its FINAL_SUBMIT holds M from the current-policy check through that acceptance, so a revocation cannot commit between those events. The bytes and destination cannot change because their bindings are immutable. Therefore the policy at acceptance is the policy that approved the unit. A failed check adds no submitted unit. RESERVE, CHECK and ARMED alone also add none. Induction proves authorization for every finite history of these submission events under the stated trusted-enforcement premises. If FINAL_SUBMIT obtains M before a concurrent REVOKE, that submission can precede the revocation commit; if REVOKE commits first, the submission must use the updated policy. This is a linearized submission contract, not revocation at request-arrival time.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Hand-check check→revoke→release and streaming
reasoning_steps.argument: Trace A: P=v0 permits destination D; CHECK(v0) succeeds; RESERVE produces HELD(r); REVOKE commits v1 denying D; FINAL_SUBMIT obtains M, reads v1, denies, and makes no transport call. The blocking transition is the current-policy guard in FINAL_SUBMIT, not queue invalidation or credential expiry. Trace B: FINAL_SUBMIT(chunk 1,v0) accepts n1 bytes; REVOKE commits v1; FINAL_SUBMIT(chunk 2) reads v1 and denies. No later application chunk may be submitted under the old approval. Bytes from chunk 1 may still be in transit. If chunk 1 was an outbound prompt already accepted by a provider, revocation does not undo provider processing or billing. An inbound provider stream may be stopped, but delivery of each output chunk across another controlled boundary needs its own authorization. Cancellation is best effort downstream and cannot certify deletion or zero charges.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Hand-check crash after authorization and specify recovery
reasoning_steps.argument: Trace C: RESERVE(r) is durable; FINAL_SUBMIT validates v0 and durably writes ARMED; B crashes before its transport call. In this actual trace no bytes were submitted. Recovery, however, may see the same durable ARMED record after a crash that occurred just after transport acceptance but before its result was recorded. It must not infer non-dispatch from that record. Recovery starts with submission disabled, requires confirmed termination/fencing of the former broker and socket ownership, loads the last durable policy and ledger, advances the epoch, and marks unfinished ARMED or OPEN attempts UNCERTAIN with r retained. It closes rather than resumes those connections and never replays their send intents. A committed v1 revocation remains effective after recovery; a merely pending revocation has not yet committed and its caller must retry. Any later permitted attempt needs fresh policy validation and sufficient reservation for additional liability. Availability is sacrificed if old-owner fencing or policy recovery cannot be established. Previously OS-accepted bytes may survive the process crash; they remain prior submissions, not permissions to resume application sends.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Preserve billing coverage without claiming atomic network-and-disk commit
reasoning_steps.argument: For each account a, require settled spend S_a plus unresolved reservations R_a to be at most its funded cap B_a. RESERVE increases R_a only when every applicable account can cover it, in one durable serialized transaction. ARMED, submission, revocation, cancellation, timeout and crash do not reclaim it. Final settlement replaces r by charge c≤r, changing accounted liability by c−r≤0. Certified non-dispatch can release a reservation only when no further transmission is possible and no earlier transmission of that attempt could incur liability. Recovery uncertainty is not such a certificate. Reconciliation and settlement must be authenticated, final under the billing contract and applied once; additional sends are prohibited after final settlement. A new potentially chargeable retry requires additional coverage rather than reusing an unresolved reservation. Reservations are not erased at month rollover: they remain backed in their original funded accounts, with any exposure to another billing period funded there too. Atomicity with physical sending is neither claimed nor required for conservative coverage: durable intent precedes sending, and uncertain outcomes retain liability. This can strand budget indefinitely without final reconciliation.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Give the physical-egress counterexample and reject overclaiming
reasoning_steps.argument: Let OS_ACCEPT(chunk,v0) occur while M is held. B releases M, REVOKE commits v1, and only then a queued packet carrying that chunk leaves the NIC. Ordinary transport buffering permits this schedule. TCP may also retransmit earlier accepted bytes after revocation. Thus a mutex around policy checks and socket submissions does not establish 'no physical byte crosses the campus boundary after commit.' Even a campus firewall policy update is not evidence of atomic ordering with every NIC queue and in-flight packet. Under this architecture I reject that stronger guarantee and retain only no new denied transport submissions after commit. If campus policy instead demands serialization at physical transmission, this proposal is insufficient: a trusted final-egress mechanism must control and order all relevant hardware queues, retransmissions and failover paths, with an explicitly accepted packet/byte granularity. No such implementation or proof is supplied.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. State the partition and baseline consequences
reasoning_steps.argument: The broker is deliberately not a partition-tolerant replica of an independently committing policy authority. Loss of its authority path stops new external submissions rather than validating cached approvals. Minimal recovery has no automatic active-active failover; adding it would require fencing and a new ordering argument. A partitioned partner cannot autonomously originate new home-campus-authorized releases under this contract. It may already possess legitimately released data, for which partner enforcement and agreements remain separate requirements. Baseline 1 needs fewer off-campus content paths but still needs internal boundary controls. Baseline 2 needs approved remote processing and budget coverage for all eligible tasks. Baseline 3 can use one explicitly approved external connector and this home-campus gate. Baseline 4 adds partner boundaries and downstream obligations without improving this submission invariant by itself. Where federation adds no demonstrated authorized task capability, baseline 3 avoids those extra obligations; no measured quality, availability or economic ranking follows.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Specify a discriminating implementation test and its limits
reasoning_steps.argument: Next test: build a synthetic-canary broker sandbox with controllable pauses after preliminary CHECK, after durable ARMED, immediately before transport submission, and after acceptance but before result logging. Run the three traces above and the competing implementation that releases M before sending. Observe successful kernel submissions independently of broker success logs, join them to authoritative policy-commit order, and reconcile durable reservations after recovery. An external packet capture separately tests the stronger physical interpretation but cannot by itself distinguish a new submission from an old transport retransmission. Predicted outcome: the detached check-then-send control admits the stale schedule, while this specification denies Trace A and chunk 2 of Trace B and retains Trace C's reservation. These are predictions, not results. Any denied new submission or uncovered liability is a safety stop; recovery that cannot fence the former owner must remain unavailable. Finite passing tests would support only those schedules, not prove complete mediation, recipient compliance or all-schedule correctness.

assumptions: The campus accepts revocation effective at durable broker commit and release defined as OS transport acceptance, not administrator request time, physical transmission or recipient delivery.

The transport adapter has no independently flushing application-content queue; the broker retains serialization through synchronous nonblocking OS submission.
Policy, intents and hierarchical reservations are durably recorded; recovery cannot roll back acknowledged commits and cannot enable submissions before exclusive ownership is established.
Each paid attempt has an enforceable aggregate liability bound covering its billing scope; all additional chargeable transmissions have coverage, and final reconciliation is trustworthy.

output.claim: Conditional on complete mediation, a trusted campus authority colocated with a serialized egress gate, durable state and effective crash fencing, the proposed state machine prevents any new controlled handoff under revoked policy after revocation commits. It does not prevent later network delivery of an already handed-off, bounded request. Authorization and handoff must share a critical section with revocation; a remote authorization check followed by an independently executed send does not provide this guarantee.
output.method: Resolve the recorded dispatch/revocation objection by defining separate authorization, controlled-handoff, physical-transmission and revocation events. Derive the safety property from a concrete serialization mechanism, examine the two requested histories and a partition counterexample, and specify an independently instrumented fault-test oracle. The hypothesis is that serialized authorization/handoff blocks a post-revocation new release, whereas check-then-send permits one; a forced pause between checking and handoff discriminates them. This is a proposed reference design and analytical argument, not implementation verification. I inspected the supplied bounded extract of artifact 1288a55b-8e0b-4b3c-b8a9-e527cd236c17, not its saved original. The truncated peer extract 12231499-34a0-41fd-b078-c6249b5edefb raises a compatible partition concern; I independently construct the relevant histories below rather than treating its claim as verified. Neither runtime nor external retrieval is available. The MindRouter documentation and PEARC’26 PDF were not accessed; 2026-10-31 remains the brief’s reported review date, not my access date. Protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry remain brief-attributed published descriptions. This state machine, frontier routing and federation are hypothetical extensions, not established MindRouter features.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define the controlled boundary and the policy contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Let A be the durable authorization commit for one attempt; H the transfer of its frozen request envelope into the trusted egress transport; S a later physical network transmission; and R the durable revocation commit at the authoritative campus gate. H, not provider receipt or the last packet leaving a NIC, is the last controlled release boundary in this contract. Before H the gate can suppress the entire request. After H the request is logically in flight, including bytes buffered in the trusted transport. Revocation blocks new handoffs; it cannot recall those bytes. Administrative submission of revocation and acknowledgement of committed revocation are distinct events.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. State the enforcement premises
reasoning_steps.argument: All relevant releases and policy changes traverse one campus enforcement service. It owns the authoritative policy state and transport credentials; workers and tenants cannot send around it. Identity revocation, classification changes, destination withdrawal and contractual restrictions must enter its policy order. Independent upstream changes not yet incorporated into that order are outside the guarantee. The service uses one serialization lock for authorization/handoff and policy mutation, durable records, and immutable request buffers. Recovery fences the previous sender before allowing new commits. These are implementation requirements, not established campus or MindRouter properties.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Specify the request and policy state
reasoning_steps.argument: Policy state is an epoch and an explicit eligibility predicate. Each attempt binds campus, subject, project, classification, exact content, destination identity, model/configuration, approved artifact domains, size/output bounds and budget-hold identifiers. A request starts QUEUED, with no reusable dispatch authority. It can become READY only when its envelope is frozen and a compatible endpoint and bounded transport capacity are available. An unknown label or missing approval gives no eligible destination. Changing content, destination, tool action or model requires a new attempt. The binding covers prompts and approved handling of outputs, logs, caches, embeddings and telemetry; it does not establish that a recipient actually honors those obligations.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Give the minimal dispatch transition
reasoning_steps.argument: From READY, obtain the required durable budget holds, then acquire the policy/egress lock. Re-evaluate eligibility against the authoritative current epoch. On failure, enter BLOCKED without handoff. On success, durably record MAY_SEND with the frozen envelope and epoch; this commit is A, the authorization linearization point. While still holding the lock, perform one nonblocking H into the trusted transport and record IN_FLIGHT if acknowledged. Only then release the lock. Transport admission must accept ownership of one bounded immutable envelope, not an unbounded workflow or future mutable stream. READY jobs are not preauthorized while waiting in scheduling queues. If the handoff outcome is uncertain, enter UNKNOWN, not retryable READY. No delayed worker may later exercise A independently.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Give revocation and the in-flight contract
reasoning_steps.argument: A revocation acquires the same lock, durably increments the epoch and changes the eligibility predicate; that commit is R. Acknowledge success only after R. Thus a revocation arriving while dispatch holds the lock remains pending until that handoff finishes or is abandoned. Existing queued requests must pass the new predicate. Requests already handed off may finish their single frozen envelope and return results only through approved handling paths. Cancellation and remote deletion are best-effort requests unless stronger inspected contracts exist. They are not recall guarantees. Every new agent call, tool call, redirect, content-bearing reconnection or fallback must re-enter admission. Transport retransmission of already accepted bytes is part of the original in-flight transfer; a new independently chargeable application attempt is not.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Prove the new-handoff safety property
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially there are no authorized attempts or handed-off envelopes. For any H, the dispatch transition requires a preceding A under the lock, with eligibility true in epoch e. No R can occur between that validation and H because R requires the same lock. Consequently policy at H still authorizes that exact envelope. After an R withdrawing its eligibility, a later dispatch sees the changed predicate and cannot reach H unless a subsequent explicit policy change authorizes it again. The remaining transitions either make no handoff or concern an envelope already handed off. Induction over these transitions proves the property for all modeled interleavings. It proves neither physical packet suppression after R nor recipient compliance.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Analyze authorization–revocation–send
reasoning_steps.argument: If send means H, a successful A–R–H history is excluded: the dispatch lock prevents R from committing between A and H. A revocation invocation may occur there, but its successful acknowledgement must wait. If dispatch crashes after A without H, recovery must abandon that attempt and fence the old sender before R can commit; A cannot later be replayed. If send means physical S, A–H–R–S is allowed: transport buffering or network delay can place physical transmission or receipt after revocation. A–R–S alone therefore lacks enough information to classify a violation. The oracle must locate H. Permitting A–R–H through an outstanding token would implement a weaker grandfathered-authorization contract, which this design does not adopt.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Analyze revocation–authorization–send
reasoning_steps.argument: For R–A–H concerning the revoked subject/destination, A must fail while that prohibition remains effective. An earlier preliminary eligibility check is not A and cannot override R. A concurrent authorization and revocation are ordered by the lock: either dispatch completes its controlled handoff first, or revocation commits first and blocks it. An authorization begun after receipt of a successful revocation acknowledgement must observe R. An explicit later reapproval can authorize a new attempt, but neither timeout nor overload constitutes reapproval. Revocations unrelated to the request do not require rejecting it; the predicate, not epoch inequality alone, determines eligibility.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Partition behavior and the competing cached-check design
reasoning_steps.argument: In the proposed minimum, authority and controlled handoff are colocated. A partition disconnecting a worker from this service prevents new handoffs by that worker; a partition disconnecting an administrator can leave a revocation uncommitted and must not produce a success acknowledgement. If authority and an autonomous sender are separated instead, consider two histories after their link partitions: in one, the authority makes no change; in the other, it commits a revocation. The sender sees the same messages in both. Sending under a cached approval preserves service in the first history but violates latest-authority handoff policy in the second. Refusing preserves safety but loses availability. A lease changes the contract by permitting a stale interval; it does not establish immediate revocation. Physical sends of envelopes handed off before the partition remain in flight.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Crash, cancellation and budget integration
reasoning_steps.argument: The MAY_SEND record is written before H because a crash can otherwise erase evidence of liability. If recovery cannot determine whether H occurred, mark UNKNOWN, prohibit replay and retain the reservation. Fencing must stop the old process from later making a new H; absent confirmed fencing, neither recovery nor successful revocation acknowledgement may proceed. An already accepted transport envelope remains in flight. This sacrifices availability rather than assuming exactly-once delivery. Preserve the prior accounting invariant independently: admission tests finalized spending plus outstanding holds against each cap; final settlement replaces a hold r by charge c ≤ r; certified non-dispatch can release a hold; unknown outcomes cannot. Revocation or cancellation alone supplies no certificate of non-dispatch or zero charge.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Define an independently observable oracle
reasoning_steps.argument: Use synthetic labeled envelopes and a security-owned test controller with separate instrumentation at the trusted transport ownership boundary and a mock destination recording received bytes and effects. The controller supplies policy changes and maintains a reference eligibility predicate; it does not infer success from router logs alone. Record attempt/content/destination bindings, A and R commit receipts, H events, fencing events and mock receipts. Establish order with barriers and acknowledgements rather than cross-host timestamps. Force pauses after preliminary checking, after A but before H, after H, and during recovery. A FAIL is an H forbidden by the reference policy in the committed order, a mutation or destination substitution, an unadmitted application retry, an unfenced old sender making H, or an acknowledgement of R followed by a new forbidden H. Receipt after R with H before R is not a safety failure. Missing capture, uncertain ordering or broken controls makes a trial inconclusive, not a pass. Include an authorized positive control to demonstrate that both sensors detect traffic.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Specify the decisive tests and deployment implication
reasoning_steps.argument: The unsafe control performs a check, releases its lock, pauses, accepts and acknowledges revocation, then hands off; the constructed history predicts a forbidden H. The proposed design, paused after A, must either complete H before R commits or abandon/fence the attempt before acknowledging R. A hung lock with no revocation acknowledgement is a liveness failure, not proof of safety or a successful revocation. Test partitions, stale workers, malicious redirects, payload mutation, simultaneous quota claims, cancellation and crash-after-handoff. In the 90-day pilot, days 1–30 assign security the boundary/contract approval and computing the instrumentation; days 31–60 run these controlled fault histories; days 61–90 measure revocation-ack latency, refusal rate, recovery time and useful completion under the agreed load. Any forbidden H stops the pilot; incomplete instrumentation blocks a go decision. Campus-local, API-only and gateway-plus-separately-approved-API services can share this campus gate. Federation adds remote enforcement and recipient obligations without eliminating the ordering constraint. Baseline 3 remains the simpler design candidate unless measured authorized pooling benefits justify those additions; no comparative winner is established.

assumptions: Every content-bearing release in the claimed scope is completely mediated; tenants, workers, tools and alternate credentials cannot bypass the campus egress gate.

The campus authoritative policy state and controlled-handoff gate are colocated and trusted. All policy changes covered by the guarantee commit through that service; an uncommitted remote instruction is not represented as an effective, acknowledged revocation.

One serialization mechanism excludes policy mutation from the interval spanning final validation, durable authorization and controlled handoff, with correct durable recovery and authenticated commit acknowledgements.

Each handoff transfers only one bounded immutable request envelope to a trusted transport; destination/content binding cannot change, and new application attempts or continuations require fresh admission.
After a crash, effective fencing prevents the old sender from making a new handoff before recovery or revocation can be acknowledged; uncertain handoffs are never replayed.

The campus explicitly accepts revocation at the controlled-handoff boundary: previously handed-off envelopes may subsequently transmit or arrive. Immediate recall, deletion and physical-packet cutoff are not part of the claim.

The current cycle answers the bounded dispatch/revocation question with a convincing, conditional reference-model argument. Authorization A and controlled handoff H share a critical section with revocation R. Therefore a successful A–R–H ordering is excluded. If R commits first and its prohibition remains effective, subsequent authorization fails. Conversely, A–H–R–S is permitted when S denotes later physical transmission. This explicitly resolves the earlier ambiguity without claiming recall of transmitted or transport-buffered data.

The partition analysis is also sound within its stated scope. Colocation removes the autonomous remote sender from the authorization decision, but does not make remotely submitted revocations instantaneous: an administrator disconnected from the authority cannot obtain a successful commit acknowledgement. For a separated sender, the unchanged-policy and revoked-policy histories are observationally identical during a partition; cached approval cannot provide both continued dispatch and compliance with the latest authority state. This is a negative result about that candidate design, not a refutation of federation generally.

The proposed oracle correctly observes H separately from destination receipt, uses causal barriers rather than cross-host clock ordering, and treats missing capture as inconclusive. No instrumentation, fencing, complete-mediation property or campus acceptance has been demonstrated. The model deliberately permits revocation acknowledgements to wait behind a dispatch; bounded revocation and recovery latency remain separate service requirements.

The cycle-1 accounting result remains supported under its separate five accounting premises: admission checks the cap, settlement changes the encumbrance by c−r ≤ 0, and unknown outcomes retain their holds. Its charged-timeout counterexample also remains valid. Neither result supplies implementation evidence.

The overall project remains partial. The exact MindRouter documentation and PEARC’26 PDF were not inspected; 2026-10-31 is the brief’s reported review date, not this reviewer’s access date. Current contractual prices, campus policies, operational measurements and comparative economics remain unavailable. Federation, frontier routing and this state machine remain proposed extensions. The next useful analytical step is to make the pilot’s statistical decision rule explicit rather than repeat the completed conditional safety proof.
objections: Material and recoverable implementation limitation: complete mediation, immutable binding, atomic transport ownership, durable recovery and effective fencing are premises, not demonstrated properties. The conditional safety proof cannot establish deployment safety.

Material and recoverable contract limitation: campus acceptance of H-boundary revocation, including buffered requests and delayed upstream identity changes, remains absent. The model does not establish instantaneous revocation at physical transmission or remote deletion.

Material evidence limitation: the required publications, dated contracts and prices, campus policies and workload measurements remain unavailable. Comparative usefulness, costs and deployment readiness cannot be inferred.

Retained local counterexamples: cycle 1 shows that premature timeout-release can permit 2b liability against a b cap; cycle 2 shows that separated check–R–H can violate current-policy handoff authorization. These refute those unsafe candidates, not the project's feasibility.

output.solution_claim: Under the Investigator’s six listed premises, the serialized campus gate prevents a new controlled handoff forbidden by a committed revocation while that prohibition remains effective. It permits later transmission or delivery of envelopes handed off before revocation and establishes neither recipient compliance nor implementation correctness. The broader four-baseline usefulness, reliability and cost comparison is not yet established.
output.argument_summary: Cycle 2 supplies an explicit A/H/S/R contract, serialized dispatch and revocation transitions, crash-fencing requirements, both requested event orderings, a partition indistinguishability argument and an independently instrumented test specification. These support the conditional handoff-safety claim. Cycle 1 artifact 1288a55b-8e0b-4b3c-b8a9-e527cd236c17 supplies the separate conditional budget induction and timeout counterexample. Pilot and deployment implications remain proposals rather than measured findings.

reasoning_assessments.rationale: Accepted as the expressly conditional boundary contract. Distinguishing transport ownership H from physical transmission S makes later delivery after R consistent with the claim; it does not establish campus acceptance of that contract.

Accepted as enforcement premises, not observations. Complete mediation, a common policy order, immutable buffers and fencing are sufficient premises for the later serialized model; excluding unincorporated upstream changes appropriately narrows its scope.

The frozen envelope and explicit eligibility predicate prevent authorization from being transferred to changed content or destinations within the model. Fail-closed classification and separate recipient-compliance limitations are consistent with the project requirements.

Holding the common lock from final validation through A and H prevents intervening policy mutation. UNKNOWN and the prohibition on delayed independent exercise of A avoid treating uncertain handoff as reusable authority. This depends on the stated transport-ownership and recovery premises.

R uses the same serialization mechanism, so pending revocation cannot be mistaken for committed revocation. The single-envelope in-flight exception and fresh admission for new application actions preserve the specified boundary without promising recall.

For each modeled H, eligibility is checked while policy mutation is excluded through handoff. A subsequent R blocks later forbidden H events until explicit reapproval. Non-handoff transitions cannot violate this property, giving the claimed conditional induction.

The common lock excludes A–R–H, whereas buffering permits A–H–R–S. Abandonment and fencing exclude replay of authorization after a crash. Thus observing A–R–S without locating H cannot classify a violation under this contract.

When R precedes final validation and the prohibition remains active, the current predicate rejects the attempt. Concurrent operations are serialized, and unrelated epoch changes need not reject an otherwise eligible envelope.

The separated sender receives identical observations in the unchanged and revoked histories, so cached dispatch cannot satisfy immediate latest-authority safety in both. Colocation changes the failure contract: disconnected clients lose admission or revocation-commit availability rather than receiving false success.

Retaining uncertain holds and prohibiting replay conservatively preserve liability coverage. Fencing prevents an abandoned sender from creating a later H. The accounting inference reuses cycle 1 under its separate five premises; the current policy premises alone do not establish an invoice cap.

Independent H instrumentation and destination observations distinguish pre-revocation handoff from forbidden post-revocation release. Causal barriers, immutable bindings, positive controls and inconclusive classifications make this a meaningful proposed oracle, not evidence that an implementation has passed.

The paused unsafe control permits check–R–H, while the serialized design must order H before R or abandon the attempt. Separating hung-lock liveness failure from safety is correct. The pilot stages and baseline-3 preference are explicitly proposals, with no measured winner asserted.

The campus authoritative policy state and controlled-handoff gate are colocated and trusted. All policy changes covered by the guarantee commit through that service; an uncommitted remote instruction is not represented as an effective, acknowledged revocation.

After a crash, effective fencing prevents the old sender from making a new handoff before recovery or revocation can be acknowledged; uncertain handoffs are never replayed.

The campus explicitly accepts revocation at the controlled-handoff boundary: previously handed-off envelopes may subsequently transmit or arrive. Immediate recall, deletion and physical-packet cutoff are not part of the claim.
