output.claim: Under the sampling and bounded-cost assumptions below, a fixed-sample paired pilot can control the probability of a false statistical go decision at 5% across the proposed completion and federation-benefit gates. Refusals remain in the useful-completion denominator. A conservative design requires approximately 2,820 independent task pairs for ±3-percentage-point completion precision, or 4,061 pairs for ±5-point precision on federation’s completion advantage. These are design calculations, not pilot results; 90 days alone does not ensure adequate evidence.
output.method: Address the statistical portion of o385/o417/o451 without treating the earlier architecture as implemented. Test federation against baseline 3—campus gateway plus separately approved external access—on the same preselected task episodes, while reporting baselines 1 and 2 descriptively. The competing explanations are genuine authorized pooling benefit versus apparent benefit caused by dropping refusals, changing task mix, excluding failures from cost, or testing only quiet periods. A common denominator, paired outcomes, independent quality adjudication, representative load blocks and simultaneous confidence bounds distinguish these explanations under the stated assumptions. The 90%, 10-percentage-point and 20% hurdles, the proposed noninferiority margin, task deadlines and governance gates are provisional campus decisions. I reviewed the supplied incomplete extract of artifact 8712830f-b69e-476e-b94d-18be7ea7c043; artifact 1288a55b-8e0b-4b3c-b8a9-e527cd236c17 is only a pointer here. The truncated peer artifact 12231499-34a0-41fd-b078-c6249b5edefb changes no statistical derivation and is not adopted as verified evidence. Neither runtime nor external retrieval is available. Neither required MindRouter source was accessed; 2026-10-31 is the brief’s reported reference-review date, not my access date.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Fix the estimand before admissions or routing
reasoning_steps.argument: Define the target population as legitimate research task episodes offered by authenticated pilot users under a prespecified campus/task/load distribution. An episode is one requested useful deliverable, not one model call: an agent workflow and a reproducible batch each retain one episode identifier through all calls, retries and terminal outcomes. Sample episodes before either service admits them. Let B denote baseline 3 and F the hypothetical federation extension, with the same external-access approvals and budget scenario. Baselines 1 and 2 use the same episode definitions, but selecting a winner among all four would require an additional multiplicity plan. The confirmatory comparison here is only F versus B.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Count refusals without rewarding unsafe behavior
reasoning_steps.argument: For service s and sampled episode i, set Y_si=1 only if the requested deliverable meets the frozen task-quality rubric, finishes within its task-specific end-to-end deadline, supplies required provenance/version information, and follows approved handling rules. Otherwise set Y_si=0. The denominator N includes policy refusals, ambiguous-classification refusals, no-fit jobs, budget exhaustion, overload, outage, provider rejection, deadline expiry, cancellation after enrollment and missing quality adjudication. An appropriate refusal is a safety success but not a useful completion. A late result remains a completion failure. Retries never create new denominator entries. Exclude malformed/nonresearch traffic only through prespecified, outcome-blind eligibility rules; malicious synthetic probes belong in a separate safety suite. Report refusal reasons and both offered-demand and admitted-only rates, but do not substitute the admitted-only rate for the primary outcome.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Separate demand coverage from positive-control safety tests
reasoning_steps.argument: Use p_s=E[Y_si] as useful-completion coverage of offered legitimate demand. Restricted or ambiguous legitimate requests remain represented even when refusal is mandatory; this reveals that a service may be safe yet unable to cover the campus’s needs. Report externally eligible and local-only strata as secondary diagnostics rather than redefining the primary denominator after observing results. Synthetic forbidden-egress tests have no legitimate deliverable and are not mixed into p_s. A counterexample to admitted-only reporting is a service that completes 10 easy tasks and refuses 90 difficult ones: admitted completion is 100%, but offered-demand useful completion is 10%. Neither denominator licenses relaxing policy.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Specify the sampling assumptions and pairing controls
reasoning_steps.argument: For the finite-sample bounds below, the N paired vectors must be independent and identically distributed draws from the prespecified target mixture. Each vector contains B and F outcomes for the same task and comparable load condition; dependence within a pair is allowed. Use authorized task copies, blinded assessors and randomized execution order, with isolated/reset budget and queue state where replay is valid. Do not duplicate sensitive work to an unapproved destination merely to form a pair. Shared queues, monthly budget depletion and repeated tasks from the same researcher generally violate episode-level independence. In those cases use independent reset load blocks as sampling units, with a fixed number of enrolled tasks per block, or design a cluster/randomized-period analysis before collection. Bounds on block averages remain valid, but N then means independent blocks, not calls or tasks. Unavailable independent replication makes inference inconclusive rather than permitting an invented effective sample size.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Define costs at a common service scale
reasoning_steps.argument: Let c_si be nonnegative cost per offered episode at a declared common annual demand and accounting perspective. Include costs of failed episodes, all billable subcalls and permitted retries, idle capacity, staffing and federation administration. Allocate fixed annual costs over the declared annual offered demand, not over observed successes; keep sunk, incremental and fully loaded analyses separate. Define mu_s=E[c_si], and cost per useful task q_s=mu_s/p_s for p_s>0. The primary economic comparison uses fully loaded cost; repeat incremental analysis as a sensitivity, not a replacement. Cost certification below additionally requires enforceable bounds 0≤c_si≤M_s, settled charges or conservative liability bounds, and a known positive baseline cost floor. Unknown fixed allocations require declared uncertainty ranges; an economic go must survive their approved adverse values. An unsettled charged timeout is not zero cost. No prices, costs or workload observations are supplied here.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Construct the paired coverage and economic contrasts
reasoning_steps.argument: Let D_i=Y_Fi−Y_Bi, so D_i lies in [−1,1] and Delta=E[D_i]=p_F−p_B. The coverage hurdle is Delta≥0.10. For the economic hurdle q_F/q_B≤0.80, positive denominators give the equivalent inequality K=mu_F p_B−0.80 mu_B p_F≤0. A mean of per-episode cost/success ratios is undefined on failures and is not this estimand. To estimate K without assuming cost and success are independent within a task, partition the N independent pairs into m=floor(N/2) disjoint two-task blocks (i,j), fixed before outcomes. Define Z=(c_Fi Y_Bj+c_Fj Y_Bi−0.80 c_Bi Y_Fj−0.80 c_Bj Y_Fi)/2. Cross-task independence gives E[Z]=K, while arbitrary within-task dependence is retained. Each Z lies in [−0.80 M_B,M_F], and disjoint blocks are independent. Using only these disjoint products sacrifices precision but makes a finite-sample paired rule transparent.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Give one simultaneous confidence rule
reasoning_steps.argument: Use one fixed final analysis with family error alpha=0.05. Form two-sided intervals for four quantities: p_F, p_B, Delta and K. Hoeffding’s bounded-variable inequality gives P(|mean−expectation|>w sqrt(log(160)/(2n)))≤0.0125 for range width w, since 2 exp(−2n r²/w²)=0.0125. A union bound therefore gives simultaneous coverage at least 95%, without independence among the four intervals. Write a=sqrt(log(160)/(2N)). The intervals are p_s: mean(Y_s)±a; Delta: mean(D)±2a; K: mean(Z)±(M_F+0.80M_B)sqrt(log(160)/(2m)). Clip probability intervals to [0,1] and the Delta interval to [−1,1]. Denote endpoints L and U. This is deliberately conservative, distribution-free under the listed assumptions, and valid for the prespecified OR between the two benefit pathways.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. State the provisional statistical go rule
reasoning_steps.argument: After all nonstatistical gates pass, require L_pF≥0.90 and either (A) L_Delta≥0.10, or (B) U_K≤0 together with L_Delta≥−0.02. The −2-point completion noninferiority margin is an additional provisional safeguard: lower cost must not hide a materially less useful service. Path B also requires L_pB>0 and a known positive mu_B, so the baseline cost-per-useful-task ratio is meaningful. On the simultaneous-coverage event, each certified inequality holds for its population parameter. Thus a statistical go with any false required parameter inequality can occur only outside that event, with probability at most 5%. This controls statistical false-go risk, not policy, contract, implementation or safety risk. At an exact hurdle, high probability of certification should not be expected; power requires a real margin beyond it.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Derive completion and paired-coverage sample requirements
reasoning_steps.argument: For completion half-width h, N≥ceil(log(160)/(2h²)): h=0.05 requires 1,016 independent pairs and h=0.03 requires 2,820. For paired Delta half-width h, its range width is 2, so N≥ceil(2 log(160)/h²): h=0.05 requires 4,061 pairs. At N=3,000 the completion half-width is approximately 0.0291 and the Delta half-width approximately 0.0582; certification therefore requires observed F completion at least about 92.91% and observed advantage at least about 15.82 points. These are analytical requirements, not measured rates. The ceiling matters: if B truly exceeds 90% completion, F cannot improve it by 10 points; if B is exactly 90%, that pathway requires perfect population completion. Cost improvement may therefore be the relevant pathway for an already effective baseline.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Distinguish precision from power and expose cost sensitivity
reasoning_steps.argument: For a bounded mean with range width w, a true favorable margin g beyond its hurdle is certified with probability at least 1−beta if N≥w²[ sqrt(log(160)/2)+sqrt(log(1/beta)/2) ]²/g². This follows by adding the confidence radius to the one-sided Hoeffding sampling deviation. If both cost bounds equal M, half-width 0.10M needs 823 independent two-task blocks, or 1,646 task pairs; half-width 0.02M needs 20,555 blocks, or 41,110 pairs. This is normalized sensitivity, not a dollar scenario. A rare expensive tail can make cost certification impractical in 90 days. reasoning_steps.title: 1. Scope and the proposed contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Define COMMIT(u,v) as the durable broker transaction that makes policy version v effective for update identifier u. Define release as the positive-length prefix accepted by the OS transport during a synchronous, nonblocking submission operation. An administrator issuing a request, a broker receiving it, a durable intent record, physical packet transmission and recipient delivery are different events. The proposed contract forbids a new OS acceptance disallowed by the policy committed before that acceptance in the broker's serialization order. It does not recall previously accepted bytes or promise timely processing of an administrator request. These definitions narrow the guarantee; campus acceptance is still required.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Explicit enabling rule and failure transitions
reasoning_steps.argument: Use broker state (mode, owner_epoch, committed_policy, durable_ledger), with mode initially DISABLED during recovery. FINAL_SUBMIT(a) may enter the transport only if, under the serialization gate: mode=ENABLED; current exclusive ownership is enforceably valid; recovery is complete; the immutable content/destination/identity binding is permitted by committed_policy; classification is unambiguous; and the attempt has sufficient durable reservation coverage. The broker retains the gate through the OS call and result classification. COMMIT uses the same gate. An observed invalid/uncertain ownership result, unrecoverable state ambiguity, or broker shutdown causes DISABLE before any further transport entry. Failure to reach an administrator is not one of these transitions. This is an explicit specification of the intended narrowed rule, not evidence that cycle 2 or MindRouter implements it.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. History A: administrator path fails, broker remains authoritative
reasoning_steps.argument: Initial state A0: broker B is ENABLED in epoch 7; durable v0 permits envelope a to destination D; a has reservation r; B can reach the client and D. A1: administrator X creates update u revoking D, but the request is dropped before B receives it. X observes no commit receipt and eventually a timeout. B observes neither u nor ownership failure; its policy remains v0. A2: B acquires the gate for a, checks the guards against v0, records the required durable intent and invokes the OS adapter while holding the gate. The OS accepts n>0 bytes; this is a permitted release under v0. A3: B releases the gate. Thus administrator unreachability alone does not produce DISABLE. The same release is allowed if u has arrived but remains pending without COMMIT, unless a separate pending-update barrier is specified. Such a barrier is not supplied here.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. History A continued: a later committed revocation
reasoning_steps.argument: A4: X reconnects and submits u. B acquires the gate, durably commits v1 denying D, and only then issues a commit receipt. A5: an unsent suffix of a, another queued envelope, or a new streaming chunk targeting D obtains the gate after that commit and fails policy validation; no OS submission is made for it. Bytes accepted at A2 may still transmit or arrive after A4. If X loses the receipt after A4, the update is nevertheless committed; X's timeout cannot distinguish this case from A1. Receipt loss is an observation ambiguity, not rollback of policy.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. History B: observed ownership uncertainty disables submission
reasoning_steps.argument: Initial state B0 equals A0. B1: before a enters the transport, the trusted ownership check returns UNKNOWN, or the broker receives an ownership-invalid event. B2: at the gate, the broker changes ENABLED to DISABLED and rejects FINAL_SUBMIT(a) before any OS call. Observations are the ownership result, the disable transition and the rejected transport entry, not an administrator timeout. B3: a replacement broker must fence the previous epoch at every managed submission path, recover committed policy and unresolved reservations without rollback, and establish exclusive epoch 8 ownership before enabling. If recovered policy is v1, a is denied; if it is v0 and all other guards pass, a may be admitted as a new authorized submission. Recovery does not automatically replay an uncertain old attempt.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Actual ownership loss is not the same as observing loss
reasoning_steps.argument: If ownership is withdrawn elsewhere while the old broker still reads a cached owner=true and retains a working socket, a local DISABLE transition need not occur. The exact bad schedule is: old broker checks epoch 7; another authority activates epoch 8 without fencing epoch 7; old broker submits using v0. This violates the exclusive-owner premise. Therefore a notification or local Boolean alone is insufficient. A safety claim covering actual ownership loss requires a fence/admission mechanism that orders ownership withdrawal against transport entry: an already admitted operation is ordered before withdrawal, or withdrawal wins and the operation is rejected. No new owner or revocation acknowledgement may rely on the old owner being stopped before that fact is enforced. With this premise absent, the specification guarantees rejection only after observed uncertainty/disable, not after an invisible loss. A dead broker performs no new calls, although its previously accepted OS buffers may still drain.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Authorization derivation and its edge cases
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially there are no releases, so the invariant holds. Consider the next positive OS acceptance. Complete mediation places it inside FINAL_SUBMIT. Its gate excludes COMMIT throughout final validation and the OS call, and effective ownership enforcement excludes an invalid owner. Therefore the latest policy in this serialization order is exactly the policy used by the final guard, which permits the immutable binding. COMMIT changes policy but accepts no content. Rejected operations and certified zero-acceptance calls add no release. Induction gives the invariant for every finite history satisfying these transition premises. For partial sends only the accepted prefix is released; every later application submission revalidates the remainder. Streaming, tool calls, logs, caches and embeddings require the same treatment wherever they cross a managed boundary. An independently flushing TLS/application queue would invalidate the stated OS-boundary premise. The schedule check(v0), COMMIT(v1), OS-accept(v0) remains a counterexample to separated check-then-send, not to this serialized machine.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Proposed oracle for committed versus uncommitted updates
reasoning_steps.argument: Give every update a stable identifier u. A commit receipt must authenticate u, the policy digest/version, ownership epoch and durable commit position; issue it only after the policy transaction is durable. A linearizable status query through the current, fenced authority can establish COMMITTED(u,c), even if the original receipt was lost. If it reports no commit through a query barrier, that establishes only 'not committed as of this barrier', not 'never delivered' or 'will never commit'. If the authority cannot be queried, classify the update UNKNOWN, not revoked and not proven undelivered. In a controlled history-A test, an independent ingress fault injector can deliberately withhold u before broker delivery and record that action; a subsequent authoritative barrier establishes the corresponding uncommitted prefix. A timeout, client send success, packet capture or wall-clock timestamp alone establishes none of these commit facts.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Proposed independent oracle for the OS-submission boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: For a bounded test, correlate update IDs and immutable envelope IDs with gate-operation ordinals, ownership decisions, durable commit positions, and independently collected host-kernel socket-acceptance events/return lengths. Gate ordinals identify mutually exclusive completed boundary operations; they are not timestamps. For each positive OS acceptance, verify that its operation is authorized by the last preceding committed policy and valid ownership epoch. The independent kernel observation must identify the actual OS socket operation rather than an SDK enqueue or TLS-buffer write. A packet received after COMMIT may belong to an earlier accepted prefix and is not by itself a violation. A write-ahead intent proves neither OS acceptance nor nonacceptance. Missing observations, trace loss, or a crash between acceptance and durable result logging yield UNKNOWN; they must not be counted as a passing test or used to justify replay. This is an oracle design, not a reported measurement.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Reservation invariant remains separate and intact
reasoning_steps.argument: For every applicable campus/user/project/department account k, let B_k be its cap, F_k its covered fixed commitments, S_k its finally settled charges, and r_ak the reserved upper liability for each open attempt a. Maintain L_k=F_k+S_k+sum_a r_ak <= B_k, beginning from a reconciled initial state. A durable atomic reservation across all applicable accounts succeeds only if each resulting inequality holds; concurrent admissions therefore cannot both spend the same headroom. Every potentially billable attempt must have an enforceable aggregate liability bound within its reservation. Final settlement q_ak<=r_ak replaces r_ak by q_ak in S_k, changing L_k by q_ak-r_ak<=0. Certified nondispatch can release unused coverage. Ambiguous charged timeouts, cancellation and uncertain crash outcomes retain coverage until trustworthy settlement or a valid tighter remaining-liability bound. No outstanding liability disappears at a billing-window boundary. These transitions preserve every cap by induction.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Reservation failure cases and coupling to the histories
reasoning_steps.argument: A revocation or DISABLE does not refund liability from an earlier accepted request. A retry that may incur an additional charge needs additional coverage unless verified billing semantics place it inside the existing aggregate bound; transport identifiers alone do not prove charge deduplication. Counterexample: one open attempt reserves the entire cap B and times out ambiguously; releasing B and retrying permits total charges of 2B. Keeping the reservation instead blocks the retry and may sacrifice availability. At B=0 no attempt with positive possible liability is admissible. Provider rejection or cancellation is not automatically certified zero cost. Thus history B may stop future submissions while reservations remain occupied, and history A's functioning transport still cannot bypass a failed budget guard.

reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied extract of 1288a55b-8e0b-4b3c-b8a9-e527cd236c17 motivates checking ambiguous-timeout accounting; the reservation proof above is explicitly rederived rather than accepted from that incomplete source. The extract of 8712830f-b69e-476e-b94d-18be7ea7c043 uses controlled handoff H, which may precede OS acceptance; its conditional handoff result cannot be transferred unchanged to this stricter OS boundary. Adopt its question about effective fencing, but leave implementation unverified. The statistical pilot extract 84d10e8b-baaa-498b-9979-b3fa8425883b does not discharge authority, ownership or transport obligations and is not used as safety evidence. This correction applies to managed paths in any of the four baselines; federation adds partner trust boundaries but is not disproven by this local counterexample. It helps specify a safer comparison with baseline 3, without establishing relative usefulness, costs or administrative burden. Novelty and empirical generality are not assessed.

reasoning_assessments.rationale: Accepted as definitions for an explicitly conditional claim, not as campus policy. Durable commit, positive OS acceptance and later delivery are distinct events, and the stated guarantee consistently excludes request-time revocation and recall.

Accepted as the proposed transition rule under the listed premises. Its guards expressly require enforceable ownership, completed recovery, authorization and reservation coverage; administrator unreachability is not a disabling event. Holding the same gate through the OS call supplies the order used by the later proof.

Dropping u before broker delivery changes neither committed policy nor any enabling guard. Therefore the allowed positive acceptance under v0 is a direct trace of the specified machine. A pending request likewise has no effect without an additional barrier.

After the serialized durable commit of v1, each later submission must validate against v1 and is denied for D. Earlier OS-accepted bytes are outside that new-submission prohibition. Losing the receipt does not undo the durable transaction, so a client timeout cannot determine commitment.

The specified UNKNOWN observation occurs before transport admission and leads to DISABLED, which falsifies an explicit submission guard. Replacement admission is correctly conditioned on effective fencing and complete recovery, with no automatic replay of uncertain attempts.

The old-owner trace demonstrates why local belief is insufficient: activating a new owner without fencing leaves the old socket usable. The step correctly identifies this as violation of the ownership premise and narrows any unconditional guarantee to observed disablement. Its stronger result remains conditional on ordering withdrawal against in-flight admission.

For each mediated positive acceptance, the final guard and OS call occupy one policy-excluding interval, so no intervening COMMIT can make the validated policy stale in that order. Partial prefixes and later submissions are treated separately. The induction is valid for finite histories under the explicit mediation, immutable-binding and transport premises.

An authenticated durable receipt or linearizable query can establish commitment despite receipt loss. A negative query establishes only an uncommitted prefix, not nondelivery or permanent noncommitment. The proposed fault injector supplies an additional oracle for controlled nondelivery rather than inferring it from timeout.

The proposed check uses operation ordering plus actual kernel socket acceptance rather than packet arrival or SDK enqueue. It expressly requires correct correlation and treats trace loss and crash ambiguity as UNKNOWN. This is a coherent bounded-test design, not a reported observation or proof of every implementation schedule.

Atomic reservation preserves each account inequality at admission. Replacing r_ak by a trustworthy final q_ak no larger than r_ak changes covered liability by q_ak-r_ak, which is nonpositive. Retaining unresolved liabilities and accounting for fixed commitments closes the stated timeout and billing-window escape paths, conditional on enforceable aggregate bounds and complete spending mediation.

For B greater than zero, an unresolved first attempt can charge B and a separately billable retry can charge another B; releasing coverage merely because of timeout therefore permits 2B liability. Retaining coverage blocks that retry. The zero-cap and cancellation conclusions follow from possible liability rather than optimistic dispatch outcomes.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Establish the source and implementation boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: The project describes MindRouter as an on-campus gateway providing OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic client protocol translation, Ollama/vLLM backends, WDRR scheduling, per-user quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry. These are source claims as reported in the project, not independently inspected documentation or measured guarantees. The starting records are https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf. This session has no access date for either. Federation, frontier routing, distributed budget enforcement and the controls below are proposed extensions, not attributed MindRouter features.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Define the safety contract precisely
reasoning_steps.argument: For a campus c, let P_c be its authoritative policy and let an egress event mean release of a data-bearing unit through a managed boundary, including request bodies, streamed output, tool arguments, logs, embeddings, cache writes and telemetry containing content. Define authorization at that event, not at initial job submission. Immediate revocation means that a revocation ordered before an egress event by the campus authority must govern that event. Previously released data cannot be recalled by this definition. This is a proposed strong contract, not a claim about an existing university policy.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Construct indistinguishable partition histories
reasoning_steps.argument: At t0 a gateway G has a valid cached permission allowing project J to send class D to partner B. At t1 G loses communication with the home authority A but can still reach B and the requester. In history H0, A leaves the permission unchanged. In history H1, A revokes it before the next request arrives. Deliver exactly the same requests, clock readings and network observations to G in both histories; A's revocation message cannot cross the partition. Thus G has the same local state when deciding whether to dispatch. A deterministic G makes the same decision; a randomized G has the same decision distribution. Dispatching in H0 for guaranteed availability therefore also permits dispatch in H1, violating the immediate-revocation contract. Denying or waiting preserves this safety condition but sacrifices partition-time dispatch availability. The example requires only one request and one revocation.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Identify what does and does not repair the counterexample
reasoning_steps.argument: A signature establishes who issued an approval, not whether it has since been revoked. A policy-version field cannot reveal an unseen newer version. WDRR and quotas decide service allocation, not destination authorization. A lease repairs the conflict only by changing the contract: permission remains valid until its defined expiry despite a later revocation, or offline dispatch is prohibited. With trusted clocks and explicitly accepted lease semantics, exposure can be bounded by the remaining lease duration, but it is not immediate revocation. Conversely, a reachable home authority can still authorize some remote routes during a partner outage; the result does not prohibit federation generally.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Propose an enforceable, narrower invariant
reasoning_steps.argument: Let L(x) be a conservative set of restrictions attached to object x. For a derivation y from inputs x_i, require L(y) to include the union of their restrictions unless an authorized declassification explicitly changes it; an additional classifier may add restrictions. Unknown classification maps to deny for off-domain egress. Define I: every controlled egress of x to destination d has an authenticated campus principal, current campus authorization for L(x), the required destination/retention agreement, and any necessary budget reservation. Tool results, outputs, caches and diagnostic records are objects under the same rule. This is a proposed information-flow discipline; it does not imply a classifier can reliably identify sensitive data from text alone.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Derive conditional preservation and its limits
reasoning_steps.argument: Assume trusted label assignment, complete mediation, authenticated destinations and an authority/enforcement mechanism that serializes policy changes with controlled release events. Initially no egress has occurred, so I holds. For the next proposed release, the gate either rejects it, leaving the egress history unchanged, or checks all predicates against the policy ordered at that release and records the authorization before releasing it. Thus the added event satisfies I; induction covers every finite egress prefix. Checking policy and then sending later without this serialization leaves a check-to-use race and does not satisfy the premise. This proof covers the specified release event, not later network delivery, remote use, deletion, arbitrary user-controlled network paths or a compromised gate. Deployment must explain how its concrete streaming and revocation semantics implement that event model.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Map a minimal deployable boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: Start with one campus gateway, campus identity integration, campus-owned policy and classification service, a durable quota/reservation ledger, local backends, approved local content stores and independently restricted audit storage. Deny direct backend and worker Internet egress; route tools, exporters, support dumps and telemetry through declared controls. Keep full prompts and outputs out of operational telemetry by default, while treating identifiers and usage metadata as potentially sensitive too. Add a separately approved external connector only for eligible projects and destinations. A federation connector additionally needs destination identity, model/version declarations, compatible retention and incident terms, home-campus attribution, authenticated receipts and revocation behavior. The home campus remains the authorization authority; a partner acceptance is necessary but not sufficient. A malicious tenant is contained only within these managed paths: a gateway cannot prevent an authorized human from copying data using unrelated systems.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Make routing policy-first rather than score-first
reasoning_steps.argument: For each request, first authenticate and resolve its project and effective data restrictions. Compute eligible destinations by intersecting home approval, destination acceptance, retention/audit/contract conditions, model and GPU-memory fit, and available authorized budget. Ambiguity yields no off-domain candidate. Only then rank feasible choices by task-specific quality, latency, reproducibility and incremental cost. Failure, overload, provider rejection, exhausted quota or a higher quality estimate cannot enlarge the eligible set. Every retry, agent subcall and tool call is a fresh admission; reusing an earlier authorization is insufficient. A selected endpoint must still pass the release-time gate. If no choice qualifies, queue locally where authorized or return a visible refusal; do not silently downgrade policy or switch providers.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Separate budget safety from cancellation and completion
reasoning_steps.argument: For a budget period with cap B, maintain settled spend S and reservations R_j for all unresolved liabilities, requiring S + sum(R_j) <= B. Admit a paid call only when its enforceable maximum liability fits the remaining cap and all user/project/department limits. Settlement replaces a reservation with a charge no larger than it; this preserves the inequality. An ambiguous charged timeout retains its reservation until authoritative reconciliation. Cancellation is not proof of no charge, and an idempotency key is not proof of provider deduplication without a contract. If a provider cannot bound token, tool and other charges, strict cap safety cannot be derived from this model; disallow that route under a hard-cap policy. Zero paid budget disables paid dispatch and paid retries, not necessarily already funded local service. The $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 monthly caps are scenarios only.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Compare the four baselines without assuming quality or availability
reasoning_steps.argument: Campus-local only has the fewest off-campus content boundaries but still needs controls for logs, caches, tools and administrators; it can fail model-fit, peak-demand or quality requirements. Approved API only needs explicit permission for each data class and an acceptable remote processing contract; without them, sensitive tasks are infeasible regardless of model capability. A campus gateway plus separately approved external access preserves local service and limits external authority to explicit connectors, but does not itself guarantee that researchers cannot bypass the gateway. Federation adds partner administrators, WAN failure modes, capacity commitments, accounting and policy synchronization; usable capacity is only capacity authorized for that task and fitting its model. If no required task gains an authorized quality/latency capability, or external processing already meets those requirements more cheaply, federation has no demonstrated compensating benefit for its additional trust obligations. These are architectural comparisons, not measured performance rankings.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Specify adversarial tests and observable oracles
reasoning_steps.argument: Use synthetic canary content, not real restricted data. Exercise the two partition histories above, revocation between enqueue and dispatch, revocation during streaming, tenant-supplied false labels, a tool exfiltration attempt, diagnostic logging to an unapproved sink, provider rejection, duplicate retries, ambiguous timeout, cancellation and concurrent quota reservations. Collect trusted boundary captures plus authority sequence records and ledger transactions; a gateway's own success log alone cannot establish absence of bypass. Expected safe behavior is no unapproved egress, no automatic external escalation, and no released reservation without settlement evidence. Test campus-authority loss separately from partner loss. For identical isolated-gateway observations, the immediate-revocation design must decline off-campus dispatch in both partition histories. Offline dispatch in H0 and refusal in H1 requires an additional observable authority channel; otherwise the claimed distinction is invalid. None of these tests has been run here.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Define a bounded 90-day decision rather than presume federation
reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: inspect and archive the two starting sources with actual access dates, obtain campus policy/contract decisions, inventory all egress paths, and agree task rubrics and latency targets. Days 31–60: implement the proposed gate in a synthetic-data sandbox and run the adversarial schedules before any sensitive pilot. Days 61–90: compare the four baselines on the same approved task strata: classroom coding, routine analysis, scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context, agentic workflows, sensitive tasks and reproducible batches. Record exact model/version where available, prompts under approved retention, tool versions, seeds/settings, completion quality, queue/cold-start/service latency, throughput, failed tasks, staff hours and costs. Include memory-fit failures, maintenance, peak demand and interactive versus batch queues; report per-campus/per-project tails and longest waits, not only averages. Proposed safety stop threshold is any observed unauthorized egress or reservation-invariant violation. Performance go thresholds must be numerically preregistered by the campuses before measurement; no universal target is invented here. Federation proceeds only if it adds a material authorized task benefit over baseline 3, meets those targets, and its incremental cost and agreements are acceptable. Passing finite tests is not proof against every schedule.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Preserve cost and useful-task denominators
reasoning_steps.argument: For each baseline report annual fully loaded cost as annualized hardware acquisition/replacement without double counting, plus power/cooling, storage, network, support, procurement, staff, API/tool/embedding/egress charges and commitments. Report sunk and incremental views separately; idle capacity remains in fully loaded cost. Monthly average is annual cost/12, not a substitute for peak monthly cash-flow analysis. Cost per active researcher is cost divided by a declared active-user count; cost per useful task is cost divided by tasks meeting both the quality and latency rubric, with zero successes reported as undefined rather than zero cost. Repeated Investigator/Skeptic calls, agent branches, failed attempts and paid retries belong in the numerator. Actual API input/output/cache rates, billing units and commitments require dated provider records that are unavailable here. No numerical break-even or institutional spending claim follows from this analysis.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Establish the source and implementation boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: The project describes MindRouter as an on-campus gateway providing OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic client protocol translation, Ollama/vLLM backends, WDRR scheduling, per-user quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry. These are source claims as reported in the project, not independently inspected documentation or measured guarantees. The starting records are https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf. This session has no access date for either. Federation, frontier routing, distributed budget enforcement and the controls below are proposed extensions, not attributed MindRouter features.

review.rationale: The step accurately limits its assertions to features reported by the project and explicitly disclaims source inspection, measurement and attribution of federation features to MindRouter.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Define the safety contract precisely
reasoning_steps.argument: For a campus c, let P_c be its authoritative policy and let an egress event mean release of a data-bearing unit through a managed boundary, including request bodies, streamed output, tool arguments, logs, embeddings, cache writes and telemetry containing content. Define authorization at that event, not at initial job submission. Immediate revocation means that a revocation ordered before an egress event by the campus authority must govern that event. Previously released data cannot be recalled by this definition. This is a proposed strong contract, not a claim about an existing university policy.

review.rationale: The controlled-egress definition and immediate-revocation ordering are explicit premises of the conditional claim, not alleged existing campus policy. The exclusion of recall of already released data keeps the contract coherent.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Construct indistinguishable partition histories
reasoning_steps.argument: At t0 a gateway G has a valid cached permission allowing project J to send class D to partner B. At t1 G loses communication with the home authority A but can still reach B and the requester. In history H0, A leaves the permission unchanged. In history H1, A revokes it before the next request arrives. Deliver exactly the same requests, clock readings and network observations to G in both histories; A's revocation message cannot cross the partition. Thus G has the same local state when deciding whether to dispatch. A deterministic G makes the same decision; a randomized G has the same decision distribution. Dispatching in H0 for guaranteed availability therefore also permits dispatch in H1, violating the immediate-revocation contract. Denying or waiting preserves this safety condition but sacrifices partition-time dispatch availability. The example requires only one request and one revocation.

review.rationale: The same gateway state and observations force the same deterministic decision or randomized distribution. Dispatch in the unchanged-policy history therefore also permits unauthorized dispatch in the revoked-policy history. The result depends on the stated unavailable revocation channel and strict contract.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Identify what does and does not repair the counterexample
reasoning_steps.argument: A signature establishes who issued an approval, not whether it has since been revoked. A policy-version field cannot reveal an unseen newer version. WDRR and quotas decide service allocation, not destination authorization. A lease repairs the conflict only by changing the contract: permission remains valid until its defined expiry despite a later revocation, or offline dispatch is prohibited. With trusted clocks and explicitly accepted lease semantics, exposure can be bounded by the remaining lease duration, but it is not immediate revocation. Conversely, a reachable home authority can still authorize some remote routes during a partner outage; the result does not prohibit federation generally.

review.rationale: Signatures and version fields cannot reveal an unobserved revocation, and allocation mechanisms do not supply that information. Accepted lease validity changes the authorization contract rather than satisfying immediate revocation; the stated trusted-clock qualification is necessary for a duration bound.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Propose an enforceable, narrower invariant
reasoning_steps.argument: Let L(x) be a conservative set of restrictions attached to object x. For a derivation y from inputs x_i, require L(y) to include the union of their restrictions unless an authorized declassification explicitly changes it; an additional classifier may add restrictions. Unknown classification maps to deny for off-domain egress. Define I: every controlled egress of x to destination d has an authenticated campus principal, current campus authorization for L(x), the required destination/retention agreement, and any necessary budget reservation. Tool results, outputs, caches and diagnostic records are objects under the same rule. This is a proposed information-flow discipline; it does not imply a classifier can reliably identify sensitive data from text alone.

review.rationale: This defines a conservative information-flow specification, conditional on correct labels and authorized declassification. Restriction union prevents derivation alone from relaxing labels, and unknown classification excludes off-domain release. It does not establish automatic classification accuracy.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Derive conditional preservation and its limits
reasoning_steps.argument: Assume trusted label assignment, complete mediation, authenticated destinations and an authority/enforcement mechanism that serializes policy changes with controlled release events. Initially no egress has occurred, so I holds. For the next proposed release, the gate either rejects it, leaving the egress history unchanged, or checks all predicates against the policy ordered at that release and records the authorization before releasing it. Thus the added event satisfies I; induction covers every finite egress prefix. Checking policy and then sending later without this serialization leaves a check-to-use race and does not satisfy the premise. This proof covers the specified release event, not later network delivery, remote use, deletion, arbitrary user-controlled network paths or a compromised gate. Deployment must explain how its concrete streaming and revocation semantics implement that event model.

review.rationale: Under the explicit complete-mediation and serialization premises, rejection adds no event and accepted release adds only an event satisfying the predicates. Induction therefore proves the invariant for finite controlled-egress histories. The step correctly excludes check-to-use races and uncontrolled paths from the conclusion.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Map a minimal deployable boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: Start with one campus gateway, campus identity integration, campus-owned policy and classification service, a durable quota/reservation ledger, local backends, approved local content stores and independently restricted audit storage. Deny direct backend and worker Internet egress; route tools, exporters, support dumps and telemetry through declared controls. Keep full prompts and outputs out of operational telemetry by default, while treating identifiers and usage metadata as potentially sensitive too. Add a separately approved external connector only for eligible projects and destinations. A federation connector additionally needs destination identity, model/version declarations, compatible retention and incident terms, home-campus attribution, authenticated receipts and revocation behavior. The home campus remains the authorization authority; a partner acceptance is necessary but not sufficient. A malicious tenant is contained only within these managed paths: a gateway cannot prevent an authorized human from copying data using unrelated systems.

review.rationale: The component inventory is a useful proposed boundary, and its limits against unrelated human copying are correctly stated. However, it does not yet realize the release-ordering premise required by step 6.
review.objection: Recoverable implementation-specification gap: identify where authoritative revocation and actual release are serialized, including streaming, queued work and crash recovery. The inventory alone does not establish the 'deployable' characterization.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Make routing policy-first rather than score-first
reasoning_steps.argument: For each request, first authenticate and resolve its project and effective data restrictions. Compute eligible destinations by intersecting home approval, destination acceptance, retention/audit/contract conditions, model and GPU-memory fit, and available authorized budget. Ambiguity yields no off-domain candidate. Only then rank feasible choices by task-specific quality, latency, reproducibility and incremental cost. Failure, overload, provider rejection, exhausted quota or a higher quality estimate cannot enlarge the eligible set. Every retry, agent subcall and tool call is a fresh admission; reusing an earlier authorization is insufficient. A selected endpoint must still pass the release-time gate. If no choice qualifies, queue locally where authorized or return a visible refusal; do not silently downgrade policy or switch providers.

review.rationale: Filtering by authorization before optimization prevents a better score or failure response from enlarging the eligible set by definition. Fresh admission and a final release-time gate address stale initial decisions, conditional on implementing that gate correctly.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Separate budget safety from cancellation and completion
reasoning_steps.argument: For a budget period with cap B, maintain settled spend S and reservations R_j for all unresolved liabilities, requiring S + sum(R_j) <= B. Admit a paid call only when its enforceable maximum liability fits the remaining cap and all user/project/department limits. Settlement replaces a reservation with a charge no larger than it; this preserves the inequality. An ambiguous charged timeout retains its reservation until authoritative reconciliation. Cancellation is not proof of no charge, and an idempotency key is not proof of provider deduplication without a contract. If a provider cannot bound token, tool and other charges, strict cap safety cannot be derived from this model; disallow that route under a hard-cap policy. Zero paid budget disables paid dispatch and paid retries, not necessarily already funded local service. The $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 monthly caps are scenarios only.

review.rationale: Atomic admission preserves the cap by reserving only available capacity. Settlement changes total liability by charge minus reservation, which is nonpositive under the stated bound. Retaining ambiguous liabilities avoids false budget reclamation. This remains conditional on enforceable charge bounds and durable atomic handling of all applicable limits.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Compare the four baselines without assuming quality or availability
reasoning_steps.argument: Campus-local only has the fewest off-campus content boundaries but still needs controls for logs, caches, tools and administrators; it can fail model-fit, peak-demand or quality requirements. Approved API only needs explicit permission for each data class and an acceptable remote processing contract; without them, sensitive tasks are infeasible regardless of model capability. A campus gateway plus separately approved external access preserves local service and limits external authority to explicit connectors, but does not itself guarantee that researchers cannot bypass the gateway. Federation adds partner administrators, WAN failure modes, capacity commitments, accounting and policy synchronization; usable capacity is only capacity authorized for that task and fitting its model. If no required task gains an authorized quality/latency capability, or external processing already meets those requirements more cheaply, federation has no demonstrated compensating benefit for its additional trust obligations. These are architectural comparisons, not measured performance rankings.

review.rationale: The comparison identifies architectural obligations and conditional infeasibility rather than asserting measured rankings. Unauthorized or model-incompatible partner capacity cannot count as useful task capacity. The absence of demonstrated compensating benefit is appropriately not a universal claim that federation is inferior.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Specify adversarial tests and observable oracles
reasoning_steps.argument: Use synthetic canary content, not real restricted data. Exercise the two partition histories above, revocation between enqueue and dispatch, revocation during streaming, tenant-supplied false labels, a tool exfiltration attempt, diagnostic logging to an unapproved sink, provider rejection, duplicate retries, ambiguous timeout, cancellation and concurrent quota reservations. Collect trusted boundary captures plus authority sequence records and ledger transactions; a gateway's own success log alone cannot establish absence of bypass. Expected safe behavior is no unapproved egress, no automatic external escalation, and no released reservation without settlement evidence. Test campus-authority loss separately from partner loss. For identical isolated-gateway observations, the immediate-revocation design must decline off-campus dispatch in both partition histories. Offline dispatch in H0 and refusal in H1 requires an additional observable authority channel; otherwise the claimed distinction is invalid. None of these tests has been run here.

review.rationale: The proposed synthetic schedules target the stated failure contracts, and independent boundary observations are stronger than gateway self-reports. Identical observations cannot support opposite dispatch decisions without an additional channel. These are discriminating test specifications, not results or all-schedule proof.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Define a bounded 90-day decision rather than presume federation
reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: inspect and archive the two starting sources with actual access dates, obtain campus policy/contract decisions, inventory all egress paths, and agree task rubrics and latency targets. Days 31–60: implement the proposed gate in a synthetic-data sandbox and run the adversarial schedules before any sensitive pilot. Days 61–90: compare the four baselines on the same approved task strata: classroom coding, routine analysis, scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context, agentic workflows, sensitive tasks and reproducible batches. Record exact model/version where available, prompts under approved retention, tool versions, seeds/settings, completion quality, queue/cold-start/service latency, throughput, failed tasks, staff hours and costs. Include memory-fit failures, maintenance, peak demand and interactive versus batch queues; report per-campus/per-project tails and longest waits, not only averages. Proposed safety stop threshold is any observed unauthorized egress or reservation-invariant violation. Performance go thresholds must be numerically preregistered by the campuses before measurement; no universal target is invented here. Federation proceeds only if it adds a material authorized task benefit over baseline 3, meets those targets, and its incremental cost and agreements are acceptable. Passing finite tests is not proof against every schedule.

review.rationale: The staged pilot separates source and policy work, synthetic safety testing and approved-task comparison. Safety stop conditions are explicit, and performance thresholds are correctly left for preregistration rather than fabricated. Finite passing tests are expressly not promoted to universal safety.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Preserve cost and useful-task denominators
reasoning_steps.argument: For each baseline report annual fully loaded cost as annualized hardware acquisition/replacement without double counting, plus power/cooling, storage, network, support, procurement, staff, API/tool/embedding/egress charges and commitments. Report sunk and incremental views separately; idle capacity remains in fully loaded cost. Monthly average is annual cost/12, not a substitute for peak monthly cash-flow analysis. Cost per active researcher is cost divided by a declared active-user count; cost per useful task is cost divided by tasks meeting both the quality and latency rubric, with zero successes reported as undefined rather than zero cost. Repeated Investigator/Skeptic calls, agent branches, failed attempts and paid retries belong in the numerator. Actual API input/output/cache rates, billing units and commitments require dated provider records that are unavailable here. No numerical break-even or institutional spending claim follows from this analysis.

review.rationale: The accounting distinguishes sunk, incremental and fully loaded views, retains idle capacity and failed paid work in the numerator, and uses quality-and-latency-qualified successes as the task denominator. Annual cost divided by twelve is properly distinguished from monthly cash flow. No unavailable rate or numerical break-even result is asserted.

artifacts.next_question: Specify one minimal campus-controlled release state machine for the immediate-revocation contract, explicitly locating the authoritative policy order and the actual egress boundary. Give hand-checked traces for check→revoke→release, revocation between streaming chunks, and a crash after authorization but before release. Show which transition blocks stale release and how unresolved billing reservations survive recovery; if physical release cannot be serialized under the stated architecture, narrow the contract explicitly. Do not claim execution or deployment evidence.
artifacts.note: Unverified research note. Any Investigator Python or SageMath execution, including its source, status, output, and captured artifacts, is recorded below and is not proof by itself.

objective_review.claim: Conditional on: The impossibility claim uses an immediate-revocation contract defined at controlled egress, with a partition hiding home-authority changes while the gateway can still reach a destination; The two histories give the gateway identical observations; no independent live revocation channel is available; The conditional authorization invariant assumes correct conservative labels, trusted enforcement, authenticated destinations, complete mediation and serialization of policy changes with release events; The budget invariant assumes durable atomic reservations and an enforceable upper bound on each admitted call's total liability; No assumption is made that a remote recipient obeys retention or deletion requirements merely because the gateway authorized a transfer. Conditional on identical gateway observations during a partition, no independent revocation channel, and a requirement that home-campus revocation govern the next controlled egress, guaranteed off-campus dispatch availability is incompatible with zero unauthorized dispatch. Conditional on correct conservative classification, trusted complete mediation, authenticated destinations and serialization of policy changes with release, the proposed gate preserves its event-level authorization invariant. Neither result establishes recipient compliance, implementation safety or the full project's operational and economic feasibility.
objective_review.argument_summary: Cycle 1 supplies a valid indistinguishability argument, a conditional induction over egress events, conditional budget-preservation arithmetic, and a policy-first architecture and pilot proposal. These establish a useful design constraint and bounded formal specifications. They do not establish that the proposed architecture implements the specifications or that federation improves useful research access over the other baselines.

A campus gateway plus separately approved external access preserves local service and limits external authority to explicit connectors, but does not itself guarantee that researchers cannot bypass the gateway. Federation adds partner administrators, WAN failure modes, capacity commitments, accounting and policy synchronization; usable capacity is only capacity authorized for that task and fitting its model. If no required task gains an authorized quality/latency capability, or external processing already meets those requirements more cheaply, federation has no demonstrated compensating benefit for its additional trust obligations. These are architectural comparisons, not measured performance rankings.

review.rationale: The comparison identifies architectural obligations and conditional infeasibility rather than asserting measured rankings. Unauthorized or model-incompatible partner capacity cannot count as useful task capacity. The absence of demonstrated compensating benefit is appropriately not a universal claim that federation is inferior.

argument_steps.title: 11. Specify adversarial tests and observable oracles
argument_steps.argument: Use synthetic canary content, not real restricted data. Exercise the two partition histories above, revocation between enqueue and dispatch, revocation during streaming, tenant-supplied false labels, a tool exfiltration attempt, diagnostic logging to an unapproved sink, provider rejection, duplicate retries, ambiguous timeout, cancellation and concurrent quota reservations. Collect trusted boundary captures plus authority sequence records and ledger transactions; a gateway's own success log alone cannot establish absence of bypass. Expected safe behavior is no unapproved egress, no automatic external escalation, and no released reservation without settlement evidence. Test campus-authority loss separately from partner loss. For identical isolated-gateway observations, the immediate-revocation design must decline off-campus dispatch in both partition histories. Offline dispatch in H0 and refusal in H1 requires an additional observable authority channel; otherwise the claimed distinction is invalid. None of these tests has been run here.

review.rationale: The proposed synthetic schedules target the stated failure contracts, and independent boundary observations are stronger than gateway self-reports. Identical observations cannot support opposite dispatch decisions without an additional channel. These are discriminating test specifications, not results or all-schedule proof.

argument_steps.title: 12. Define a bounded 90-day decision rather than presume federation
argument_steps.argument: Days 1–30: inspect and archive the two starting sources with actual access dates, obtain campus policy/contract decisions, inventory all egress paths, and agree task rubrics and latency targets. Days 31–60: implement the proposed gate in a synthetic-data sandbox and run the adversarial schedules before any sensitive pilot. Days 61–90: compare the four baselines on the same approved task strata: classroom coding, routine analysis, scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context, agentic workflows, sensitive tasks and reproducible batches. Record exact model/version where available, prompts under approved retention, tool versions, seeds/settings, completion quality, queue/cold-start/service latency, throughput, failed tasks, staff hours and costs. Include memory-fit failures, maintenance, peak demand and interactive versus batch queues; report per-campus/per-project tails and longest waits, not only averages. Proposed safety stop threshold is any observed unauthorized egress or reservation-invariant violation. Performance go thresholds must be numerically preregistered by the campuses before measurement; no universal target is invented here. Federation proceeds only if it adds a material authorized task benefit over baseline 3, meets those targets, and its incremental cost and agreements are acceptable. Passing finite tests is not proof against every schedule.

review.rationale: The staged pilot separates source and policy work, synthetic safety testing and approved-task comparison. Safety stop conditions are explicit, and performance thresholds are correctly left for preregistration rather than fabricated. Finite passing tests are expressly not promoted to universal safety.

argument_steps.title: 13. Preserve cost and useful-task denominators
argument_steps.argument: For each baseline report annual fully loaded cost as annualized hardware acquisition/replacement without double counting, plus power/cooling, storage, network, support, procurement, staff, API/tool/embedding/egress charges and commitments. Report sunk and incremental views separately; idle capacity remains in fully loaded cost. Monthly average is annual cost/12, not a substitute for peak monthly cash-flow analysis. Cost per active researcher is cost divided by a declared active-user count; cost per useful task is cost divided by tasks meeting both the quality and latency rubric, with zero successes reported as undefined rather than zero cost. Repeated Investigator/Skeptic calls, agent branches, failed attempts and paid retries belong in the numerator. Actual API input/output/cache rates, billing units and commitments require dated provider records that are unavailable here. No numerical break-even or institutional spending claim follows from this analysis.

review.rationale: The accounting distinguishes sunk, incremental and fully loaded views, retains idle capacity and failed paid work in the numerator, and uses quality-and-latency-qualified successes as the task denominator. Annual cost divided by twelve is properly distinguished from monthly cash flow. No unavailable rate or numerical break-even result is asserted.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define scope and the accounting contract
reasoning_steps.argument: For each budget account k and billing window, let B_k be its cap, F_k finalized spending, and H_k outstanding reservations. Each attempt a has an upper bound r_ak covering its entire possible liability to account k, including applicable tokens, tools, retries internal to the service, fees and currency exposure. Partially billed but unresolved attempts remain entirely represented by their reservation, avoiding double counting. Parent and child accounts overlap intentionally: one dollar consumes one dollar of each applicable user/project/department/campus limit, but is not added repeatedly to campus spending. Fixed commitments must already be charged to F or reserved. This model concerns expenses controlled by the gateway; unauthorized credentials or independent purchases lie outside its guarantee.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Admission and dispatch require separate policy and budget gates
reasoning_steps.argument: First determine eligible destinations using campus identity, classification, destination approval, contracts, retention, audit rules and model/resource fit. Classification covers prompts, outputs, logs, embeddings, caches and tool traffic; ambiguity gives an empty eligible set. Unclassified task-derived telemetry is not automatically exportable. Only then rank eligible routes by task suitability, estimated completion latency and cost. Immediately before egress, revalidate authoritative policy and atomically reserve every applicable account, accepting only if F_k + sum(H_k) + r_ak <= B_k for every k. Persist a may-have-been-sent state before transmission. A crash or transport retry cannot authorize a second potentially chargeable attempt without another reservation or verified provider deduplication covering charges. Bounded output alone is insufficient if unbounded tool loops or fees remain possible. Reject or require a contractually enforceable bound when liability cannot be bounded.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Prove the budget invariant under the stated contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially require F_k + sum(H_k) <= B_k. Atomic admission preserves this inequality by its explicit test; dispatch does not change it. At final settlement, remove r_ak and add actual final charge c_ak, where 0 <= c_ak <= r_ak, so the total cannot increase. A certified never-sent attempt can release its reservation without adding a charge. Unknown outcomes, cancellation requests and timeouts leave the reservation unchanged. These cases exhaust allowed transitions, proving the invariant by induction for every account and any interleaving serialized by the ledger. Actual eventual liability is bounded by finalized spending plus held upper bounds. This proves an accounting property, not provider compliance, implementation correctness or useful availability. Across months, unresolved liability cannot simply disappear at reset: retain a cross-window encumbrance or assign it according to an explicitly bounded billing contract.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Minimal indistinguishable timeout counterexample
reasoning_steps.argument: Take remaining budget b > 0 and calls costing exactly b. In history A, the provider never receives the first request; in history B, it completes and charges b, but the response is lost. Up to the timeout, the campus sees identical observations. If it releases the hold and sends another independently billable call, history B can incur 2b against a cap of b. If it keeps the hold, history A can leave a useful retry blocked despite zero actual spending. A guaranteed safe, immediate retry cannot be chosen from these observations alone. An oracle could separate the histories: a binding no-charge receipt, final billing reconciliation, or documented and tested idempotency that deduplicates billing and all tool effects. A cancellation acknowledgement is not such an oracle unless its contract explicitly establishes final liability. This is an exact constructed counterexample, not observed provider behavior.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Minimal architecture and remaining trust boundaries
reasoning_steps.argument: Deploy campus SSO and classification entry points, a campus policy decision service, enforced egress, a durable hierarchical ledger, admission queues and endpoint adapters, with restricted audit storage and reconciliation. Every tool call and agent continuation re-enters admission; a multi-call workflow may reserve a bounded parent envelope and allocate child holds without double spending it. External access uses separately approved credentials and destinations, not an overload fallback. Enforce policy at the actual egress boundary; control-plane ranking alone is insufficient. During policy-authority or ledger partitions, fail closed for new dispatches requiring them. Immediate remote revocation after data has already been transmitted cannot be guaranteed; define revocation semantics and retention/deletion obligations contractually. A hypothetical federation adds remote identity mapping, destination attestations, remote logs/caches, agreements and accountable charge/service records. It must not receive content until all those domains are authorized.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Scheduling fairness is separate from eligibility and budget safety
reasoning_steps.argument: Apply proposed hierarchical fair sharing within eligible resource pools, distinguishing interactive and batch capacity. GPU memory, model version, context length and modality constrain which queues can actually run. WDRR weights and per-user quotas alone do not prove bounded waiting: a job requiring an unavailable large-memory GPU never becomes runnable, and one uninterruptible job can occupy a device indefinitely. A finite waiting bound additionally needs bounded nonpreemptive work or effective preemption, recurring compatible capacity, positive scheduling shares and controlled admitted load. Use bounded request sizes, aging or reserved batch windows, and report resource-ineligible waiting separately from scheduler waiting. Enforce quotas above identities at project and department levels to limit account-splitting. Measure GPU-seconds, memory occupancy and delivered work within compatible pools; equal token counts are not necessarily equal GPU cost. Cold starts, maintenance and reserved idle headroom belong in capacity planning. Backend support for preemption or bounded service quanta remains unverified.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Compare four baselines on authorized usefulness, not nominal reachability
reasoning_steps.argument: Campus-local only minimizes external trust dependencies but cannot serve tasks exceeding local fit, quality or capacity. Approved API only removes campus inference hardware dependence but requires WAN/provider availability, suitable contracts and payable budget; it may be ineligible for sensitive tasks. A campus gateway plus separately approved external access supports a visible choice of authorized services without automatic policy-crossing fallback. Federation can help only if another campus offers authorized, compatible capacity at the needed time; it cannot rescue a task authorized exclusively for the originating campus. It also introduces WAN, remote-operation and agreement dependencies. Compare all four on the same task inventory, showing both shared-eligible performance and total authorized coverage. Include coding, routine analysis, demanding reasoning, multimodal/long-context tasks, agent workflows, restricted-data tasks and pinned reproducible batches. Record unavailable or rejected tasks rather than excluding them. A reachable endpoint is not success: success requires rubric quality, deadline, provenance and policy compliance. Record model/version, backend, parameters, tools, policy version and seeds where supported; pinned provenance does not imply bitwise reproducibility.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Cost accounting determines whether pooling is worth its extra burden
reasoning_steps.argument: For each baseline report annual fully loaded cost as annualized hardware purchase plus replacement allowance, idle and utilized power/cooling, storage, network, hardware support, procurement, operations staff, external charges and agreement/security administration. Avoid counting the same replacement both in depreciation and a replacement allowance. Separately report sunk expenditure and avoidable incremental cash cost. API charges require dated contractual input/output/cache prices, actual multi-call token counts, tool/embedding charges, retries, egress, minimum commitments and unresolved-liability bounds; none are available here. Monthly equivalent is annual cost/12; cost per active researcher divides by a defined active population, and cost per useful task divides by tasks satisfying the declared quality/latency/policy target, including failed-attempt costs in the numerator. A zero-success denominator is undefined, not zero cost. The illustrative external caps of $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 monthly correspond to $24,000/$48,000/$96,000 annual ceilings, not expected expenditure or total service cost. At zero paid budget, admit no positively priced external attempt; local operation still has resource and staff costs. Federation is economically preferred only when its measured gains exceed WAN, administration, duplicated support and agreement costs over the relevant feasible alternatives.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. A measurable 90-day pilot with an adversarial oracle
reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: campus computing owns workload/fit inventory and instrumentation; security owns classification and egress tests; procurement/legal verifies prices, billing bounds, retention and agreements; faculty and students define usefulness rubrics and task-specific latency targets before testing. Days 31–60: run synthetic fault tests against an independently logged mock provider recording receives, effects and charges. Inject stale policy, malicious tenant routing hints, simultaneous quota claims, WAN/campus/provider outages, rejection, accepted-but-response-lost timeouts, cancellation races, crash-after-send and unsafe fallback. Every unauthorized transmission or excess worst-case liability fails the gate. Explicit controls compare premature timeout-release with hold-until-reconciliation; the constructed two-history test predicts overspend only for premature release when the first attempt was charged. Days 61–90: after approvals, compare eligible real tasks across available baselines using paired tasks, randomized order and blinded quality scoring where feasible. Test peak demand, cold starts, maintenance, batch/interactive contention and heterogeneous model fit. Use synthetic sensitive data until real-data approval. Federation remains an emulation unless actual agreements and a deployment exist. Report per-class success, p50/p95 queue and end-to-end latency, throughput, authorized useful availability, starvation counts, utilization, incident/reconciliation time, staff hours and cost, with uncertainty intervals and explicit sample counts.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Proposed decision thresholds and discriminating federation test
reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed thresholds, not observed results: stop immediately on any demonstrated unauthorized egress, ledger overspend, or silent paid escalation. Proceed to a limited deployment only if billing contracts support the invariant, all specified fault cases pass, and each advertised task class achieves at least 90% useful completion within its predeclared latency target; report confidence intervals and do not describe sparse classes as established. Count rejections and deadline expiry as failures in end-user availability, so safety-driven refusal cannot inflate reliability. Computing must separately show no admitted runnable job exceeds its declared queue deadline under the advertised load envelope; overload requires explicit rejection rather than an unconditional starvation guarantee. Prefer baseline 3 unless federation demonstrates either at least a 10-percentage-point increase in authorized useful coverage or at least a 20% reduction in fully loaded cost per useful task, with uncertainty supporting the direction, no safety regression and named staffing/legal ownership. These are proposed governance hurdles, not universal optimal thresholds. The key competing explanation is that federation adds nominal GPU supply but little authorized, compatible, timely supply. A paired peak-load test with per-request eligibility and completion records can distinguish that explanation from useful pooling.
