reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define scope and the accounting contract
reasoning_steps.argument: For each budget account k and billing window, let B_k be its cap, F_k finalized spending, and H_k outstanding reservations. Each attempt a has an upper bound r_ak covering its entire possible liability to account k, including applicable tokens, tools, retries internal to the service, fees and currency exposure. Partially billed but unresolved attempts remain entirely represented by their reservation, avoiding double counting. Parent and child accounts overlap intentionally: one dollar consumes one dollar of each applicable user/project/department/campus limit, but is not added repeatedly to campus spending. Fixed commitments must already be charged to F or reserved. This model concerns expenses controlled by the gateway; unauthorized credentials or independent purchases lie outside its guarantee.

review.rationale: Accepted as the explicit premise of the conditional claim, not an established provider or campus property. Overlapping hierarchical accounts do not double-count campus expenditure, and unresolved partial billing can remain represented by the full hold if it is not also added to finalized spending.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Admission and dispatch require separate policy and budget gates
reasoning_steps.argument: First determine eligible destinations using campus identity, classification, destination approval, contracts, retention, audit rules and model/resource fit. Classification covers prompts, outputs, logs, embeddings, caches and tool traffic; ambiguity gives an empty eligible set. Unclassified task-derived telemetry is not automatically exportable. Only then rank eligible routes by task suitability, estimated completion latency and cost. Immediately before egress, revalidate authoritative policy and atomically reserve every applicable account, accepting only if F_k + sum(H_k) + r_ak <= B_k for every k. Persist a may-have-been-sent state before transmission. A crash or transport retry cannot authorize a second potentially chargeable attempt without another reservation or verified provider deduplication covering charges. Bounded output alone is insufficient if unbounded tool loops or fees remain possible. Reject or require a contractually enforceable bound when liability cannot be bounded.

review.rationale: The atomic multi-account budget gate supports the accounting invariant. The policy gate, however, does not define the ordering of authorization, revocation and transmission.
review.objection: Revalidate under policy v; revoke authorization; transmit. The proposal needs an explicit contract stating whether this request was already authorized in flight or must be blocked. Merely saying immediately before egress does not resolve the race.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Prove the budget invariant under the stated contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially require F_k + sum(H_k) <= B_k. Atomic admission preserves this inequality by its explicit test; dispatch does not change it. At final settlement, remove r_ak and add actual final charge c_ak, where 0 <= c_ak <= r_ak, so the total cannot increase. A certified never-sent attempt can release its reservation without adding a charge. Unknown outcomes, cancellation requests and timeouts leave the reservation unchanged. These cases exhaust allowed transitions, proving the invariant by induction for every account and any interleaving serialized by the ledger. Actual eventual liability is bounded by finalized spending plus held upper bounds. This proves an accounting property, not provider compliance, implementation correctness or useful availability. Across months, unresolved liability cannot simply disappear at reset: retain a cross-window encumbrance or assign it according to an explicitly bounded billing contract.

review.rationale: Under the listed accounting contract and initial invariant, admission checks the bound, dispatch leaves it unchanged, settlement substitutes c ≤ r, and certified release decreases holds. Induction therefore establishes the bound for the specified transitions. Cross-window safety remains conditional on retained liability and the applicable billing contract.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Minimal indistinguishable timeout counterexample
reasoning_steps.argument: Take remaining budget b > 0 and calls costing exactly b. In history A, the provider never receives the first request; in history B, it completes and charges b, but the response is lost. Up to the timeout, the campus sees identical observations. If it releases the hold and sends another independently billable call, history B can incur 2b against a cap of b. If it keeps the hold, history A can leave a useful retry blocked despite zero actual spending. A guaranteed safe, immediate retry cannot be chosen from these observations alone. An oracle could separate the histories: a binding no-charge receipt, final billing reconciliation, or documented and tested idempotency that deduplicates billing and all tool effects. A cancellation acknowledgement is not such an oracle unless its contract explicitly establishes final liability. This is an exact constructed counterexample, not observed provider behavior.

review.rationale: The campus observations can be identical despite different provider liabilities. A second independently charged attempt can produce 2b liability in the charged history, whereas retaining the hold blocks retry in the uncharged history. A binding settlement or deduplication oracle supplies information absent from the timeout alone.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Minimal architecture and remaining trust boundaries
reasoning_steps.argument: Deploy campus SSO and classification entry points, a campus policy decision service, enforced egress, a durable hierarchical ledger, admission queues and endpoint adapters, with restricted audit storage and reconciliation. Every tool call and agent continuation re-enters admission; a multi-call workflow may reserve a bounded parent envelope and allocate child holds without double spending it. External access uses separately approved credentials and destinations, not an overload fallback. Enforce policy at the actual egress boundary; control-plane ranking alone is insufficient. During policy-authority or ledger partitions, fail closed for new dispatches requiring them. Immediate remote revocation after data has already been transmitted cannot be guaranteed; define revocation semantics and retention/deletion obligations contractually. A hypothetical federation adds remote identity mapping, destination attestations, remote logs/caches, agreements and accountable charge/service records. It must not receive content until all those domains are authorized.

review.rationale: The listed components identify relevant enforcement and trust boundaries, and correctly distinguish already-exported data from future admission. They do not yet establish complete policy enforcement across revocation and dispatch races.
review.objection: Specify the freshness, partition and in-flight semantics connecting the policy authority to actual egress. The architectural component list alone is not a safety argument.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Scheduling fairness is separate from eligibility and budget safety
reasoning_steps.argument: Apply proposed hierarchical fair sharing within eligible resource pools, distinguishing interactive and batch capacity. GPU memory, model version, context length and modality constrain which queues can actually run. WDRR weights and per-user quotas alone do not prove bounded waiting: a job requiring an unavailable large-memory GPU never becomes runnable, and one uninterruptible job can occupy a device indefinitely. A finite waiting bound additionally needs bounded nonpreemptive work or effective preemption, recurring compatible capacity, positive scheduling shares and controlled admitted load. Use bounded request sizes, aging or reserved batch windows, and report resource-ineligible waiting separately from scheduler waiting. Enforce quotas above identities at project and department levels to limit account-splitting. Measure GPU-seconds, memory occupancy and delivered work within compatible pools; equal token counts are not necessarily equal GPU cost. Cold starts, maintenance and reserved idle headroom belong in capacity planning. Backend support for preemption or bounded service quanta remains unverified.

review.rationale: The unavailable-compatible-GPU and indefinitely occupied-device examples establish why weights and quotas alone cannot guarantee waiting bounds. The additional conditions are presented as requirements to investigate, not as an already-proved sufficient scheduler contract.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Compare four baselines on authorized usefulness, not nominal reachability
reasoning_steps.argument: Campus-local only minimizes external trust dependencies but cannot serve tasks exceeding local fit, quality or capacity. Approved API only removes campus inference hardware dependence but requires WAN/provider availability, suitable contracts and payable budget; it may be ineligible for sensitive tasks. A campus gateway plus separately approved external access supports a visible choice of authorized services without automatic policy-crossing fallback. Federation can help only if another campus offers authorized, compatible capacity at the needed time; it cannot rescue a task authorized exclusively for the originating campus. It also introduces WAN, remote-operation and agreement dependencies. Compare all four on the same task inventory, showing both shared-eligible performance and total authorized coverage. Include coding, routine analysis, demanding reasoning, multimodal/long-context tasks, agent workflows, restricted-data tasks and pinned reproducible batches. Record unavailable or rejected tasks rather than excluding them. A reachable endpoint is not success: success requires rubric quality, deadline, provenance and policy compliance. Record model/version, backend, parameters, tools, policy version and seeds where supported; pinned provenance does not imply bitwise reproducibility.

review.rationale: The baseline distinctions follow from eligibility, capacity and dependency constraints. Reporting both common-eligible performance and total authorized coverage avoids hiding rejected tasks; recording provenance does not imply deterministic reproduction. No measured ranking is asserted.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Cost accounting determines whether pooling is worth its extra burden
reasoning_steps.argument: For each baseline report annual fully loaded cost as annualized hardware purchase plus replacement allowance, idle and utilized power/cooling, storage, network, hardware support, procurement, operations staff, external charges and agreement/security administration. Avoid counting the same replacement both in depreciation and a replacement allowance. Separately report sunk expenditure and avoidable incremental cash cost. API charges require dated contractual input/output/cache prices, actual multi-call token counts, tool/embedding charges, retries, egress, minimum commitments and unresolved-liability bounds; none are available here. Monthly equivalent is annual cost/12; cost per active researcher divides by a defined active population, and cost per useful task divides by tasks satisfying the declared quality/latency/policy target, including failed-attempt costs in the numerator. A zero-success denominator is undefined, not zero cost. The illustrative external caps of $2,000/$4,000/$8,000 monthly correspond to $24,000/$48,000/$96,000 annual ceilings, not expected expenditure or total service cost. At zero paid budget, admit no positively priced external attempt; local operation still has resource and staff costs. Federation is economically preferred only when its measured gains exceed WAN, administration, duplicated support and agreement costs over the relevant feasible alternatives.

review.rationale: The cost categories and denominators form a defensible accounting framework, with explicit avoidance of replacement double-counting and failed-attempt exclusion. Multiplying the illustrative monthly caps by twelve gives the stated annual ceilings, not expected spending. Numerical total-cost and break-even results are appropriately left unavailable.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. A measurable 90-day pilot with an adversarial oracle
reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: campus computing owns workload/fit inventory and instrumentation; security owns classification and egress tests; procurement/legal verifies prices, billing bounds, retention and agreements; faculty and students define usefulness rubrics and task-specific latency targets before testing. Days 31–60: run synthetic fault tests against an independently logged mock provider recording receives, effects and charges. Inject stale policy, malicious tenant routing hints, simultaneous quota claims, WAN/campus/provider outages, rejection, accepted-but-response-lost timeouts, cancellation races, crash-after-send and unsafe fallback. Every unauthorized transmission or excess worst-case liability fails the gate. Explicit controls compare premature timeout-release with hold-until-reconciliation; the constructed two-history test predicts overspend only for premature release when the first attempt was charged. Days 61–90: after approvals, compare eligible real tasks across available baselines using paired tasks, randomized order and blinded quality scoring where feasible. Test peak demand, cold starts, maintenance, batch/interactive contention and heterogeneous model fit. Use synthetic sensitive data until real-data approval. Federation remains an emulation unless actual agreements and a deployment exist. Report per-class success, p50/p95 queue and end-to-end latency, throughput, authorized useful availability, starvation counts, utilization, incident/reconciliation time, staff hours and cost, with uncertainty intervals and explicit sample counts.

review.rationale: Accepted as a proposed experimental protocol. An independently logged mock provider can distinguish unknown campus outcomes from actual acceptance and charges, directly testing premature release against retained holds. Mock results would not establish real-provider contract compliance.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Proposed decision thresholds and discriminating federation test
reasoning_steps.argument: Proposed thresholds, not observed results: stop immediately on any demonstrated unauthorized egress, ledger overspend, or silent paid escalation. Proceed to a limited deployment only if billing contracts support the invariant, all specified fault cases pass, and each advertised task class achieves at least 90% useful completion within its predeclared latency target; report confidence intervals and do not describe sparse classes as established. Count rejections and deadline expiry as failures in end-user availability, so safety-driven refusal cannot inflate reliability. Computing must separately show no admitted runnable job exceeds its declared queue deadline under the advertised load envelope; overload requires explicit rejection rather than an unconditional starvation guarantee. Prefer baseline 3 unless federation demonstrates either at least a 10-percentage-point increase in authorized useful coverage or at least a 20% reduction in fully loaded cost per useful task, with uncertainty supporting the direction, no safety regression and named staffing/legal ownership. These are proposed governance hurdles, not universal optimal thresholds. The key competing explanation is that federation adds nominal GPU supply but little authorized, compatible, timely supply. A paired peak-load test with per-request eligibility and completion records can distinguish that explanation from useful pooling.

review.rationale: Accepted as explicitly proposed governance thresholds, not empirically justified optima. Paired peak-load records can test whether nominal remote supply becomes authorized useful capacity. Sample sizes, uncertainty rules and agreed latency targets must still be fixed before these thresholds support deployment decisions.

Analyze authorization–revocation–send and revocation–authorization–send histories, including a partition, and define an independently observable pass/fail oracle. State which policy guarantee is achievable without claiming instantaneous revocation of already transmitted data.

artifacts.skeptic_response:
The current cycle answers the bounded dispatch/revocation question with a convincing, conditional reference-model argument. Authorization A and controlled handoff H share a critical section with revocation R. Therefore a successful A–R–H ordering is excluded. If R commits first and its prohibition remains effective, subsequent authorization fails. Conversely, A–H–R–S is permitted when S denotes later physical transmission. This explicitly resolves the earlier ambiguity without claiming recall of transmitted or transport-buffered data.

The partition analysis is also sound within its stated scope. Colocation removes the autonomous remote sender from the authorization decision, but does not make remotely submitted revocations instantaneous: an administrator disconnected from the authority cannot obtain a successful commit acknowledgement. For a separated sender, the unchanged-policy and revoked-policy histories are observationally identical during a partition; cached approval cannot provide both continued dispatch and compliance with the latest authority state. This is a negative result about that candidate design, not a refutation of federation generally.

The proposed oracle correctly observes H separately from destination receipt, uses causal barriers rather than cross-host clock ordering, and treats missing capture as inconclusive. No instrumentation, fencing, complete-mediation property or campus acceptance has been demonstrated. The model deliberately permits revocation acknowledgements to wait behind a dispatch; bounded revocation and recovery latency remain separate service requirements.

The cycle-1 accounting result remains supported under its separate five accounting premises: admission checks the cap, settlement changes the encumbrance by c−r ≤ 0, and unknown outcomes retain their holds. Its charged-timeout counterexample also remains valid. Neither result supplies implementation evidence.

The overall project remains partial. The exact MindRouter documentation and PEARC’26 PDF were not inspected; 2026-10-31 is the brief’s reported review date, not this reviewer’s access date. Current contractual prices, campus policies, operational measurements and comparative economics remain unavailable. Federation, frontier routing and this state machine remain proposed extensions. The next useful analytical step is to make the pilot’s statistical decision rule explicit rather than repeat the completed conditional safety proof.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define the controlled boundary and the policy contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Let A be the durable authorization commit for one attempt; H the transfer of its frozen request envelope into the trusted egress transport; S a later physical network transmission; and R the durable revocation commit at the authoritative campus gate. H, not provider receipt or the last packet leaving a NIC, is the last controlled release boundary in this contract. Before H the gate can suppress the entire request. After H the request is logically in flight, including bytes buffered in the trusted transport. Revocation blocks new handoffs; it cannot recall those bytes. Administrative submission of revocation and acknowledgement of committed revocation are distinct events.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. State the enforcement premises
reasoning_steps.argument: All relevant releases and policy changes traverse one campus enforcement service. It owns the authoritative policy state and transport credentials; workers and tenants cannot send around it. Identity revocation, classification changes, destination withdrawal and contractual restrictions must enter its policy order. Independent upstream changes not yet incorporated into that order are outside the guarantee. The service uses one serialization lock for authorization/handoff and policy mutation, durable records, and immutable request buffers. Recovery fences the previous sender before allowing new commits. These are implementation requirements, not established campus or MindRouter properties.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Specify the request and policy state
reasoning_steps.argument: Policy state is an epoch and an explicit eligibility predicate. Each attempt binds campus, subject, project, classification, exact content, destination identity, model/configuration, approved artifact domains, size/output bounds and budget-hold identifiers. A request starts QUEUED, with no reusable dispatch authority. It can become READY only when its envelope is frozen and a compatible endpoint and bounded transport capacity are available. An unknown label or missing approval gives no eligible destination. Changing content, destination, tool action or model requires a new attempt. The binding covers prompts and approved handling of outputs, logs, caches, embeddings and telemetry; it does not establish that a recipient actually honors those obligations.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Give the minimal dispatch transition
reasoning_steps.argument: From READY, obtain the required durable budget holds, then acquire the policy/egress lock. Re-evaluate eligibility against the authoritative current epoch. On failure, enter BLOCKED without handoff. On success, durably record MAY_SEND with the frozen envelope and epoch; this commit is A, the authorization linearization point. While still holding the lock, perform one nonblocking H into the trusted transport and record IN_FLIGHT if acknowledged. Only then release the lock. Transport admission must accept ownership of one bounded immutable envelope, not an unbounded workflow or future mutable stream. READY jobs are not preauthorized while waiting in scheduling queues. If the handoff outcome is uncertain, enter UNKNOWN, not retryable READY. No delayed worker may later exercise A independently.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Give revocation and the in-flight contract
reasoning_steps.argument: A revocation acquires the same lock, durably increments the epoch and changes the eligibility predicate; that commit is R. Acknowledge success only after R. Thus a revocation arriving while dispatch holds the lock remains pending until that handoff finishes or is abandoned. Existing queued requests must pass the new predicate. Requests already handed off may finish their single frozen envelope and return results only through approved handling paths. Cancellation and remote deletion are best-effort requests unless stronger inspected contracts exist. They are not recall guarantees. Every new agent call, tool call, redirect, content-bearing reconnection or fallback must re-enter admission. Transport retransmission of already accepted bytes is part of the original in-flight transfer; a new independently chargeable application attempt is not.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Prove the new-handoff safety property
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially there are no authorized attempts or handed-off envelopes. For any H, the dispatch transition requires a preceding A under the lock, with eligibility true in epoch e. No R can occur between that validation and H because R requires the same lock. Consequently policy at H still authorizes that exact envelope. After an R withdrawing its eligibility, a later dispatch sees the changed predicate and cannot reach H unless a subsequent explicit policy change authorizes it again. The remaining transitions either make no handoff or concern an envelope already handed off. Induction over these transitions proves the property for all modeled interleavings. It proves neither physical packet suppression after R nor recipient compliance.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Analyze authorization–revocation–send
reasoning_steps.argument: If send means H, a successful A–R–H history is excluded: the dispatch lock prevents R from committing between A and H. A revocation invocation may occur there, but its successful acknowledgement must wait. If dispatch crashes after A without H, recovery must abandon that attempt and fence the old sender before R can commit; A cannot later be replayed. If send means physical S, A–H–R–S is allowed: transport buffering or network delay can place physical transmission or receipt after revocation. A–R–S alone therefore lacks enough information to classify a violation. The oracle must locate H. Permitting A–R–H through an outstanding token would implement a weaker grandfathered-authorization contract, which this design does not adopt.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Analyze revocation–authorization–send
reasoning_steps.argument: For R–A–H concerning the revoked subject/destination, A must fail while that prohibition remains effective. An earlier preliminary eligibility check is not A and cannot override R. A concurrent authorization and revocation are ordered by the lock: either dispatch completes its controlled handoff first, or revocation commits first and blocks it. An authorization begun after receipt of a successful revocation acknowledgement must observe R. An explicit later reapproval can authorize a new attempt, but neither timeout nor overload constitutes reapproval. Revocations unrelated to the request do not require rejecting it; the predicate, not epoch inequality alone, determines eligibility.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Partition behavior and the competing cached-check design
reasoning_steps.argument: In the proposed minimum, authority and controlled handoff are colocated. A partition disconnecting a worker from this service prevents new handoffs by that worker; a partition disconnecting an administrator can leave a revocation uncommitted and must not produce a success acknowledgement. If authority and an autonomous sender are separated instead, consider two histories after their link partitions: in one, the authority makes no change; in the other, it commits a revocation. The sender sees the same messages in both. Sending under a cached approval preserves service in the first history but violates latest-authority handoff policy in the second. Refusing preserves safety but loses availability. A lease changes the contract by permitting a stale interval; it does not establish immediate revocation. Physical sends of envelopes handed off before the partition remain in flight.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Crash, cancellation and budget integration
reasoning_steps.argument: The MAY_SEND record is written before H because a crash can otherwise erase evidence of liability. If recovery cannot determine whether H occurred, mark UNKNOWN, prohibit replay and retain the reservation. Fencing must stop the old process from later making a new H; absent confirmed fencing, neither recovery nor successful revocation acknowledgement may proceed. An already accepted transport envelope remains in flight. This sacrifices availability rather than assuming exactly-once delivery. Preserve the prior accounting invariant independently: admission tests finalized spending plus outstanding holds against each cap; final settlement replaces a hold r by charge c ≤ r; certified non-dispatch can release a hold; unknown outcomes cannot. Revocation or cancellation alone supplies no certificate of non-dispatch or zero charge.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Define an independently observable oracle
reasoning_steps.argument: Use synthetic labeled envelopes and a security-owned test controller with separate instrumentation at the trusted transport ownership boundary and a mock destination recording received bytes and effects. The controller supplies policy changes and maintains a reference eligibility predicate; it does not infer success from router logs alone. Record attempt/content/destination bindings, A and R commit receipts, H events, fencing events and mock receipts. Establish order with barriers and acknowledgements rather than cross-host timestamps. Force pauses after preliminary checking, after A but before H, after H, and during recovery. A FAIL is an H forbidden by the reference policy in the committed order, a mutation or destination substitution, an unadmitted application retry, an unfenced old sender making H, or an acknowledgement of R followed by a new forbidden H. Receipt after R with H before R is not a safety failure. Missing capture, uncertain ordering or broken controls makes a trial inconclusive, not a pass. Include an authorized positive control to demonstrate that both sensors detect traffic.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Specify the decisive tests and deployment implication
reasoning_steps.argument: The unsafe control performs a check, releases its lock, pauses, accepts and acknowledges revocation, then hands off; the constructed history predicts a forbidden H. The proposed design, paused after A, must either complete H before R commits or abandon/fence the attempt before acknowledging R. A hung lock with no revocation acknowledgement is a liveness failure, not proof of safety or a successful revocation. Test partitions, stale workers, malicious redirects, payload mutation, simultaneous quota claims, cancellation and crash-after-handoff. In the 90-day pilot, days 1–30 assign security the boundary/contract approval and computing the instrumentation; days 31–60 run these controlled fault histories; days 61–90 measure revocation-ack latency, refusal rate, recovery time and useful completion under the agreed load. Any forbidden H stops the pilot; incomplete instrumentation blocks a go decision. Campus-local, API-only and gateway-plus-separately-approved-API services can share this campus gate. Federation adds remote enforcement and recipient obligations without eliminating the ordering constraint. Baseline 3 remains the simpler design candidate unless measured authorized pooling benefits justify those additions; no comparative winner is established.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Define the controlled boundary and the policy contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Let A be the durable authorization commit for one attempt; H the transfer of its frozen request envelope into the trusted egress transport; S a later physical network transmission; and R the durable revocation commit at the authoritative campus gate. H, not provider receipt or the last packet leaving a NIC, is the last controlled release boundary in this contract. Before H the gate can suppress the entire request. After H the request is logically in flight, including bytes buffered in the trusted transport. Revocation blocks new handoffs; it cannot recall those bytes. Administrative submission of revocation and acknowledgement of committed revocation are distinct events.

review.rationale: Accepted as the expressly conditional boundary contract. Distinguishing transport ownership H from physical transmission S makes later delivery after R consistent with the claim; it does not establish campus acceptance of that contract.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. State the enforcement premises
reasoning_steps.argument: All relevant releases and policy changes traverse one campus enforcement service. It owns the authoritative policy state and transport credentials; workers and tenants cannot send around it. Identity revocation, classification changes, destination withdrawal and contractual restrictions must enter its policy order. Independent upstream changes not yet incorporated into that order are outside the guarantee. The service uses one serialization lock for authorization/handoff and policy mutation, durable records, and immutable request buffers. Recovery fences the previous sender before allowing new commits. These are implementation requirements, not established campus or MindRouter properties.

review.rationale: Accepted as enforcement premises, not observations. Complete mediation, a common policy order, immutable buffers and fencing are sufficient premises for the later serialized model; excluding unincorporated upstream changes appropriately narrows its scope.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Specify the request and policy state
reasoning_steps.argument: Policy state is an epoch and an explicit eligibility predicate. Each attempt binds campus, subject, project, classification, exact content, destination identity, model/configuration, approved artifact domains, size/output bounds and budget-hold identifiers. A request starts QUEUED, with no reusable dispatch authority. It can become READY only when its envelope is frozen and a compatible endpoint and bounded transport capacity are available. An unknown label or missing approval gives no eligible destination. Changing content, destination, tool action or model requires a new attempt. The binding covers prompts and approved handling of outputs, logs, caches, embeddings and telemetry; it does not establish that a recipient actually honors those obligations.

review.rationale: The frozen envelope and explicit eligibility predicate prevent authorization from being transferred to changed content or destinations within the model. Fail-closed classification and separate recipient-compliance limitations are consistent with the project requirements.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Give the minimal dispatch transition
reasoning_steps.argument: From READY, obtain the required durable budget holds, then acquire the policy/egress lock. Re-evaluate eligibility against the authoritative current epoch. On failure, enter BLOCKED without handoff. On success, durably record MAY_SEND with the frozen envelope and epoch; this commit is A, the authorization linearization point. While still holding the lock, perform one nonblocking H into the trusted transport and record IN_FLIGHT if acknowledged. Only then release the lock. Transport admission must accept ownership of one bounded immutable envelope, not an unbounded workflow or future mutable stream. READY jobs are not preauthorized while waiting in scheduling queues. If the handoff outcome is uncertain, enter UNKNOWN, not retryable READY. No delayed worker may later exercise A independently.

review.rationale: Holding the common lock from final validation through A and H prevents intervening policy mutation. UNKNOWN and the prohibition on delayed independent exercise of A avoid treating uncertain handoff as reusable authority. This depends on the stated transport-ownership and recovery premises.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Give revocation and the in-flight contract
reasoning_steps.argument: A revocation acquires the same lock, durably increments the epoch and changes the eligibility predicate; that commit is R. Acknowledge success only after R. Thus a revocation arriving while dispatch holds the lock remains pending until that handoff finishes or is abandoned. Existing queued requests must pass the new predicate. Requests already handed off may finish their single frozen envelope and return results only through approved handling paths. Cancellation and remote deletion are best-effort requests unless stronger inspected contracts exist. They are not recall guarantees. Every new agent call, tool call, redirect, content-bearing reconnection or fallback must re-enter admission. Transport retransmission of already accepted bytes is part of the original in-flight transfer; a new independently chargeable application attempt is not.

review.rationale: R uses the same serialization mechanism, so pending revocation cannot be mistaken for committed revocation. The single-envelope in-flight exception and fresh admission for new application actions preserve the specified boundary without promising recall.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Prove the new-handoff safety property
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially there are no authorized attempts or handed-off envelopes. For any H, the dispatch transition requires a preceding A under the lock, with eligibility true in epoch e. No R can occur between that validation and H because R requires the same lock. Consequently policy at H still authorizes that exact envelope. After an R withdrawing its eligibility, a later dispatch sees the changed predicate and cannot reach H unless a subsequent explicit policy change authorizes it again. The remaining transitions either make no handoff or concern an envelope already handed off. Induction over these transitions proves the property for all modeled interleavings. It proves neither physical packet suppression after R nor recipient compliance.

review.rationale: For each modeled H, eligibility is checked while policy mutation is excluded through handoff. A subsequent R blocks later forbidden H events until explicit reapproval. Non-handoff transitions cannot violate this property, giving the claimed conditional induction.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Analyze authorization–revocation–send
reasoning_steps.argument: If send means H, a successful A–R–H history is excluded: the dispatch lock prevents R from committing between A and H. A revocation invocation may occur there, but its successful acknowledgement must wait. If dispatch crashes after A without H, recovery must abandon that attempt and fence the old sender before R can commit; A cannot later be replayed. If send means physical S, A–H–R–S is allowed: transport buffering or network delay can place physical transmission or receipt after revocation. A–R–S alone therefore lacks enough information to classify a violation. The oracle must locate H. Permitting A–R–H through an outstanding token would implement a weaker grandfathered-authorization contract, which this design does not adopt.

review.rationale: The common lock excludes A–R–H, whereas buffering permits A–H–R–S. Abandonment and fencing exclude replay of authorization after a crash. Thus observing A–R–S without locating H cannot classify a violation under this contract.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Analyze revocation–authorization–send
reasoning_steps.argument: For R–A–H concerning the revoked subject/destination, A must fail while that prohibition remains effective. An earlier preliminary eligibility check is not A and cannot override R. A concurrent authorization and revocation are ordered by the lock: either dispatch completes its controlled handoff first, or revocation commits first and blocks it. An authorization begun after receipt of a successful revocation acknowledgement must observe R. An explicit later reapproval can authorize a new attempt, but neither timeout nor overload constitutes reapproval. Revocations unrelated to the request do not require rejecting it; the predicate, not epoch inequality alone, determines eligibility.

review.rationale: When R precedes final validation and the prohibition remains active, the current predicate rejects the attempt. Concurrent operations are serialized, and unrelated epoch changes need not reject an otherwise eligible envelope.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Partition behavior and the competing cached-check design
reasoning_steps.argument: In the proposed minimum, authority and controlled handoff are colocated. A partition disconnecting a worker from this service prevents new handoffs by that worker; a partition disconnecting an administrator can leave a revocation uncommitted and must not produce a success acknowledgement. If authority and an autonomous sender are separated instead, consider two histories after their link partitions: in one, the authority makes no change; in the other, it commits a revocation. The sender sees the same messages in both. Sending under a cached approval preserves service in the first history but violates latest-authority handoff policy in the second. Refusing preserves safety but loses availability. A lease changes the contract by permitting a stale interval; it does not establish immediate revocation. Physical sends of envelopes handed off before the partition remain in flight.

review.rationale: The separated sender receives identical observations in the unchanged and revoked histories, so cached dispatch cannot satisfy immediate latest-authority safety in both. Colocation changes the failure contract: disconnected clients lose admission or revocation-commit availability rather than receiving false success.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Crash, cancellation and budget integration
reasoning_steps.argument: The MAY_SEND record is written before H because a crash can otherwise erase evidence of liability. If recovery cannot determine whether H occurred, mark UNKNOWN, prohibit replay and retain the reservation. Fencing must stop the old process from later making a new H; absent confirmed fencing, neither recovery nor successful revocation acknowledgement may proceed. An already accepted transport envelope remains in flight. This sacrifices availability rather than assuming exactly-once delivery. Preserve the prior accounting invariant independently: admission tests finalized spending plus outstanding holds against each cap; final settlement replaces a hold r by charge c ≤ r; certified non-dispatch can release a hold; unknown outcomes cannot. Revocation or cancellation alone supplies no certificate of non-dispatch or zero charge.

review.rationale: Retaining uncertain holds and prohibiting replay conservatively preserve liability coverage. Fencing prevents an abandoned sender from creating a later H. The accounting inference reuses cycle 1 under its separate five premises; the current policy premises alone do not establish an invoice cap.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Define an independently observable oracle
reasoning_steps.argument: Use synthetic labeled envelopes and a security-owned test controller with separate instrumentation at the trusted transport ownership boundary and a mock destination recording received bytes and effects. The controller supplies policy changes and maintains a reference eligibility predicate; it does not infer success from router logs alone. Record attempt/content/destination bindings, A and R commit receipts, H events, fencing events and mock receipts. Establish order with barriers and acknowledgements rather than cross-host timestamps. Force pauses after preliminary checking, after A but before H, after H, and during recovery. A FAIL is an H forbidden by the reference policy in the committed order, a mutation or destination substitution, an unadmitted application retry, an unfenced old sender making H, or an acknowledgement of R followed by a new forbidden H. Receipt after R with H before R is not a safety failure. Missing capture, uncertain ordering or broken controls makes a trial inconclusive, not a pass. Include an authorized positive control to demonstrate that both sensors detect traffic.

review.rationale: Independent H instrumentation and destination observations distinguish pre-revocation handoff from forbidden post-revocation release. Causal barriers, immutable bindings, positive controls and inconclusive classifications make this a meaningful proposed oracle, not evidence that an implementation has passed.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Specify the decisive tests and deployment implication
reasoning_steps.argument: The unsafe control performs a check, releases its lock, pauses, accepts and acknowledges revocation, then hands off; the constructed history predicts a forbidden H. The proposed design, paused after A, must either complete H before R commits or abandon/fence the attempt before acknowledging R. A hung lock with no revocation acknowledgement is a liveness failure, not proof of safety or a successful revocation. Test partitions, stale workers, malicious redirects, payload mutation, simultaneous quota claims, cancellation and crash-after-handoff. In the 90-day pilot, days 1–30 assign security the boundary/contract approval and computing the instrumentation; days 31–60 run these controlled fault histories; days 61–90 measure revocation-ack latency, refusal rate, recovery time and useful completion under the agreed load. Any forbidden H stops the pilot; incomplete instrumentation blocks a go decision. Campus-local, API-only and gateway-plus-separately-approved-API services can share this campus gate. Federation adds remote enforcement and recipient obligations without eliminating the ordering constraint. Baseline 3 remains the simpler design candidate unless measured authorized pooling benefits justify those additions; no comparative winner is established.

review.rationale: The paused unsafe control permits check–R–H, while the serialized design must order H before R or abandon the attempt. Separating hung-lock liveness failure from safety is correct. The pilot stages and baseline-3 preference are explicitly proposals, with no measured winner asserted.

The binding covers prompts and approved handling of outputs, logs, caches, embeddings and telemetry; it does not establish that a recipient actually honors those obligations.

review.rationale: The frozen envelope and explicit eligibility predicate prevent authorization from being transferred to changed content or destinations within the model. Fail-closed classification and separate recipient-compliance limitations are consistent with the project requirements.

argument_steps.title: 4. Give the minimal dispatch transition
argument_steps.argument: From READY, obtain the required durable budget holds, then acquire the policy/egress lock. Re-evaluate eligibility against the authoritative current epoch. On failure, enter BLOCKED without handoff. On success, durably record MAY_SEND with the frozen envelope and epoch; this commit is A, the authorization linearization point. While still holding the lock, perform one nonblocking H into the trusted transport and record IN_FLIGHT if acknowledged. Only then release the lock. Transport admission must accept ownership of one bounded immutable envelope, not an unbounded workflow or future mutable stream. READY jobs are not preauthorized while waiting in scheduling queues. If the handoff outcome is uncertain, enter UNKNOWN, not retryable READY. No delayed worker may later exercise A independently.

review.rationale: Holding the common lock from final validation through A and H prevents intervening policy mutation. UNKNOWN and the prohibition on delayed independent exercise of A avoid treating uncertain handoff as reusable authority. This depends on the stated transport-ownership and recovery premises.

argument_steps.title: 5. Give revocation and the in-flight contract
argument_steps.argument: A revocation acquires the same lock, durably increments the epoch and changes the eligibility predicate; that commit is R. Acknowledge success only after R. Thus a revocation arriving while dispatch holds the lock remains pending until that handoff finishes or is abandoned. Existing queued requests must pass the new predicate. Requests already handed off may finish their single frozen envelope and return results only through approved handling paths. Cancellation and remote deletion are best-effort requests unless stronger inspected contracts exist. They are not recall guarantees. Every new agent call, tool call, redirect, content-bearing reconnection or fallback must re-enter admission. Transport retransmission of already accepted bytes is part of the original in-flight transfer; a new independently chargeable application attempt is not.

review.rationale: R uses the same serialization mechanism, so pending revocation cannot be mistaken for committed revocation. The single-envelope in-flight exception and fresh admission for new application actions preserve the specified boundary without promising recall.

argument_steps.title: 6. Prove the new-handoff safety property
argument_steps.argument: Initially there are no authorized attempts or handed-off envelopes. For any H, the dispatch transition requires a preceding A under the lock, with eligibility true in epoch e. No R can occur between that validation and H because R requires the same lock. Consequently policy at H still authorizes that exact envelope. After an R withdrawing its eligibility, a later dispatch sees the changed predicate and cannot reach H unless a subsequent explicit policy change authorizes it again. The remaining transitions either make no handoff or concern an envelope already handed off. Induction over these transitions proves the property for all modeled interleavings. It proves neither physical packet suppression after R nor recipient compliance.

review.rationale: For each modeled H, eligibility is checked while policy mutation is excluded through handoff. A subsequent R blocks later forbidden H events until explicit reapproval. Non-handoff transitions cannot violate this property, giving the claimed conditional induction.

argument_steps.title: 7. Analyze authorization–revocation–send
argument_steps.argument: If send means H, a successful A–R–H history is excluded: the dispatch lock prevents R from committing between A and H. A revocation invocation may occur there, but its successful acknowledgement must wait. If dispatch crashes after A without H, recovery must abandon that attempt and fence the old sender before R can commit; A cannot later be replayed. If send means physical S, A–H–R–S is allowed: transport buffering or network delay can place physical transmission or receipt after revocation. A–R–S alone therefore lacks enough information to classify a violation. The oracle must locate H. Permitting A–R–H through an outstanding token would implement a weaker grandfathered-authorization contract, which this design does not adopt.

review.rationale: The common lock excludes A–R–H, whereas buffering permits A–H–R–S. Abandonment and fencing exclude replay of authorization after a crash. Thus observing A–R–S without locating H cannot classify a violation under this contract.

argument_steps.title: 8. Analyze revocation–authorization–send
argument_steps.argument: For R–A–H concerning the revoked subject/destination, A must fail while that prohibition remains effective. An earlier preliminary eligibility check is not A and cannot override R. A concurrent authorization and revocation are ordered by the lock: either dispatch completes its controlled handoff first, or revocation commits first and blocks it. An authorization begun after receipt of a successful revocation acknowledgement must observe R. An explicit later reapproval can authorize a new attempt, but neither timeout nor overload constitutes reapproval. Revocations unrelated to the request do not require rejecting it; the predicate, not epoch inequality alone, determines eligibility.

review.rationale: When R precedes final validation and the prohibition remains active, the current predicate rejects the attempt. Concurrent operations are serialized, and unrelated epoch changes need not reject an otherwise eligible envelope.

argument_steps.title: 9. Partition behavior and the competing cached-check design
argument_steps.argument: In the proposed minimum, authority and controlled handoff are colocated. A partition disconnecting a worker from this service prevents new handoffs by that worker; a partition disconnecting an administrator can leave a revocation uncommitted and must not produce a success acknowledgement. If authority and an autonomous sender are separated instead, consider two histories after their link partitions: in one, the authority makes no change; in the other, it commits a revocation. The sender sees the same messages in both. Sending under a cached approval preserves service in the first history but violates latest-authority handoff policy in the second. Refusing preserves safety but loses availability. A lease changes the contract by permitting a stale interval; it does not establish immediate revocation. Physical sends of envelopes handed off before the partition remain in flight.

review.rationale: The separated sender receives identical observations in the unchanged and revoked histories, so cached dispatch cannot satisfy immediate latest-authority safety in both. Colocation changes the failure contract: disconnected clients lose admission or revocation-commit availability rather than receiving false success.

argument_steps.title: 10. Crash, cancellation and budget integration
argument_steps.argument: The MAY_SEND record is written before H because a crash can otherwise erase evidence of liability. If recovery cannot determine whether H occurred, mark UNKNOWN, prohibit replay and retain the reservation. Fencing must stop the old process from later making a new H; absent confirmed fencing, neither recovery nor successful revocation acknowledgement may proceed. An already accepted transport envelope remains in flight. This sacrifices availability rather than assuming exactly-once delivery. Preserve the prior accounting invariant independently: admission tests finalized spending plus outstanding holds against each cap; final settlement replaces a hold r by charge c ≤ r; certified non-dispatch can release a hold; unknown outcomes cannot. Revocation or cancellation alone supplies no certificate of non-dispatch or zero charge.

review.rationale: Retaining uncertain holds and prohibiting replay conservatively preserve liability coverage. Fencing prevents an abandoned sender from creating a later H. The accounting inference reuses cycle 1 under its separate five premises; the current policy premises alone do not establish an invoice cap.

argument_steps.title: 11. Define an independently observable oracle
argument_steps.argument: Use synthetic labeled envelopes and a security-owned test controller with separate instrumentation at the trusted transport ownership boundary and a mock destination recording received bytes and effects. The controller supplies policy changes and maintains a reference eligibility predicate; it does not infer success from router logs alone. Record attempt/content/destination bindings, A and R commit receipts, H events, fencing events and mock receipts. Establish order with barriers and acknowledgements rather than cross-host timestamps. Force pauses after preliminary checking, after A but before H, after H, and during recovery. A FAIL is an H forbidden by the reference policy in the committed order, a mutation or destination substitution, an unadmitted application retry, an unfenced old sender making H, or an acknowledgement of R followed by a new forbidden H. Receipt after R with H before R is not a safety failure. Missing capture, uncertain ordering or broken controls makes a trial inconclusive, not a pass. Include an authorized positive control to demonstrate that both sensors detect traffic.

review.rationale: Independent H instrumentation and destination observations distinguish pre-revocation handoff from forbidden post-revocation release. Causal barriers, immutable bindings, positive controls and inconclusive classifications make this a meaningful proposed oracle, not evidence that an implementation has passed.

argument_steps.title: 12. Specify the decisive tests and deployment implication
argument_steps.argument: The unsafe control performs a check, releases its lock, pauses, accepts and acknowledges revocation, then hands off; the constructed history predicts a forbidden H. The proposed design, paused after A, must either complete H before R commits or abandon/fence the attempt before acknowledging R. A hung lock with no revocation acknowledgement is a liveness failure, not proof of safety or a successful revocation. Test partitions, stale workers, malicious redirects, payload mutation, simultaneous quota claims, cancellation and crash-after-handoff. In the 90-day pilot, days 1–30 assign security the boundary/contract approval and computing the instrumentation; days 31–60 run these controlled fault histories; days 61–90 measure revocation-ack latency, refusal rate, recovery time and useful completion under the agreed load. Any forbidden H stops the pilot; incomplete instrumentation blocks a go decision. Campus-local, API-only and gateway-plus-separately-approved-API services can share this campus gate. Federation adds remote enforcement and recipient obligations without eliminating the ordering constraint. Baseline 3 remains the simpler design candidate unless measured authorized pooling benefits justify those additions; no comparative winner is established.

review.rationale: The paused unsafe control permits check–R–H, while the serialized design must order H before R or abandon the attempt. Separating hung-lock liveness failure from safety is correct. The pilot stages and baseline-3 preference are explicitly proposals, with no measured winner asserted.

artifacts.skeptic_response:
The statistical design makes substantial progress on the current question. Its offered-demand denominator, paired comparison, fixed-sample Hoeffding bounds, multiplicity allocation and distinction between safety-stop, no-go and inconclusive are sound under the stated independence assumptions. The sample-size arithmetic checks analytically. No computation or pilot was executed.

One material economic inference needs correction. Conservative upper liability estimates cannot simply replace both services’ actual costs in the contrast K: baseline cost enters with a negative coefficient, so overestimating it can falsely favor federation. For example, let every episode succeed, actual costs equal 1 for both services, federation’s cost be settled at 1, and baseline’s unresolved charge have an upper bound of 2 and a known lower bound of 1. Substituting upper bounds gives K=−0.60 although the actual cost-per-useful-task ratio is 1, not at most 0.80. At N=30,000 identical independent pairs, the proposed completion and noninferiority bounds pass, and the substituted-cost upper confidence bound is approximately −0.566. Thus sampling uncertainty can vanish while settlement uncertainty still produces a false economic conclusion. This refutes that substitution, not the fixed-cost statistical theorem or federation generally.

A direct repair is available without execution. Record charge intervals [l_si,u_si]. In the two-task product, an upper bound on actual K uses federation upper costs and baseline lower costs; a lower bound uses federation lower costs and baseline upper costs. Apply one upper-tail bound to the upper contrast and one lower-tail bound to the lower contrast. Together with the six existing probability/coverage tails, eight tails at 0.00625 each retain the same log(160) allocation and 5% union bound. Economic go uses the upper contrast’s upper confidence endpoint; economic exclusion uses the lower contrast’s lower endpoint. Alternatively, require settled costs for both services and otherwise leave economics inconclusive.

A second important feasibility qualification is that the economic pathway’s proposed −2-point noninferiority safeguard can dominate the advertised sample sizes. With observed paired difference zero, its current Hoeffding rule needs at least ceil(2 log(160)/0.02²)=25,376 independent pairs merely to make its lower endpoint reach −0.02. The 1,646-pair normalized cost example alone therefore cannot support economic go. This is a planning constraint, not evidence that an actual 90-day pilot is infeasible.

The cycle-2 handoff model remains a conditional reference design, not deployment evidence. Its analytical ordering result need not be rewritten. Publications, dated prices, actual campus approvals, independent sampling feasibility, implementation tests and four-baseline measurements remain outstanding. The brief’s 2026-10-31 review date is not an access date established by this review.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Fix the estimand before admissions or routing
reasoning_steps.argument: Define the target population as legitimate research task episodes offered by authenticated pilot users under a prespecified campus/task/load distribution. An episode is one requested useful deliverable, not one model call: an agent workflow and a reproducible batch each retain one episode identifier through all calls, retries and terminal outcomes. Sample episodes before either service admits them. Let B denote baseline 3 and F the hypothetical federation extension, with the same external-access approvals and budget scenario. Baselines 1 and 2 use the same episode definitions, but selecting a winner among all four would require an additional multiplicity plan. The confirmatory comparison here is only F versus B.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Count refusals without rewarding unsafe behavior
reasoning_steps.argument: For service s and sampled episode i, set Y_si=1 only if the requested deliverable meets the frozen task-quality rubric, finishes within its task-specific end-to-end deadline, supplies required provenance/version information, and follows approved handling rules. Otherwise set Y_si=0. The denominator N includes policy refusals, ambiguous-classification refusals, no-fit jobs, budget exhaustion, overload, outage, provider rejection, deadline expiry, cancellation after enrollment and missing quality adjudication. An appropriate refusal is a safety success but not a useful completion. A late result remains a completion failure. Retries never create new denominator entries. Exclude malformed/nonresearch traffic only through prespecified, outcome-blind eligibility rules; malicious synthetic probes belong in a separate safety suite. Report refusal reasons and both offered-demand and admitted-only rates, but do not substitute the admitted-only rate for the primary outcome.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Separate demand coverage from positive-control safety tests
reasoning_steps.argument: Use p_s=E[Y_si] as useful-completion coverage of offered legitimate demand. Restricted or ambiguous legitimate requests remain represented even when refusal is mandatory; this reveals that a service may be safe yet unable to cover the campus’s needs. Report externally eligible and local-only strata as secondary diagnostics rather than redefining the primary denominator after observing results. Synthetic forbidden-egress tests have no legitimate deliverable and are not mixed into p_s. A counterexample to admitted-only reporting is a service that completes 10 easy tasks and refuses 90 difficult ones: admitted completion is 100%, but offered-demand useful completion is 10%. Neither denominator licenses relaxing policy.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Specify the sampling assumptions and pairing controls
reasoning_steps.argument: For the finite-sample bounds below, the N paired vectors must be independent and identically distributed draws from the prespecified target mixture. Each vector contains B and F outcomes for the same task and comparable load condition; dependence within a pair is allowed. Use authorized task copies, blinded assessors and randomized execution order, with isolated/reset budget and queue state where replay is valid. Do not duplicate sensitive work to an unapproved destination merely to form a pair. Shared queues, monthly budget depletion and repeated tasks from the same researcher generally violate episode-level independence. In those cases use independent reset load blocks as sampling units, with a fixed number of enrolled tasks per block, or design a cluster/randomized-period analysis before collection. Bounds on block averages remain valid, but N then means independent blocks, not calls or tasks. Unavailable independent replication makes inference inconclusive rather than permitting an invented effective sample size.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Define costs at a common service scale
reasoning_steps.argument: Let c_si be nonnegative cost per offered episode at a declared common annual demand and accounting perspective. Include costs of failed episodes, all billable subcalls and permitted retries, idle capacity, staffing and federation administration. Allocate fixed annual costs over the declared annual offered demand, not over observed successes; keep sunk, incremental and fully loaded analyses separate. Define mu_s=E[c_si], and cost per useful task q_s=mu_s/p_s for p_s>0. The primary economic comparison uses fully loaded cost; repeat incremental analysis as a sensitivity, not a replacement. Cost certification below additionally requires enforceable bounds 0≤c_si≤M_s, settled charges or conservative liability bounds, and a known positive baseline cost floor. Unknown fixed allocations require declared uncertainty ranges; an economic go must survive their approved adverse values. An unsettled charged timeout is not zero cost. No prices, costs or workload observations are supplied here.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Construct the paired coverage and economic contrasts
reasoning_steps.argument: Let D_i=Y_Fi−Y_Bi, so D_i lies in [−1,1] and Delta=E[D_i]=p_F−p_B. The coverage hurdle is Delta≥0.10. For the economic hurdle q_F/q_B≤0.80, positive denominators give the equivalent inequality K=mu_F p_B−0.80 mu_B p_F≤0. A mean of per-episode cost/success ratios is undefined on failures and is not this estimand. To estimate K without assuming cost and success are independent within a task, partition the N independent pairs into m=floor(N/2) disjoint two-task blocks (i,j), fixed before outcomes. Define Z=(c_Fi Y_Bj+c_Fj Y_Bi−0.80 c_Bi Y_Fj−0.80 c_Bj Y_Fi)/2. Cross-task independence gives E[Z]=K, while arbitrary within-task dependence is retained. Each Z lies in [−0.80 M_B,M_F], and disjoint blocks are independent. Using only these disjoint products sacrifices precision but makes a finite-sample paired rule transparent.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Give one simultaneous confidence rule
reasoning_steps.argument: Use one fixed final analysis with family error alpha=0.05. Form two-sided intervals for four quantities: p_F, p_B, Delta and K. Hoeffding’s bounded-variable inequality gives P(|mean−expectation|>w sqrt(log(160)/(2n)))≤0.0125 for range width w, since 2 exp(−2n r²/w²)=0.0125. A union bound therefore gives simultaneous coverage at least 95%, without independence among the four intervals. Write a=sqrt(log(160)/(2N)). The intervals are p_s: mean(Y_s)±a; Delta: mean(D)±2a; K: mean(Z)±(M_F+0.80M_B)sqrt(log(160)/(2m)). Clip probability intervals to [0,1] and the Delta interval to [−1,1]. Denote endpoints L and U. This is deliberately conservative, distribution-free under the listed assumptions, and valid for the prespecified OR between the two benefit pathways.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. State the provisional statistical go rule
reasoning_steps.argument: After all nonstatistical gates pass, require L_pF≥0.90 and either (A) L_Delta≥0.10, or (B) U_K≤0 together with L_Delta≥−0.02. The −2-point completion noninferiority margin is an additional provisional safeguard: lower cost must not hide a materially less useful service. Path B also requires L_pB>0 and a known positive mu_B, so the baseline cost-per-useful-task ratio is meaningful. On the simultaneous-coverage event, each certified inequality holds for its population parameter. Thus a statistical go with any false required parameter inequality can occur only outside that event, with probability at most 5%. This controls statistical false-go risk, not policy, contract, implementation or safety risk. At an exact hurdle, high probability of certification should not be expected; power requires a real margin beyond it.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Derive completion and paired-coverage sample requirements
reasoning_steps.argument: For completion half-width h, N≥ceil(log(160)/(2h²)): h=0.05 requires 1,016 independent pairs and h=0.03 requires 2,820. For paired Delta half-width h, its range width is 2, so N≥ceil(2 log(160)/h²): h=0.05 requires 4,061 pairs. At N=3,000 the completion half-width is approximately 0.0291 and the Delta half-width approximately 0.0582; certification therefore requires observed F completion at least about 92.91% and observed advantage at least about 15.82 points. These are analytical requirements, not measured rates. The ceiling matters: if B truly exceeds 90% completion, F cannot improve it by 10 points; if B is exactly 90%, that pathway requires perfect population completion. Cost improvement may therefore be the relevant pathway for an already effective baseline.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Distinguish precision from power and expose cost sensitivity
reasoning_steps.argument: For a bounded mean with range width w, a true favorable margin g beyond its hurdle is certified with probability at least 1−beta if N≥w²[ sqrt(log(160)/2)+sqrt(log(1/beta)/2) ]²/g². This follows by adding the confidence radius to the one-sided Hoeffding sampling deviation. With beta=0.20, true p_F=0.95 versus the 0.90 hurdle is certifiable with at least 80% probability at N=2,500; true Delta=0.15 versus 0.10 requires N=10,000 under this conservative bound. These are individual-gate power guarantees, not joint pilot power. For K precision e, require m≥ceil((M_F+0.80M_B)² log(160)/(2e²)). If both cost bounds equal M, half-width 0.10M needs 823 independent two-task blocks, or 1,646 task pairs; half-width 0.02M needs 20,555 blocks, or 41,110 pairs. This is normalized sensitivity, not a dollar scenario. A rare expensive tail can make cost certification impractical in 90 days. Moreover K=(R−0.80)mu_B p_F for R=q_F/q_B, so a 20% saving exactly at R=0.80 supplies no favorable margin at all.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Distinguish safety-stop, no-go and inconclusive
reasoning_steps.argument: Safety-stop: immediately suspend affected routing on a confirmed forbidden controlled handoff, unauthorized derived-artifact disclosure, unreserved paid attempt or verified cap breach; investigate rather than average the incident into a success rate. Missing safety instrumentation blocks go but is not evidence of a breach. Statistical no-go: U_pF<0.90, or both benefit pathways are ruled out—U_Delta<0.10 and either L_K>0 or U_Delta<−0.02. A definite campus contract/security veto or infeasible funding is an administrative no-go, separately labeled. Inconclusive: bounds overlap a required hurdle, sample assumptions fail, evidence is missing, or neither a go nor a no-go condition holds. Failure to reject a hurdle is not evidence that it was met. No paid trial runs after budget exhaustion; resulting service refusals stay in the enrolled denominator. A pilot stopped for safety has no deployment go regardless of favorable completion estimates.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Make the 90-day collection plan executable without optional stopping
reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: security owns approved domains and fault-test oracles; computing owns load blocks, queues, hardware-fit and independent egress instrumentation; procurement/finance owns liability bounds and cost allocations; faculty and student representatives own task rubrics, deadlines and blinded adjudication; an evaluation lead freezes sampling, N, analysis and exclusions. Include coding, routine analysis, scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context, agentic, sensitive and reproducible-batch strata, with peak, cold-start and maintenance conditions. Days 31–60: run synthetic safety/fault tests and estimate variance/dependence using a development set excluded from confirmatory analysis. Days 61–90: collect the frozen confirmatory sample under approved hard caps, then analyze once after every episode’s deadline and the declared billing-reconciliation cutoff. Safety monitoring is continuous, but favorable interim estimates do not permit early statistical go. Insufficient independent units by day 90 means inconclusive; extension needs a fresh approved plan or a prespecified sequential method. If the budget cannot support four service executions per episode, prioritize the B–F paired comparison and clearly label reduced descriptive coverage of baselines 1 and 2.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Preserve autonomy, fairness and evidence limitations
reasoning_steps.argument: Overall mixture success cannot certify each campus, task class or protected queue. Report campus/task/load-stratum completion, refusal reasons, queue-deadline misses, starvation, throughput, availability, provenance completeness, staff hours and cost attribution. A deployment rule requiring a separate completion floor for every campus needs additional simultaneous intervals and enough independent units per campus; the pooled sample counts above do not establish that. Governance must approve those floors and interactive/batch shares before deployment. Retain the earlier negative constraints: separated check-then-send is not current-policy handoff enforcement, and releasing an unresolved timeout hold can permit overspending. The supplied cycle-2 extract describes conditional models, not implementation evidence; o411 remains recorded as addressed analytically, while its contract and operational duties and the other unresolved ledger entries stay open. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions. The brief attributes protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, logging and telemetry to the published campus MindRouter gateway; current source verification, comparative usefulness and deployment readiness are not established here.
