reasoning_steps.title: 1. Fix the estimand before admissions or routing
reasoning_steps.argument: Define the target population as legitimate research task episodes offered by authenticated pilot users under a prespecified campus/task/load distribution. An episode is one requested useful deliverable, not one model call: an agent workflow and a reproducible batch each retain one episode identifier through all calls, retries and terminal outcomes. Sample episodes before either service admits them. Let B denote baseline 3 and F the hypothetical federation extension, with the same external-access approvals and budget scenario. Baselines 1 and 2 use the same episode definitions, but selecting a winner among all four would require an additional multiplicity plan. The confirmatory comparison here is only F versus B.

review.rationale: Sampling before service admission fixes a common offered-demand population and prevents service-specific selection from defining the estimand. Restricting confirmation to F versus baseline 3 correctly avoids claiming a four-way winner under a two-service multiplicity plan.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Count refusals without rewarding unsafe behavior
reasoning_steps.argument: For service s and sampled episode i, set Y_si=1 only if the requested deliverable meets the frozen task-quality rubric, finishes within its task-specific end-to-end deadline, supplies required provenance/version information, and follows approved handling rules. Otherwise set Y_si=0. The denominator N includes policy refusals, ambiguous-classification refusals, no-fit jobs, budget exhaustion, overload, outage, provider rejection, deadline expiry, cancellation after enrollment and missing quality adjudication. An appropriate refusal is a safety success but not a useful completion. A late result remains a completion failure. Retries never create new denominator entries. Exclude malformed/nonresearch traffic only through prespecified, outcome-blind eligibility rules; malicious synthetic probes belong in a separate safety suite. Report refusal reasons and both offered-demand and admitted-only rates, but do not substitute the admitted-only rate for the primary outcome.

review.rationale: The binary outcome requires quality, deadline, provenance and approved handling jointly. Retaining refusals, failures, enrolled cancellations and missing adjudication in the denominator prevents admission filtering and retries from inflating useful completion.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Separate demand coverage from positive-control safety tests
reasoning_steps.argument: Use p_s=E[Y_si] as useful-completion coverage of offered legitimate demand. Restricted or ambiguous legitimate requests remain represented even when refusal is mandatory; this reveals that a service may be safe yet unable to cover the campus’s needs. Report externally eligible and local-only strata as secondary diagnostics rather than redefining the primary denominator after observing results. Synthetic forbidden-egress tests have no legitimate deliverable and are not mixed into p_s. A counterexample to admitted-only reporting is a service that completes 10 easy tasks and refuses 90 difficult ones: admitted completion is 100%, but offered-demand useful completion is 10%. Neither denominator licenses relaxing policy.

review.rationale: The explicit 10-success/90-refusal example independently establishes the difference between admitted-only performance and offered-demand coverage. Separating forbidden-egress probes from legitimate deliverables avoids conflating safety testing with service usefulness.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Specify the sampling assumptions and pairing controls
reasoning_steps.argument: For the finite-sample bounds below, the N paired vectors must be independent and identically distributed draws from the prespecified target mixture. Each vector contains B and F outcomes for the same task and comparable load condition; dependence within a pair is allowed. Use authorized task copies, blinded assessors and randomized execution order, with isolated/reset budget and queue state where replay is valid. Do not duplicate sensitive work to an unapproved destination merely to form a pair. Shared queues, monthly budget depletion and repeated tasks from the same researcher generally violate episode-level independence. In those cases use independent reset load blocks as sampling units, with a fixed number of enrolled tasks per block, or design a cluster/randomized-period analysis before collection. Bounds on block averages remain valid, but N then means independent blocks, not calls or tasks. Unavailable independent replication makes inference inconclusive rather than permitting an invented effective sample size.

review.rationale: Accepted only as the explicitly conditional sampling premise. Within-pair dependence is compatible with independent paired vectors; genuinely independent fixed-size block averages are also bounded variables. The step correctly excludes ordinary shared-state episodes from an unsupported independence claim.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Define costs at a common service scale
reasoning_steps.argument: Let c_si be nonnegative cost per offered episode at a declared common annual demand and accounting perspective. Include costs of failed episodes, all billable subcalls and permitted retries, idle capacity, staffing and federation administration. Allocate fixed annual costs over the declared annual offered demand, not over observed successes; keep sunk, incremental and fully loaded analyses separate. Define mu_s=E[c_si], and cost per useful task q_s=mu_s/p_s for p_s>0. The primary economic comparison uses fully loaded cost; repeat incremental analysis as a sensitivity, not a replacement. Cost certification below additionally requires enforceable bounds 0≤c_si≤M_s, settled charges or conservative liability bounds, and a known positive baseline cost floor. Unknown fixed allocations require declared uncertainty ranges; an economic go must survive their approved adverse values. An unsettled charged timeout is not zero cost. No prices, costs or workload observations are supplied here.

review.rationale: The common-demand cost allocation and ratio-of-means estimand are coherent for actual costs. The alternative allowing conservative liability bounds is insufficiently specified to support certification of actual economic cost.
review.objection: Upper bounds on baseline costs are not conservative when those costs later enter the economic contrast negatively. Require settled costs, a clearly labeled liability-surrogate estimand, or signed propagation of lower and upper cost bounds.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Construct the paired coverage and economic contrasts
reasoning_steps.argument: Let D_i=Y_Fi−Y_Bi, so D_i lies in [−1,1] and Delta=E[D_i]=p_F−p_B. The coverage hurdle is Delta≥0.10. For the economic hurdle q_F/q_B≤0.80, positive denominators give the equivalent inequality K=mu_F p_B−0.80 mu_B p_F≤0. A mean of per-episode cost/success ratios is undefined on failures and is not this estimand. To estimate K without assuming cost and success are independent within a task, partition the N independent pairs into m=floor(N/2) disjoint two-task blocks (i,j), fixed before outcomes. Define Z=(c_Fi Y_Bj+c_Fj Y_Bi−0.80 c_Bi Y_Fj−0.80 c_Bj Y_Fi)/2. Cross-task independence gives E[Z]=K, while arbitrary within-task dependence is retained. Each Z lies in [−0.80 M_B,M_F], and disjoint blocks are independent. Using only these disjoint products sacrifices precision but makes a finite-sample paired rule transparent.

review.rationale: For exact costs and positive denominators, multiplying q_F/q_B≤0.80 gives the stated K inequality. Cross-task independence makes each product’s expectation a product of means without requiring within-task independence. Averaging two terms preserves the stated range, and disjoint task blocks preserve independence.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Give one simultaneous confidence rule
reasoning_steps.argument: Use one fixed final analysis with family error alpha=0.05. Form two-sided intervals for four quantities: p_F, p_B, Delta and K. Hoeffding’s bounded-variable inequality gives P(|mean−expectation|>w sqrt(log(160)/(2n)))≤0.0125 for range width w, since 2 exp(−2n r²/w²)=0.0125. A union bound therefore gives simultaneous coverage at least 95%, without independence among the four intervals. Write a=sqrt(log(160)/(2N)). The intervals are p_s: mean(Y_s)±a; Delta: mean(D)±2a; K: mean(Z)±(M_F+0.80M_B)sqrt(log(160)/(2m)). Clip probability intervals to [0,1] and the Delta interval to [−1,1]. Denote endpoints L and U. This is deliberately conservative, distribution-free under the listed assumptions, and valid for the prespecified OR between the two benefit pathways.

review.rationale: For each exact bounded mean, the radius gives two-tail error 2 exp(−log(160))=0.0125. Four such errors sum to 0.05, regardless of dependence among intervals. Probability and difference clipping do not reduce coverage.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. State the provisional statistical go rule
reasoning_steps.argument: After all nonstatistical gates pass, require L_pF≥0.90 and either (A) L_Delta≥0.10, or (B) U_K≤0 together with L_Delta≥−0.02. The −2-point completion noninferiority margin is an additional provisional safeguard: lower cost must not hide a materially less useful service. Path B also requires L_pB>0 and a known positive mu_B, so the baseline cost-per-useful-task ratio is meaningful. On the simultaneous-coverage event, each certified inequality holds for its population parameter. Thus a statistical go with any false required parameter inequality can occur only outside that event, with probability at most 5%. This controls statistical false-go risk, not policy, contract, implementation or safety risk. At an exact hurdle, high probability of certification should not be expected; power requires a real margin beyond it.

review.rationale: The simultaneous-event argument correctly controls false certification for exact-cost K and the probability inequalities, including the prespecified OR. It does not cover the settlement bias permitted in step 5.
review.objection: The blanket false-go claim must exclude replacing both services’ actual costs with upper liability estimates. Equal actual costs can then pass the economic pathway with probability one at sufficiently large N; confidence coverage for the surrogate does not establish coverage for actual K.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Derive completion and paired-coverage sample requirements
reasoning_steps.argument: For completion half-width h, N≥ceil(log(160)/(2h²)): h=0.05 requires 1,016 independent pairs and h=0.03 requires 2,820. For paired Delta half-width h, its range width is 2, so N≥ceil(2 log(160)/h²): h=0.05 requires 4,061 pairs. At N=3,000 the completion half-width is approximately 0.0291 and the Delta half-width approximately 0.0582; certification therefore requires observed F completion at least about 92.91% and observed advantage at least about 15.82 points. These are analytical requirements, not measured rates. The ceiling matters: if B truly exceeds 90% completion, F cannot improve it by 10 points; if B is exactly 90%, that pathway requires perfect population completion. Cost improvement may therefore be the relevant pathway for an already effective baseline.

review.rationale: Solving the stated radii for N gives the reported ceilings 1,016, 2,820 and 4,061. The N=3,000 radii and certification thresholds agree with those formulas. The population ceiling p_F≤1 establishes the stated limitation of the 10-point advantage pathway.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Distinguish precision from power and expose cost sensitivity
reasoning_steps.argument: For a bounded mean with range width w, a true favorable margin g beyond its hurdle is certified with probability at least 1−beta if N≥w²[ sqrt(log(160)/2)+sqrt(log(1/beta)/2) ]²/g². This follows by adding the confidence radius to the one-sided Hoeffding sampling deviation. With beta=0.20, true p_F=0.95 versus the 0.90 hurdle is certifiable with at least 80% probability at N=2,500; true Delta=0.15 versus 0.10 requires N=10,000 under this conservative bound. These are individual-gate power guarantees, not joint pilot power. For K precision e, require m≥ceil((M_F+0.80M_B)² log(160)/(2e²)). If both cost bounds equal M, half-width 0.10M needs 823 independent two-task blocks, or 1,646 task pairs; half-width 0.02M needs 20,555 blocks, or 41,110 pairs. This is normalized sensitivity, not a dollar scenario. A rare expensive tail can make cost certification impractical in 90 days. Moreover K=(R−0.80)mu_B p_F for R=q_F/q_B, so a 20% saving exactly at R=0.80 supplies no favorable margin at all.

review.rationale: Adding the confidence radius to a one-sided Hoeffding deviation yields the stated individual-gate power bound. The conservative rounded counts and normalized cost-precision counts satisfy their formulas, and K=(R−0.80)mu_B p_F follows algebraically.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Distinguish safety-stop, no-go and inconclusive
reasoning_steps.argument: Safety-stop: immediately suspend affected routing on a confirmed forbidden controlled handoff, unauthorized derived-artifact disclosure, unreserved paid attempt or verified cap breach; investigate rather than average the incident into a success rate. Missing safety instrumentation blocks go but is not evidence of a breach. Statistical no-go: U_pF<0.90, or both benefit pathways are ruled out—U_Delta<0.10 and either L_K>0 or U_Delta<−0.02. A definite campus contract/security veto or infeasible funding is an administrative no-go, separately labeled. Inconclusive: bounds overlap a required hurdle, sample assumptions fail, evidence is missing, or neither a go nor a no-go condition holds. Failure to reject a hurdle is not evidence that it was met. No paid trial runs after budget exhaustion; resulting service refusals stay in the enrolled denominator. A pilot stopped for safety has no deployment go regardless of favorable completion estimates.

review.rationale: Safety-stop, missing-instrumentation and inconclusive classifications are appropriately separated. For exact K, the no-go Boolean expression is the complement of the two benefit pathways on the simultaneous-coverage event.
review.objection: Economic no-go also needs signed settlement uncertainty: overestimated federation costs can spuriously make L_K positive. Apply a lower confidence bound to a valid lower contrast for actual K, not a contrast containing arbitrary upper cost estimates.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Make the 90-day collection plan executable without optional stopping
reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: security owns approved domains and fault-test oracles; computing owns load blocks, queues, hardware-fit and independent egress instrumentation; procurement/finance owns liability bounds and cost allocations; faculty and student representatives own task rubrics, deadlines and blinded adjudication; an evaluation lead freezes sampling, N, analysis and exclusions. Include coding, routine analysis, scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context, agentic, sensitive and reproducible-batch strata, with peak, cold-start and maintenance conditions. Days 31–60: run synthetic safety/fault tests and estimate variance/dependence using a development set excluded from confirmatory analysis. Days 61–90: collect the frozen confirmatory sample under approved hard caps, then analyze once after every episode’s deadline and the declared billing-reconciliation cutoff. Safety monitoring is continuous, but favorable interim estimates do not permit early statistical go. Insufficient independent units by day 90 means inconclusive; extension needs a fresh approved plan or a prespecified sequential method. If the budget cannot support four service executions per episode, prioritize the B–F paired comparison and clearly label reduced descriptive coverage of baselines 1 and 2.

review.rationale: The proposed development/confirmation split, frozen final analysis and prohibition on favorable interim stopping are compatible with the fixed-sample guarantee. Independent-unit and budget shortfalls are explicitly classified as inconclusive rather than quietly reducing the sample or escalating spending.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Preserve autonomy, fairness and evidence limitations
reasoning_steps.argument: Overall mixture success cannot certify each campus, task class or protected queue. Report campus/task/load-stratum completion, refusal reasons, queue-deadline misses, starvation, throughput, availability, provenance completeness, staff hours and cost attribution. A deployment rule requiring a separate completion floor for every campus needs additional simultaneous intervals and enough independent units per campus; the pooled sample counts above do not establish that. Governance must approve those floors and interactive/batch shares before deployment. Retain the earlier negative constraints: separated check-then-send is not current-policy handoff enforcement, and releasing an unresolved timeout hold can permit overspending. The supplied cycle-2 extract describes conditional models, not implementation evidence; o411 remains recorded as addressed analytically, while its contract and operational duties and the other unresolved ledger entries stay open. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions. The brief attributes protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, logging and telemetry to the published campus MindRouter gateway; current source verification, comparative usefulness and deployment readiness are not established here.

review.rationale: A pooled mixture mean cannot entail campus- or stratum-specific floors; additional simultaneous inference is correctly required. The step preserves conditional safety constraints and distinguishes brief-attributed MindRouter descriptions from inspected sources and hypothetical extensions.

objective_review.claim: Conditional on: For the statistical guarantee, paired episode vectors are independent identically distributed draws from a prespecified target task/load mixture, or the analysis uses genuinely independent fixed-size reset blocks as its units; Outcomes, episode enrollment, deadlines, rubrics, multiplicity allocation and the final sample size are fixed before confirmatory outcomes are inspected; missing adjudication counts as failure and favorable optional stopping is prohibited; For economic certification only, all covered costs use a common declared demand scale, nonnegative enforceable bounds M_F and M_B, conservative treatment of unresolved liability, approved fixed-cost allocations and a known positive baseline mean cost; Both service variants can be evaluated within approved domains without unsafe replication or interference invalidating their paired comparison; The proposed numerical gates are adopted only as provisional pilot decision criteria; they are not asserted to be existing university policy or accepted deployment thresholds. Conditional on the Investigator’s listed sampling, preregistration, bounded-cost, approved-domain and provisional-governance assumptions, the fixed-sample confidence construction controls false statistical certification for the probability gates and for economic contrasts formed from exact settled costs. The stated extension to conservatively estimated unresolved costs is not yet justified. No comparative winner, deployment safety or economic advantage has been established.
objective_review.argument_summary: Cycle 3 defines offered-demand useful completion, derives paired coverage and cross-task economic contrasts, and allocates four two-sided Hoeffding intervals to a 5% family error budget. Those deductions work for the specified independent bounded variables. Upper liability substitution does not generally preserve the sign of the actual economic contrast; signed interval propagation repairs this gap. Sample arithmetic is correct, but joint feasibility must include the stringent noninferiority gate. Cycle 2 supplies a reusable conditional handoff-ordering argument, not implementation evidence.

Use authorized task copies, blinded assessors and randomized execution order, with isolated/reset budget and queue state where replay is valid. Do not duplicate sensitive work to an unapproved destination merely to form a pair. Shared queues, monthly budget depletion and repeated tasks from the same researcher generally violate episode-level independence. In those cases use independent reset load blocks as sampling units, with a fixed number of enrolled tasks per block, or design a cluster/randomized-period analysis before collection. Bounds on block averages remain valid, but N then means independent blocks, not calls or tasks. Unavailable independent replication makes inference inconclusive rather than permitting an invented effective sample size.

review.rationale: Accepted only as the explicitly conditional sampling premise. Within-pair dependence is compatible with independent paired vectors; genuinely independent fixed-size block averages are also bounded variables. The step correctly excludes ordinary shared-state episodes from an unsupported independence claim.

argument_steps.title: 5. Define costs at a common service scale
argument_steps.argument: Let c_si be nonnegative cost per offered episode at a declared common annual demand and accounting perspective. Include costs of failed episodes, all billable subcalls and permitted retries, idle capacity, staffing and federation administration. Allocate fixed annual costs over the declared annual offered demand, not over observed successes; keep sunk, incremental and fully loaded analyses separate. Define mu_s=E[c_si], and cost per useful task q_s=mu_s/p_s for p_s>0. The primary economic comparison uses fully loaded cost; repeat incremental analysis as a sensitivity, not a replacement. Cost certification below additionally requires enforceable bounds 0≤c_si≤M_s, settled charges or conservative liability bounds, and a known positive baseline cost floor. Unknown fixed allocations require declared uncertainty ranges; an economic go must survive their approved adverse values. An unsettled charged timeout is not zero cost. No prices, costs or workload observations are supplied here.

review.rationale: The common-demand cost allocation and ratio-of-means estimand are coherent for actual costs. The alternative allowing conservative liability bounds is insufficiently specified to support certification of actual economic cost.
review.objection: Upper bounds on baseline costs are not conservative when those costs later enter the economic contrast negatively. Require settled costs, a clearly labeled liability-surrogate estimand, or signed propagation of lower and upper cost bounds.

argument_steps.title: 6. Construct the paired coverage and economic contrasts
argument_steps.argument: Let D_i=Y_Fi−Y_Bi, so D_i lies in [−1,1] and Delta=E[D_i]=p_F−p_B. The coverage hurdle is Delta≥0.10. For the economic hurdle q_F/q_B≤0.80, positive denominators give the equivalent inequality K=mu_F p_B−0.80 mu_B p_F≤0. A mean of per-episode cost/success ratios is undefined on failures and is not this estimand. To estimate K without assuming cost and success are independent within a task, partition the N independent pairs into m=floor(N/2) disjoint two-task blocks (i,j), fixed before outcomes. Define Z=(c_Fi Y_Bj+c_Fj Y_Bi−0.80 c_Bi Y_Fj−0.80 c_Bj Y_Fi)/2. Cross-task independence gives E[Z]=K, while arbitrary within-task dependence is retained. Each Z lies in [−0.80 M_B,M_F], and disjoint blocks are independent. Using only these disjoint products sacrifices precision but makes a finite-sample paired rule transparent.

review.rationale: For exact costs and positive denominators, multiplying q_F/q_B≤0.80 gives the stated K inequality. Cross-task independence makes each product’s expectation a product of means without requiring within-task independence. Averaging two terms preserves the stated range, and disjoint task blocks preserve independence.

argument_steps.title: 7. Give one simultaneous confidence rule
argument_steps.argument: Use one fixed final analysis with family error alpha=0.05. Form two-sided intervals for four quantities: p_F, p_B, Delta and K. Hoeffding’s bounded-variable inequality gives P(|mean−expectation|>w sqrt(log(160)/(2n)))≤0.0125 for range width w, since 2 exp(−2n r²/w²)=0.0125. A union bound therefore gives simultaneous coverage at least 95%, without independence among the four intervals. Write a=sqrt(log(160)/(2N)). The intervals are p_s: mean(Y_s)±a; Delta: mean(D)±2a; K: mean(Z)±(M_F+0.80M_B)sqrt(log(160)/(2m)). Clip probability intervals to [0,1] and the Delta interval to [−1,1]. Denote endpoints L and U. This is deliberately conservative, distribution-free under the listed assumptions, and valid for the prespecified OR between the two benefit pathways.

review.rationale: For each exact bounded mean, the radius gives two-tail error 2 exp(−log(160))=0.0125. Four such errors sum to 0.05, regardless of dependence among intervals. Probability and difference clipping do not reduce coverage.

argument_steps.title: 8. State the provisional statistical go rule
argument_steps.argument: After all nonstatistical gates pass, require L_pF≥0.90 and either (A) L_Delta≥0.10, or (B) U_K≤0 together with L_Delta≥−0.02. The −2-point completion noninferiority margin is an additional provisional safeguard: lower cost must not hide a materially less useful service. Path B also requires L_pB>0 and a known positive mu_B, so the baseline cost-per-useful-task ratio is meaningful. On the simultaneous-coverage event, each certified inequality holds for its population parameter. Thus a statistical go with any false required parameter inequality can occur only outside that event, with probability at most 5%. This controls statistical false-go risk, not policy, contract, implementation or safety risk. At an exact hurdle, high probability of certification should not be expected; power requires a real margin beyond it.

review.rationale: The simultaneous-event argument correctly controls false certification for exact-cost K and the probability inequalities, including the prespecified OR. It does not cover the settlement bias permitted in step 5.
review.objection: The blanket false-go claim must exclude replacing both services’ actual costs with upper liability estimates. Equal actual costs can then pass the economic pathway with probability one at sufficiently large N; confidence coverage for the surrogate does not establish coverage for actual K.

argument_steps.title: 9. Derive completion and paired-coverage sample requirements
argument_steps.argument: For completion half-width h, N≥ceil(log(160)/(2h²)): h=0.05 requires 1,016 independent pairs and h=0.03 requires 2,820. For paired Delta half-width h, its range width is 2, so N≥ceil(2 log(160)/h²): h=0.05 requires 4,061 pairs. At N=3,000 the completion half-width is approximately 0.0291 and the Delta half-width approximately 0.0582; certification therefore requires observed F completion at least about 92.91% and observed advantage at least about 15.82 points. These are analytical requirements, not measured rates. The ceiling matters: if B truly exceeds 90% completion, F cannot improve it by 10 points; if B is exactly 90%, that pathway requires perfect population completion. Cost improvement may therefore be the relevant pathway for an already effective baseline.

review.rationale: Solving the stated radii for N gives the reported ceilings 1,016, 2,820 and 4,061. The N=3,000 radii and certification thresholds agree with those formulas. The population ceiling p_F≤1 establishes the stated limitation of the 10-point advantage pathway.

argument_steps.title: 10. Distinguish precision from power and expose cost sensitivity
argument_steps.argument: For a bounded mean with range width w, a true favorable margin g beyond its hurdle is certified with probability at least 1−beta if N≥w²[ sqrt(log(160)/2)+sqrt(log(1/beta)/2) ]²/g². This follows by adding the confidence radius to the one-sided Hoeffding sampling deviation. With beta=0.20, true p_F=0.95 versus the 0.90 hurdle is certifiable with at least 80% probability at N=2,500; true Delta=0.15 versus 0.10 requires N=10,000 under this conservative bound. These are individual-gate power guarantees, not joint pilot power. For K precision e, require m≥ceil((M_F+0.80M_B)² log(160)/(2e²)). If both cost bounds equal M, half-width 0.10M needs 823 independent two-task blocks, or 1,646 task pairs; half-width 0.02M needs 20,555 blocks, or 41,110 pairs. This is normalized sensitivity, not a dollar scenario. A rare expensive tail can make cost certification impractical in 90 days. Moreover K=(R−0.80)mu_B p_F for R=q_F/q_B, so a 20% saving exactly at R=0.80 supplies no favorable margin at all.

review.rationale: Adding the confidence radius to a one-sided Hoeffding deviation yields the stated individual-gate power bound. The conservative rounded counts and normalized cost-precision counts satisfy their formulas, and K=(R−0.80)mu_B p_F follows algebraically.

argument_steps.title: 11. Distinguish safety-stop, no-go and inconclusive
argument_steps.argument: Safety-stop: immediately suspend affected routing on a confirmed forbidden controlled handoff, unauthorized derived-artifact disclosure, unreserved paid attempt or verified cap breach; investigate rather than average the incident into a success rate. Missing safety instrumentation blocks go but is not evidence of a breach. Statistical no-go: U_pF<0.90, or both benefit pathways are ruled out—U_Delta<0.10 and either L_K>0 or U_Delta<−0.02. A definite campus contract/security veto or infeasible funding is an administrative no-go, separately labeled. Inconclusive: bounds overlap a required hurdle, sample assumptions fail, evidence is missing, or neither a go nor a no-go condition holds. Failure to reject a hurdle is not evidence that it was met. No paid trial runs after budget exhaustion; resulting service refusals stay in the enrolled denominator. A pilot stopped for safety has no deployment go regardless of favorable completion estimates.

review.rationale: Safety-stop, missing-instrumentation and inconclusive classifications are appropriately separated. For exact K, the no-go Boolean expression is the complement of the two benefit pathways on the simultaneous-coverage event.
review.objection: Economic no-go also needs signed settlement uncertainty: overestimated federation costs can spuriously make L_K positive. Apply a lower confidence bound to a valid lower contrast for actual K, not a contrast containing arbitrary upper cost estimates.

argument_steps.title: 12. Make the 90-day collection plan executable without optional stopping
argument_steps.argument: Days 1–30: security owns approved domains and fault-test oracles; computing owns load blocks, queues, hardware-fit and independent egress instrumentation; procurement/finance owns liability bounds and cost allocations; faculty and student representatives own task rubrics, deadlines and blinded adjudication; an evaluation lead freezes sampling, N, analysis and exclusions. Include coding, routine analysis, scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context, agentic, sensitive and reproducible-batch strata, with peak, cold-start and maintenance conditions. Days 31–60: run synthetic safety/fault tests and estimate variance/dependence using a development set excluded from confirmatory analysis. Days 61–90: collect the frozen confirmatory sample under approved hard caps, then analyze once after every episode’s deadline and the declared billing-reconciliation cutoff. Safety monitoring is continuous, but favorable interim estimates do not permit early statistical go. Insufficient independent units by day 90 means inconclusive; extension needs a fresh approved plan or a prespecified sequential method. If the budget cannot support four service executions per episode, prioritize the B–F paired comparison and clearly label reduced descriptive coverage of baselines 1 and 2.

review.rationale: The proposed development/confirmation split, frozen final analysis and prohibition on favorable interim stopping are compatible with the fixed-sample guarantee. Independent-unit and budget shortfalls are explicitly classified as inconclusive rather than quietly reducing the sample or escalating spending.

argument_steps.title: 13. Preserve autonomy, fairness and evidence limitations
argument_steps.argument: Overall mixture success cannot certify each campus, task class or protected queue. Report campus/task/load-stratum completion, refusal reasons, queue-deadline misses, starvation, throughput, availability, provenance completeness, staff hours and cost attribution. A deployment rule requiring a separate completion floor for every campus needs additional simultaneous intervals and enough independent units per campus; the pooled sample counts above do not establish that. Governance must approve those floors and interactive/batch shares before deployment. Retain the earlier negative constraints: separated check-then-send is not current-policy handoff enforcement, and releasing an unresolved timeout hold can permit overspending. The supplied cycle-2 extract describes conditional models, not implementation evidence; o411 remains recorded as addressed analytically, while its contract and operational duties and the other unresolved ledger entries stay open. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions. The brief attributes protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, logging and telemetry to the published campus MindRouter gateway; current source verification, comparative usefulness and deployment readiness are not established here.

review.rationale: A pooled mixture mean cannot entail campus- or stratum-specific floors; additional simultaneous inference is correctly required. The step preserves conditional safety constraints and distinguishes brief-attributed MindRouter descriptions from inspected sources and hypothetical extensions.

artifacts.claim_or_question: A single campus-controlled policy-and-egress broker can exclude the check→revoke→release race at a precisely defined boundary: acceptance of bytes by its outbound operating-system transport. Conditional on complete mediation, trusted enforcement, durable accounting and exclusive broker ownership, every such submission is authorized by the campus policy then in force. This does not guarantee that no bytes physically leave a NIC or reach a recipient after revocation: previously accepted transport data may remain queued or be retransmitted. The contract must therefore be narrowed to immediate revocation of new transport submissions, with unresolved billing reservations retained across crashes.

artifacts.skeptic_response:
Cycle 2 substantially answers the requested state-machine question. Holding the same mutex across final validation and synchronous OS transport acceptance excludes an intervening policy commit. Durable ARMED records do not become replayable permissions, and retaining uncertain reservations avoids assuming an atomic disk-and-network transaction. These are convincing conditional specifications, not implementation evidence.

An independent event-order check confirms the distinction: CHECK(v0), COMMIT_REVOKE(v1), FINAL_SUBMIT must deny; ACCEPT(chunk1,v0), COMMIT_REVOKE(v1), FINAL_SUBMIT(chunk2) permits only the earlier acceptance. A crash immediately before versus immediately after acceptance can leave the same durable ARMED record, so recovery cannot safely infer non-dispatch. Retaining liability and prohibiting replay is conservative in both histories. Settlement changes accounted liability by c−r≤0 when the enforceable charge satisfies c≤r.

The physical-egress counterexample is valid: ACCEPT, COMMIT_REVOKE, NIC_TRANSMIT is compatible with ordinary buffering. Narrowing the guarantee to new OS submissions explicitly avoids claiming physical cutoff or recipient deletion. Campus acceptance of this narrower contract remains essential.

One statement needs correction or an additional mechanism: step 11 says loss of the authority path stops submissions. If this means broker failure, it follows from exclusive ownership and fencing. If it means loss of an administrator-to-broker path while the broker remains operational, the specified machine has no transition that detects that loss and stops submissions. A remote revocation request that never commits is deliberately outside the new contract. The core submission invariant survives, but the broader partition-availability description does not follow without specifying which path and event disable admission.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Separate the existing gateway description from this proposal
reasoning_steps.argument: The project reports MindRouter protocol translation for OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic clients and Ollama/vLLM backends, WDRR scheduling, per-user quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry. No inspected source establishes that it implements the broker below. Federation, frontier routing, release serialization and a financial reservation ledger are proposed extensions. The missing source records are https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf. Their supplied prior review date is 2026-10-31; this investigator has no access date and cannot verify changed claims.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Locate the authority and narrow the release contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Propose one home-campus broker B as both the policy-commit authority for managed releases and the sole owner of their outbound sockets. Authenticated campus administrators submit updates to B; a separate administrative database or cached policy service cannot independently make a policy effective. An update takes effect when B durably commits it under its exclusive mutex M, and acknowledgment follows that commit. This defines the authoritative order, not an administrator's click time or message arrival time. Define release as successful acceptance of a positive byte count by the OS outbound transport through B. It is not enqueueing an application job, committing an authorization record, calling an asynchronously buffered client, NIC transmission or recipient delivery. The proposed contract forbids any new submission denied by a revocation committed earlier. It gives no bounded revocation-response time and does not recall prior submissions.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. State the minimal enforcement boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: B uses one serialized execution path for policy updates and content submissions. Only it holds destination credentials and owns managed outbound connections; workers and tenants have no alternative managed egress. Its transport adapter exposes synchronous nonblocking submission without an independently flushing application/TLS content queue. Encryption may prepare immutable bytes inside the trusted broker, but all submissions to sockets still pass through B. Each immutable data unit binds its bytes, conservative label, authenticated principal/project, destination identity, connection, retention/contract requirements and reservation identifier. Changing any binding requires revalidation. Logs, embeddings, tool calls, caches, streamed outputs and content-bearing telemetry require equivalent mediation when crossing their approved boundaries. Unknown classification denies release to a domain not explicitly approved for that uncertainty. A malicious tenant cannot lower a trusted label. Compromise of B, the OS enforcement boundary or label assignment is outside the conditional guarantee; unrelated human copying is also outside it.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Define durable state and admission transitions
reasoning_steps.argument: Durable global state contains policy P with version v, a monotone operation identifier, broker recovery epoch, an audit journal and hierarchical budget accounts. An attempt has immutable request bindings, a reservation r and phase READY, HELD, ARMED, OPEN, UNCERTAIN or CLOSED. READY means locally queued and confers no release permission. A preliminary CHECK may estimate eligibility but creates no reusable capability. RESERVE atomically checks every applicable campus/department/project/user limit and durably changes READY→HELD, reserving an enforceable upper bound for the entire billable attempt. It creates no permission to send. With no paid headroom, no paid attempt is admitted; already funded local service may remain eligible. Retries and agent subcalls are separate attempts unless already covered by an explicit enforceable aggregate bound. Provider/SDK automatic application retries are disabled unless separately covered. If no reliable liability bound exists, the paid route is ineligible under a strict hard-cap requirement.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Make FINAL_SUBMIT, not CHECK or ARM, the gate
reasoning_steps.argument: For each bounded data unit, FINAL_SUBMIT acquires M and re-evaluates its immutable bindings against current P, destination authentication, contract/retention requirements, cancellation state and sufficient pinned reservation coverage. Denial makes no transport call. On approval, B durably appends an ARMED intent identifying the unit and policy version, while retaining M. It then immediately performs one nonblocking transport submission under the same M. A positive result n means exactly that prefix was submitted; B records the returned count and marks the attempt OPEN before releasing M. A partial remainder is a new unit requiring another FINAL_SUBMIT. Errors or lost outcome records are handled conservatively; an error never proves that earlier units of the same attempt were not released. No other thread may commit policy or release reservation coverage during this critical section. REVOKE also acquires M, durably updates P and v, then releases M and acknowledges. ARMED is a write-ahead record, not an independently executable send permit. There is deliberately no detached authorized outbox worker.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Derive the submission invariant
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially no units have been submitted. Consider the next positive transport acceptance. Its FINAL_SUBMIT holds M from the current-policy check through that acceptance, so a revocation cannot commit between those events. The bytes and destination cannot change because their bindings are immutable. Therefore the policy at acceptance is the policy that approved the unit. A failed check adds no submitted unit. RESERVE, CHECK and ARMED alone also add none. Induction proves authorization for every finite history of these submission events under the stated trusted-enforcement premises. If FINAL_SUBMIT obtains M before a concurrent REVOKE, that submission can precede the revocation commit; if REVOKE commits first, the submission must use the updated policy. This is a linearized submission contract, not revocation at request-arrival time.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Hand-check check→revoke→release and streaming
reasoning_steps.argument: Trace A: P=v0 permits destination D; CHECK(v0) succeeds; RESERVE produces HELD(r); REVOKE commits v1 denying D; FINAL_SUBMIT obtains M, reads v1, denies, and makes no transport call. The blocking transition is the current-policy guard in FINAL_SUBMIT, not queue invalidation or credential expiry. Trace B: FINAL_SUBMIT(chunk 1,v0) accepts n1 bytes; REVOKE commits v1; FINAL_SUBMIT(chunk 2) reads v1 and denies. No later application chunk may be submitted under the old approval. Bytes from chunk 1 may still be in transit. If chunk 1 was an outbound prompt already accepted by a provider, revocation does not undo provider processing or billing. An inbound provider stream may be stopped, but delivery of each output chunk across another controlled boundary needs its own authorization. Cancellation is best effort downstream and cannot certify deletion or zero charges.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Hand-check crash after authorization and specify recovery
reasoning_steps.argument: Trace C: RESERVE(r) is durable; FINAL_SUBMIT validates v0 and durably writes ARMED; B crashes before its transport call. In this actual trace no bytes were submitted. Recovery, however, may see the same durable ARMED record after a crash that occurred just after transport acceptance but before its result was recorded. It must not infer non-dispatch from that record. Recovery starts with submission disabled, requires confirmed termination/fencing of the former broker and socket ownership, loads the last durable policy and ledger, advances the epoch, and marks unfinished ARMED or OPEN attempts UNCERTAIN with r retained. It closes rather than resumes those connections and never replays their send intents. A committed v1 revocation remains effective after recovery; a merely pending revocation has not yet committed and its caller must retry. Any later permitted attempt needs fresh policy validation and sufficient reservation for additional liability. Availability is sacrificed if old-owner fencing or policy recovery cannot be established. Previously OS-accepted bytes may survive the process crash; they remain prior submissions, not permissions to resume application sends.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Preserve billing coverage without claiming atomic network-and-disk commit
reasoning_steps.argument: For each account a, require settled spend S_a plus unresolved reservations R_a to be at most its funded cap B_a. RESERVE increases R_a only when every applicable account can cover it, in one durable serialized transaction. ARMED, submission, revocation, cancellation, timeout and crash do not reclaim it. Final settlement replaces r by charge c≤r, changing accounted liability by c−r≤0. Certified non-dispatch can release a reservation only when no further transmission is possible and no earlier transmission of that attempt could incur liability. Recovery uncertainty is not such a certificate. Reconciliation and settlement must be authenticated, final under the billing contract and applied once; additional sends are prohibited after final settlement. A new potentially chargeable retry requires additional coverage rather than reusing an unresolved reservation. Reservations are not erased at month rollover: they remain backed in their original funded accounts, with any exposure to another billing period funded there too. Atomicity with physical sending is neither claimed nor required for conservative coverage: durable intent precedes sending, and uncertain outcomes retain liability. This can strand budget indefinitely without final reconciliation.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Give the physical-egress counterexample and reject overclaiming
reasoning_steps.argument: Let OS_ACCEPT(chunk,v0) occur while M is held. B releases M, REVOKE commits v1, and only then a queued packet carrying that chunk leaves the NIC. Ordinary transport buffering permits this schedule. TCP may also retransmit earlier accepted bytes after revocation. Thus a mutex around policy checks and socket submissions does not establish 'no physical byte crosses the campus boundary after commit.' Even a campus firewall policy update is not evidence of atomic ordering with every NIC queue and in-flight packet. Under this architecture I reject that stronger guarantee and retain only no new denied transport submissions after commit. If campus policy instead demands serialization at physical transmission, this proposal is insufficient: a trusted final-egress mechanism must control and order all relevant hardware queues, retransmissions and failover paths, with an explicitly accepted packet/byte granularity. No such implementation or proof is supplied.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. State the partition and baseline consequences
reasoning_steps.argument: The broker is deliberately not a partition-tolerant replica of an independently committing policy authority. Loss of its authority path stops new external submissions rather than validating cached approvals. Minimal recovery has no automatic active-active failover; adding it would require fencing and a new ordering argument. A partitioned partner cannot autonomously originate new home-campus-authorized releases under this contract. It may already possess legitimately released data, for which partner enforcement and agreements remain separate requirements. Baseline 1 needs fewer off-campus content paths but still needs internal boundary controls. Baseline 2 needs approved remote processing and budget coverage for all eligible tasks. Baseline 3 can use one explicitly approved external connector and this home-campus gate. Baseline 4 adds partner boundaries and downstream obligations without improving this submission invariant by itself. Where federation adds no demonstrated authorized task capability, baseline 3 avoids those extra obligations; no measured quality, availability or economic ranking follows.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Specify a discriminating implementation test and its limits
reasoning_steps.argument: Next test: build a synthetic-canary broker sandbox with controllable pauses after preliminary CHECK, after durable ARMED, immediately before transport submission, and after acceptance but before result logging. Run the three traces above and the competing implementation that releases M before sending. Observe successful kernel submissions independently of broker success logs, join them to authoritative policy-commit order, and reconcile durable reservations after recovery. An external packet capture separately tests the stronger physical interpretation but cannot by itself distinguish a new submission from an old transport retransmission. Predicted outcome: the detached check-then-send control admits the stale schedule, while this specification denies Trace A and chunk 2 of Trace B and retains Trace C's reservation. These are predictions, not results. Any denied new submission or uncovered liability is a safety stop; recovery that cannot fence the former owner must remain unavailable. Finite passing tests would support only those schedules, not prove complete mediation, recipient compliance or all-schedule correctness.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Separate the existing gateway description from this proposal
reasoning_steps.argument: The project reports MindRouter protocol translation for OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic clients and Ollama/vLLM backends, WDRR scheduling, per-user quotas, audit logging and GPU telemetry. No inspected source establishes that it implements the broker below. Federation, frontier routing, release serialization and a financial reservation ledger are proposed extensions. The missing source records are https://mindrouter.ai/documentation.html and https://ai4ra.uidaho.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Sheneman_MindRouter_PEARC26_Short_Paper.pdf. Their supplied prior review date is 2026-10-31; this investigator has no access date and cannot verify changed claims.

review.rationale: The step attributes features only to the project description, identifies both missing publications and does not represent federation, frontier routing or the reservation ledger as documented MindRouter features.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Locate the authority and narrow the release contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Propose one home-campus broker B as both the policy-commit authority for managed releases and the sole owner of their outbound sockets. Authenticated campus administrators submit updates to B; a separate administrative database or cached policy service cannot independently make a policy effective. An update takes effect when B durably commits it under its exclusive mutex M, and acknowledgment follows that commit. This defines the authoritative order, not an administrator's click time or message arrival time. Define release as successful acceptance of a positive byte count by the OS outbound transport through B. It is not enqueueing an application job, committing an authorization record, calling an asynchronously buffered client, NIC transmission or recipient delivery. The proposed contract forbids any new submission denied by a revocation committed earlier. It gives no bounded revocation-response time and does not recall prior submissions.

review.rationale: This is an explicit premise of the conditional claim. Making durable broker commit authoritative and OS acceptance the release event gives a definite order without implying revocation at administrator intent, message arrival or physical transmission.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. State the minimal enforcement boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: B uses one serialized execution path for policy updates and content submissions. Only it holds destination credentials and owns managed outbound connections; workers and tenants have no alternative managed egress. Its transport adapter exposes synchronous nonblocking submission without an independently flushing application/TLS content queue. Encryption may prepare immutable bytes inside the trusted broker, but all submissions to sockets still pass through B. Each immutable data unit binds its bytes, conservative label, authenticated principal/project, destination identity, connection, retention/contract requirements and reservation identifier. Changing any binding requires revalidation. Logs, embeddings, tool calls, caches, streamed outputs and content-bearing telemetry require equivalent mediation when crossing their approved boundaries. Unknown classification denies release to a domain not explicitly approved for that uncertainty. A malicious tenant cannot lower a trusted label. Compromise of B, the OS enforcement boundary or label assignment is outside the conditional guarantee; unrelated human copying is also outside it.

review.rationale: As listed premises, exclusive socket ownership, immutable bindings, conservative labels and mediation cover the paths required by the claimed invariant. Excluding independent application-content flushing is necessary to avoid a deferred send outside the gate; none of these properties is presented as measured.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Define durable state and admission transitions
reasoning_steps.argument: Durable global state contains policy P with version v, a monotone operation identifier, broker recovery epoch, an audit journal and hierarchical budget accounts. An attempt has immutable request bindings, a reservation r and phase READY, HELD, ARMED, OPEN, UNCERTAIN or CLOSED. READY means locally queued and confers no release permission. A preliminary CHECK may estimate eligibility but creates no reusable capability. RESERVE atomically checks every applicable campus/department/project/user limit and durably changes READY→HELD, reserving an enforceable upper bound for the entire billable attempt. It creates no permission to send. With no paid headroom, no paid attempt is admitted; already funded local service may remain eligible. Retries and agent subcalls are separate attempts unless already covered by an explicit enforceable aggregate bound. Provider/SDK automatic application retries are disabled unless separately covered. If no reliable liability bound exists, the paid route is ineligible under a strict hard-cap requirement.

review.rationale: READY, CHECK and reservation creation confer no send permission. Atomic reservation against every applicable account and an enforceable whole-attempt bound are sufficient admission premises; uncovered automatic retries are expressly excluded.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Make FINAL_SUBMIT, not CHECK or ARM, the gate
reasoning_steps.argument: For each bounded data unit, FINAL_SUBMIT acquires M and re-evaluates its immutable bindings against current P, destination authentication, contract/retention requirements, cancellation state and sufficient pinned reservation coverage. Denial makes no transport call. On approval, B durably appends an ARMED intent identifying the unit and policy version, while retaining M. It then immediately performs one nonblocking transport submission under the same M. A positive result n means exactly that prefix was submitted; B records the returned count and marks the attempt OPEN before releasing M. A partial remainder is a new unit requiring another FINAL_SUBMIT. Errors or lost outcome records are handled conservatively; an error never proves that earlier units of the same attempt were not released. No other thread may commit policy or release reservation coverage during this critical section. REVOKE also acquires M, durably updates P and v, then releases M and acknowledges. ARMED is a write-ahead record, not an independently executable send permit. There is deliberately no detached authorized outbox worker.

review.rationale: Under the stated adapter premise, retaining M through the synchronous acceptance result prevents REVOKE from committing between validation and acceptance. Treating every partial remainder as a fresh unit and ARMED as non-executable prevents reuse of an earlier authorization.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Derive the submission invariant
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially no units have been submitted. Consider the next positive transport acceptance. Its FINAL_SUBMIT holds M from the current-policy check through that acceptance, so a revocation cannot commit between those events. The bytes and destination cannot change because their bindings are immutable. Therefore the policy at acceptance is the policy that approved the unit. A failed check adds no submitted unit. RESERVE, CHECK and ARMED alone also add none. Induction proves authorization for every finite history of these submission events under the stated trusted-enforcement premises. If FINAL_SUBMIT obtains M before a concurrent REVOKE, that submission can precede the revocation commit; if REVOKE commits first, the submission must use the updated policy. This is a linearized submission contract, not revocation at request-arrival time.

review.rationale: For each positive acceptance, mutual exclusion fixes the effective policy throughout validation and acceptance, while immutable bindings fix the authorized object and destination. Rejection adds no acceptance event, so induction proves the finite-history submission invariant under the listed premises.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Hand-check check→revoke→release and streaming
reasoning_steps.argument: Trace A: P=v0 permits destination D; CHECK(v0) succeeds; RESERVE produces HELD(r); REVOKE commits v1 denying D; FINAL_SUBMIT obtains M, reads v1, denies, and makes no transport call. The blocking transition is the current-policy guard in FINAL_SUBMIT, not queue invalidation or credential expiry. Trace B: FINAL_SUBMIT(chunk 1,v0) accepts n1 bytes; REVOKE commits v1; FINAL_SUBMIT(chunk 2) reads v1 and denies. No later application chunk may be submitted under the old approval. Bytes from chunk 1 may still be in transit. If chunk 1 was an outbound prompt already accepted by a provider, revocation does not undo provider processing or billing. An inbound provider stream may be stopped, but delivery of each output chunk across another controlled boundary needs its own authorization. Cancellation is best effort downstream and cannot certify deletion or zero charges.

review.rationale: After v1 commits, each subsequent FINAL_SUBMIT reads v1 and denies the prohibited destination. The earlier accepted prefix is outside recall, and separate authorization for output-boundary crossings correctly avoids treating an admitted request as unlimited streaming permission.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Hand-check crash after authorization and specify recovery
reasoning_steps.argument: Trace C: RESERVE(r) is durable; FINAL_SUBMIT validates v0 and durably writes ARMED; B crashes before its transport call. In this actual trace no bytes were submitted. Recovery, however, may see the same durable ARMED record after a crash that occurred just after transport acceptance but before its result was recorded. It must not infer non-dispatch from that record. Recovery starts with submission disabled, requires confirmed termination/fencing of the former broker and socket ownership, loads the last durable policy and ledger, advances the epoch, and marks unfinished ARMED or OPEN attempts UNCERTAIN with r retained. It closes rather than resumes those connections and never replays their send intents. A committed v1 revocation remains effective after recovery; a merely pending revocation has not yet committed and its caller must retry. Any later permitted attempt needs fresh policy validation and sufficient reservation for additional liability. Availability is sacrificed if old-owner fencing or policy recovery cannot be established. Previously OS-accepted bytes may survive the process crash; they remain prior submissions, not permissions to resume application sends.

review.rationale: Crashes just before and just after acceptance can expose the same durable ARMED record. Recovery therefore cannot infer non-dispatch; no replay, retained reservations and confirmed old-owner fencing are conservative in both cases. This remains conditional on the stated recovery and ownership premises.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Preserve billing coverage without claiming atomic network-and-disk commit
reasoning_steps.argument: For each account a, require settled spend S_a plus unresolved reservations R_a to be at most its funded cap B_a. RESERVE increases R_a only when every applicable account can cover it, in one durable serialized transaction. ARMED, submission, revocation, cancellation, timeout and crash do not reclaim it. Final settlement replaces r by charge c≤r, changing accounted liability by c−r≤0. Certified non-dispatch can release a reservation only when no further transmission is possible and no earlier transmission of that attempt could incur liability. Recovery uncertainty is not such a certificate. Reconciliation and settlement must be authenticated, final under the billing contract and applied once; additional sends are prohibited after final settlement. A new potentially chargeable retry requires additional coverage rather than reusing an unresolved reservation. Reservations are not erased at month rollover: they remain backed in their original funded accounts, with any exposure to another billing period funded there too. Atomicity with physical sending is neither claimed nor required for conservative coverage: durable intent precedes sending, and uncertain outcomes retain liability. This can strand budget indefinitely without final reconciliation.

review.rationale: Atomic admission preserves each cap, and final settlement changes accounted liability by c−r≤0. Keeping unresolved coverage through cancellation, crash and rollover avoids premature reclamation. The result explicitly depends on enforceable billing scope, final reconciliation and coverage in every exposed account or period.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Give the physical-egress counterexample and reject overclaiming
reasoning_steps.argument: Let OS_ACCEPT(chunk,v0) occur while M is held. B releases M, REVOKE commits v1, and only then a queued packet carrying that chunk leaves the NIC. Ordinary transport buffering permits this schedule. TCP may also retransmit earlier accepted bytes after revocation. Thus a mutex around policy checks and socket submissions does not establish 'no physical byte crosses the campus boundary after commit.' Even a campus firewall policy update is not evidence of atomic ordering with every NIC queue and in-flight packet. Under this architecture I reject that stronger guarantee and retain only no new denied transport submissions after commit. If campus policy instead demands serialization at physical transmission, this proposal is insufficient: a trusted final-egress mechanism must control and order all relevant hardware queues, retransmissions and failover paths, with an explicitly accepted packet/byte granularity. No such implementation or proof is supplied.

review.rationale: The exact order OS acceptance, revocation commit, later NIC transmission is compatible with the specified boundary. It refutes the stronger physical-cutoff interpretation without refuting authorization of new OS acceptances. The changed scope is stated explicitly.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. State the partition and baseline consequences
reasoning_steps.argument: The broker is deliberately not a partition-tolerant replica of an independently committing policy authority. Loss of its authority path stops new external submissions rather than validating cached approvals. Minimal recovery has no automatic active-active failover; adding it would require fencing and a new ordering argument. A partitioned partner cannot autonomously originate new home-campus-authorized releases under this contract. It may already possess legitimately released data, for which partner enforcement and agreements remain separate requirements. Baseline 1 needs fewer off-campus content paths but still needs internal boundary controls. Baseline 2 needs approved remote processing and budget coverage for all eligible tasks. Baseline 3 can use one explicitly approved external connector and this home-campus gate. Baseline 4 adds partner boundaries and downstream obligations without improving this submission invariant by itself. Where federation adds no demonstrated authorized task capability, baseline 3 avoids those extra obligations; no measured quality, availability or economic ranking follows.

review.rationale: The architectural baseline comparison is appropriately non-empirical, and a partner has no independent home-authority permission. However, the claimed response to loss of the authority path is not entailed for every plausible meaning of that path.
review.objection: Specify whether this is broker/ownership failure or an administrator-to-broker partition. In the latter case, the broker can retain P=v0 and submit while an undelivered revocation remains uncommitted; no supplied disabling transition forbids it. Narrow the statement or add an explicit mechanism and its detection limits.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Specify a discriminating implementation test and its limits
reasoning_steps.argument: Next test: build a synthetic-canary broker sandbox with controllable pauses after preliminary CHECK, after durable ARMED, immediately before transport submission, and after acceptance but before result logging. Run the three traces above and the competing implementation that releases M before sending. Observe successful kernel submissions independently of broker success logs, join them to authoritative policy-commit order, and reconcile durable reservations after recovery. An external packet capture separately tests the stronger physical interpretation but cannot by itself distinguish a new submission from an old transport retransmission. Predicted outcome: the detached check-then-send control admits the stale schedule, while this specification denies Trace A and chunk 2 of Trace B and retains Trace C's reservation. These are predictions, not results. Any denied new submission or uncovered liability is a safety stop; recovery that cannot fence the former owner must remain unavailable. Finite passing tests would support only those schedules, not prove complete mediation, recipient compliance or all-schedule correctness.

review.rationale: Pausing at the named boundaries distinguishes detached check-then-send from serialized submission, and an independent submission observer plus policy order is the relevant oracle. Packet capture alone cannot distinguish fresh acceptance from retransmission. The step reports predictions and finite-test limits, not results.

artifacts.next_question: Clarify cycle-2 step 11 using two exact histories: (A) an administrator cannot reach an otherwise functioning broker while an update remains uncommitted, and (B) the broker loses exclusive authority or confirmed ownership. For each, list the observations and transition that permit or disable FINAL_SUBMIT. Show whether the current specification actually guarantees fail-closed behavior, or explicitly narrow that statement to broker/ownership failure. Give an observation oracle that distinguishes a committed revocation from an undelivered request without equating timestamps or packet transmission with OS acceptance. Preserve the submission and reservation derivations; no execution or deployment claim is needed.
artifacts.note: Unverified research note. Any Investigator Python or SageMath execution, including its source, status, output, and captured artifacts, is recorded below and is not proof by itself.

objective_review.claim: Conditional on: The campus accepts revocation effective at durable broker commit and release defined as OS transport acceptance, not administrator request time, physical transmission or recipient delivery; One trusted broker exclusively orders policy commits and managed submissions under one mutex; no independent authority can make a newer policy effective outside that order; Trusted labels are conservative, data/destination bindings are immutable, destinations are authenticated, and every relevant managed content path is completely mediated; The transport adapter has no independently flushing application-content queue; the broker retains serialization through synchronous nonblocking OS submission; Policy, intents and hierarchical reservations are durably recorded; recovery cannot roll back acknowledged commits and cannot enable submissions before exclusive ownership is established; Each paid attempt has an enforceable aggregate liability bound covering its billing scope; all additional chargeable transmissions have coverage, and final reconciliation is trustworthy. Conditional on campus acceptance of commit-time revocation at OS transport acceptance, one exclusively owned trusted broker, complete mediation, immutable conservative labels and destination bindings, a transport adapter without independently flushing application-content queues, durable non-rollback recovery and enforceable aggregate billing bounds, the proposed machine prevents new transport submissions denied by an earlier committed revocation and conservatively retains unresolved billing liability. It does not establish physical-egress cutoff, prompt processing of unreachable administrators' updates, recipient compliance, implementation safety or comparative institutional feasibility.
objective_review.argument_summary: Cycle 1's supplied steps 2–4 establish the partition conflict for an autonomous sender separated from its policy authority; steps 5–6 and 9 give conditional authorization and budget invariants. Cycle 2 supplies a concrete abstract serialization mechanism and recovery discipline, while explicitly narrowing release to OS acceptance. The induction and three hand traces support that narrowed specification. Step 11's unspecified authority-path failure behavior and the project's external-evidence and measurement requirements remain open.

argument_steps.title: 11. State the partition and baseline consequences
argument_steps.argument: The broker is deliberately not a partition-tolerant replica of an independently committing policy authority. Loss of its authority path stops new external submissions rather than validating cached approvals. Minimal recovery has no automatic active-active failover; adding it would require fencing and a new ordering argument. A partitioned partner cannot autonomously originate new home-campus-authorized releases under this contract. It may already possess legitimately released data, for which partner enforcement and agreements remain separate requirements. Baseline 1 needs fewer off-campus content paths but still needs internal boundary controls. Baseline 2 needs approved remote processing and budget coverage for all eligible tasks. Baseline 3 can use one explicitly approved external connector and this home-campus gate. Baseline 4 adds partner boundaries and downstream obligations without improving this submission invariant by itself. Where federation adds no demonstrated authorized task capability, baseline 3 avoids those extra obligations; no measured quality, availability or economic ranking follows.

review.rationale: The architectural baseline comparison is appropriately non-empirical, and a partner has no independent home-authority permission. However, the claimed response to loss of the authority path is not entailed for every plausible meaning of that path.
review.objection: Specify whether this is broker/ownership failure or an administrator-to-broker partition. In the latter case, the broker can retain P=v0 and submit while an undelivered revocation remains uncommitted; no supplied disabling transition forbids it. argument_steps.title: 12. Specify a discriminating implementation test and its limits
argument_steps.argument: Next test: build a synthetic-canary broker sandbox with controllable pauses after preliminary CHECK, after durable ARMED, immediately before transport submission, and after acceptance but before result logging. Run the three traces above and the competing implementation that releases M before sending. Observe successful kernel submissions independently of broker success logs, join them to authoritative policy-commit order, and reconcile durable reservations after recovery. An external packet capture separately tests the stronger physical interpretation but cannot by itself distinguish a new submission from an old transport retransmission. Predicted outcome: the detached check-then-send control admits the stale schedule, while this specification denies Trace A and chunk 2 of Trace B and retains Trace C's reservation. These are predictions, not results. Any denied new submission or uncovered liability is a safety stop; recovery that cannot fence the former owner must remain unavailable. Finite passing tests would support only those schedules, not prove complete mediation, recipient compliance or all-schedule correctness.

review.rationale: Pausing at the named boundaries distinguishes detached check-then-send from serialized submission, and an independent submission observer plus policy order is the relevant oracle.
