reasoning_steps.title: 1. Scope and the proposed contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Define COMMIT(u,v) as the durable broker transaction that makes policy version v effective for update identifier u. Define release as the positive-length prefix accepted by the OS transport during a synchronous, nonblocking submission operation. An administrator issuing a request, a broker receiving it, a durable intent record, physical packet transmission and recipient delivery are different events. The proposed contract forbids a new OS acceptance disallowed by the policy committed before that acceptance in the broker's serialization order. It does not recall previously accepted bytes or promise timely processing of an administrator request. These definitions narrow the guarantee; campus acceptance is still required.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Explicit enabling rule and failure transitions
reasoning_steps.argument: Use broker state (mode, owner_epoch, committed_policy, durable_ledger), with mode initially DISABLED during recovery. FINAL_SUBMIT(a) may enter the transport only if, under the serialization gate: mode=ENABLED; current exclusive ownership is enforceably valid; recovery is complete; the immutable content/destination/identity binding is permitted by committed_policy; classification is unambiguous; and the attempt has sufficient durable reservation coverage. The broker retains the gate through the OS call and result classification. COMMIT uses the same gate. An observed invalid/uncertain ownership result, unrecoverable state ambiguity, or broker shutdown causes DISABLE before any further transport entry. Failure to reach an administrator is not one of these transitions. This is an explicit specification of the intended narrowed rule, not evidence that cycle 2 or MindRouter implements it.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. History A: administrator path fails, broker remains authoritative
reasoning_steps.argument: Initial state A0: broker B is ENABLED in epoch 7; durable v0 permits envelope a to destination D; a has reservation r; B can reach the client and D. A1: administrator X creates update u revoking D, but the request is dropped before B receives it. X observes no commit receipt and eventually a timeout. B observes neither u nor ownership failure; its policy remains v0. A2: B acquires the gate for a, checks the guards against v0, records the required durable intent and invokes the OS adapter while holding the gate. The OS accepts n>0 bytes; this is a permitted release under v0. A3: B releases the gate. Thus administrator unreachability alone does not produce DISABLE. The same release is allowed if u has arrived but remains pending without COMMIT, unless a separate pending-update barrier is specified. Such a barrier is not supplied here.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. History A continued: a later committed revocation
reasoning_steps.argument: A4: X reconnects and submits u. B acquires the gate, durably commits v1 denying D, and only then issues a commit receipt. A5: an unsent suffix of a, another queued envelope, or a new streaming chunk targeting D obtains the gate after that commit and fails policy validation; no OS submission is made for it. Bytes accepted at A2 may still transmit or arrive after A4. If X loses the receipt after A4, the update is nevertheless committed; X's timeout cannot distinguish this case from A1. Receipt loss is an observation ambiguity, not rollback of policy.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. History B: observed ownership uncertainty disables submission
reasoning_steps.argument: Initial state B0 equals A0. B1: before a enters the transport, the trusted ownership check returns UNKNOWN, or the broker receives an ownership-invalid event. B2: at the gate, the broker changes ENABLED to DISABLED and rejects FINAL_SUBMIT(a) before any OS call. Observations are the ownership result, the disable transition and the rejected transport entry, not an administrator timeout. B3: a replacement broker must fence the previous epoch at every managed submission path, recover committed policy and unresolved reservations without rollback, and establish exclusive epoch 8 ownership before enabling. If recovered policy is v1, a is denied; if it is v0 and all other guards pass, a may be admitted as a new authorized submission. Recovery does not automatically replay an uncertain old attempt.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Actual ownership loss is not the same as observing loss
reasoning_steps.argument: If ownership is withdrawn elsewhere while the old broker still reads a cached owner=true and retains a working socket, a local DISABLE transition need not occur. The exact bad schedule is: old broker checks epoch 7; another authority activates epoch 8 without fencing epoch 7; old broker submits using v0. This violates the exclusive-owner premise. Therefore a notification or local Boolean alone is insufficient. A safety claim covering actual ownership loss requires a fence/admission mechanism that orders ownership withdrawal against transport entry: an already admitted operation is ordered before withdrawal, or withdrawal wins and the operation is rejected. No new owner or revocation acknowledgement may rely on the old owner being stopped before that fact is enforced. With this premise absent, the specification guarantees rejection only after observed uncertainty/disable, not after an invisible loss. A dead broker performs no new calls, although its previously accepted OS buffers may still drain.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Authorization derivation and its edge cases
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially there are no releases, so the invariant holds. Consider the next positive OS acceptance. Complete mediation places it inside FINAL_SUBMIT. Its gate excludes COMMIT throughout final validation and the OS call, and effective ownership enforcement excludes an invalid owner. Therefore the latest policy in this serialization order is exactly the policy used by the final guard, which permits the immutable binding. COMMIT changes policy but accepts no content. Rejected operations and certified zero-acceptance calls add no release. Induction gives the invariant for every finite history satisfying these transition premises. For partial sends only the accepted prefix is released; every later application submission revalidates the remainder. Streaming, tool calls, logs, caches and embeddings require the same treatment wherever they cross a managed boundary. An independently flushing TLS/application queue would invalidate the stated OS-boundary premise. The schedule check(v0), COMMIT(v1), OS-accept(v0) remains a counterexample to separated check-then-send, not to this serialized machine.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Proposed oracle for committed versus uncommitted updates
reasoning_steps.argument: Give every update a stable identifier u. A commit receipt must authenticate u, the policy digest/version, ownership epoch and durable commit position; issue it only after the policy transaction is durable. A linearizable status query through the current, fenced authority can establish COMMITTED(u,c), even if the original receipt was lost. If it reports no commit through a query barrier, that establishes only 'not committed as of this barrier', not 'never delivered' or 'will never commit'. If the authority cannot be queried, classify the update UNKNOWN, not revoked and not proven undelivered. In a controlled history-A test, an independent ingress fault injector can deliberately withhold u before broker delivery and record that action; a subsequent authoritative barrier establishes the corresponding uncommitted prefix. A timeout, client send success, packet capture or wall-clock timestamp alone establishes none of these commit facts.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Proposed independent oracle for the OS-submission boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: For a bounded test, correlate update IDs and immutable envelope IDs with gate-operation ordinals, ownership decisions, durable commit positions, and independently collected host-kernel socket-acceptance events/return lengths. Gate ordinals identify mutually exclusive completed boundary operations; they are not timestamps. For each positive OS acceptance, verify that its operation is authorized by the last preceding committed policy and valid ownership epoch. The independent kernel observation must identify the actual OS socket operation rather than an SDK enqueue or TLS-buffer write. A packet received after COMMIT may belong to an earlier accepted prefix and is not by itself a violation. A write-ahead intent proves neither OS acceptance nor nonacceptance. Missing observations, trace loss, or a crash between acceptance and durable result logging yield UNKNOWN; they must not be counted as a passing test or used to justify replay. This is an oracle design, not a reported measurement.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Reservation invariant remains separate and intact
reasoning_steps.argument: For every applicable campus/user/project/department account k, let B_k be its cap, F_k its covered fixed commitments, S_k its finally settled charges, and r_ak the reserved upper liability for each open attempt a. Maintain L_k=F_k+S_k+sum_a r_ak <= B_k, beginning from a reconciled initial state. A durable atomic reservation across all applicable accounts succeeds only if each resulting inequality holds; concurrent admissions therefore cannot both spend the same headroom. Every potentially billable attempt must have an enforceable aggregate liability bound within its reservation. Final settlement q_ak<=r_ak replaces r_ak by q_ak in S_k, changing L_k by q_ak-r_ak<=0. Certified nondispatch can release unused coverage. Ambiguous charged timeouts, cancellation and uncertain crash outcomes retain coverage until trustworthy settlement or a valid tighter remaining-liability bound. No outstanding liability disappears at a billing-window boundary. These transitions preserve every cap by induction.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Reservation failure cases and coupling to the histories
reasoning_steps.argument: A revocation or DISABLE does not refund liability from an earlier accepted request. A retry that may incur an additional charge needs additional coverage unless verified billing semantics place it inside the existing aggregate bound; transport identifiers alone do not prove charge deduplication. Counterexample: one open attempt reserves the entire cap B and times out ambiguously; releasing B and retrying permits total charges of 2B. Keeping the reservation instead blocks the retry and may sacrifice availability. At B=0 no attempt with positive possible liability is admissible. Provider rejection or cancellation is not automatically certified zero cost. reasoning_assessments.rationale: Accepted as definitions for an explicitly conditional claim, not as campus policy. Durable commit, positive OS acceptance and later delivery are distinct events, and the stated guarantee consistently excludes request-time revocation and recall.

Accepted as the proposed transition rule under the listed premises. Its guards expressly require enforceable ownership, completed recovery, authorization and reservation coverage; administrator unreachability is not a disabling event. Holding the same gate through the OS call supplies the order used by the later proof.

Dropping u before broker delivery changes neither committed policy nor any enabling guard. Therefore the allowed positive acceptance under v0 is a direct trace of the specified machine. A pending request likewise has no effect without an additional barrier.

After the serialized durable commit of v1, each later submission must validate against v1 and is denied for D. Earlier OS-accepted bytes are outside that new-submission prohibition. Losing the receipt does not undo the durable transaction, so a client timeout cannot determine commitment.

The specified UNKNOWN observation occurs before transport admission and leads to DISABLED, which falsifies an explicit submission guard. Replacement admission is correctly conditioned on effective fencing and complete recovery, with no automatic replay of uncertain attempts.

The old-owner trace demonstrates why local belief is insufficient: activating a new owner without fencing leaves the old socket usable. The step correctly identifies this as violation of the ownership premise and narrows any unconditional guarantee to observed disablement. Its stronger result remains conditional on ordering withdrawal against in-flight admission.

For each mediated positive acceptance, the final guard and OS call occupy one policy-excluding interval, so no intervening COMMIT can make the validated policy stale in that order. Partial prefixes and later submissions are treated separately. The induction is valid for finite histories under the explicit mediation, immutable-binding and transport premises.

An authenticated durable receipt or linearizable query can establish commitment despite receipt loss. A negative query establishes only an uncommitted prefix, not nondelivery or permanent noncommitment. The proposed fault injector supplies an additional oracle for controlled nondelivery rather than inferring it from timeout.

The proposed check uses operation ordering plus actual kernel socket acceptance rather than packet arrival or SDK enqueue. It expressly requires correct correlation and treats trace loss and crash ambiguity as UNKNOWN. This is a coherent bounded-test design, not a reported observation or proof of every implementation schedule.

Atomic reservation preserves each account inequality at admission. Replacing r_ak by a trustworthy final q_ak no larger than r_ak changes covered liability by q_ak-r_ak, which is nonpositive. Retaining unresolved liabilities and accounting for fixed commitments closes the stated timeout and billing-window escape paths, conditional on enforceable aggregate bounds and complete spending mediation.

For B greater than zero, an unresolved first attempt can charge B and a separately billable retry can charge another B; releasing coverage merely because of timeout therefore permits 2B liability. Retaining coverage blocks that retry. The zero-cap and cancellation conclusions follow from possible liability rather than optimistic dispatch outcomes.

The supplied peer assumptions support the stated scope distinctions: the budget branch uses matching liability premises, controlled handoff H need not coincide with OS acceptance, and statistical pilot claims do not establish authority enforcement. The Investigator does not import truncated proofs, assert independent confirmation or infer federation failure from the local counterexample.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Scope and the proposed contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Define COMMIT(u,v) as the durable broker transaction that makes policy version v effective for update identifier u. Define release as the positive-length prefix accepted by the OS transport during a synchronous, nonblocking submission operation. An administrator issuing a request, a broker receiving it, a durable intent record, physical packet transmission and recipient delivery are different events. The proposed contract forbids a new OS acceptance disallowed by the policy committed before that acceptance in the broker's serialization order. It does not recall previously accepted bytes or promise timely processing of an administrator request. These definitions narrow the guarantee; campus acceptance is still required.

review.rationale: Accepted as definitions for an explicitly conditional claim, not as campus policy. Durable commit, positive OS acceptance and later delivery are distinct events, and the stated guarantee consistently excludes request-time revocation and recall.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Explicit enabling rule and failure transitions
reasoning_steps.argument: Use broker state (mode, owner_epoch, committed_policy, durable_ledger), with mode initially DISABLED during recovery. FINAL_SUBMIT(a) may enter the transport only if, under the serialization gate: mode=ENABLED; current exclusive ownership is enforceably valid; recovery is complete; the immutable content/destination/identity binding is permitted by committed_policy; classification is unambiguous; and the attempt has sufficient durable reservation coverage. The broker retains the gate through the OS call and result classification. COMMIT uses the same gate. An observed invalid/uncertain ownership result, unrecoverable state ambiguity, or broker shutdown causes DISABLE before any further transport entry. Failure to reach an administrator is not one of these transitions. This is an explicit specification of the intended narrowed rule, not evidence that cycle 2 or MindRouter implements it.

review.rationale: Accepted as the proposed transition rule under the listed premises. Its guards expressly require enforceable ownership, completed recovery, authorization and reservation coverage; administrator unreachability is not a disabling event. Holding the same gate through the OS call supplies the order used by the later proof.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. History A: administrator path fails, broker remains authoritative
reasoning_steps.argument: Initial state A0: broker B is ENABLED in epoch 7; durable v0 permits envelope a to destination D; a has reservation r; B can reach the client and D. A1: administrator X creates update u revoking D, but the request is dropped before B receives it. X observes no commit receipt and eventually a timeout. B observes neither u nor ownership failure; its policy remains v0. A2: B acquires the gate for a, checks the guards against v0, records the required durable intent and invokes the OS adapter while holding the gate. The OS accepts n>0 bytes; this is a permitted release under v0. A3: B releases the gate. Thus administrator unreachability alone does not produce DISABLE. The same release is allowed if u has arrived but remains pending without COMMIT, unless a separate pending-update barrier is specified. Such a barrier is not supplied here.

review.rationale: Dropping u before broker delivery changes neither committed policy nor any enabling guard. Therefore the allowed positive acceptance under v0 is a direct trace of the specified machine. A pending request likewise has no effect without an additional barrier.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. History A continued: a later committed revocation
reasoning_steps.argument: A4: X reconnects and submits u. B acquires the gate, durably commits v1 denying D, and only then issues a commit receipt. A5: an unsent suffix of a, another queued envelope, or a new streaming chunk targeting D obtains the gate after that commit and fails policy validation; no OS submission is made for it. Bytes accepted at A2 may still transmit or arrive after A4. If X loses the receipt after A4, the update is nevertheless committed; X's timeout cannot distinguish this case from A1. Receipt loss is an observation ambiguity, not rollback of policy.

review.rationale: After the serialized durable commit of v1, each later submission must validate against v1 and is denied for D. Earlier OS-accepted bytes are outside that new-submission prohibition. Losing the receipt does not undo the durable transaction, so a client timeout cannot determine commitment.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. History B: observed ownership uncertainty disables submission
reasoning_steps.argument: Initial state B0 equals A0. B1: before a enters the transport, the trusted ownership check returns UNKNOWN, or the broker receives an ownership-invalid event. B2: at the gate, the broker changes ENABLED to DISABLED and rejects FINAL_SUBMIT(a) before any OS call. Observations are the ownership result, the disable transition and the rejected transport entry, not an administrator timeout. B3: a replacement broker must fence the previous epoch at every managed submission path, recover committed policy and unresolved reservations without rollback, and establish exclusive epoch 8 ownership before enabling. If recovered policy is v1, a is denied; if it is v0 and all other guards pass, a may be admitted as a new authorized submission. Recovery does not automatically replay an uncertain old attempt.

review.rationale: The specified UNKNOWN observation occurs before transport admission and leads to DISABLED, which falsifies an explicit submission guard. Replacement admission is correctly conditioned on effective fencing and complete recovery, with no automatic replay of uncertain attempts.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Actual ownership loss is not the same as observing loss
reasoning_steps.argument: If ownership is withdrawn elsewhere while the old broker still reads a cached owner=true and retains a working socket, a local DISABLE transition need not occur. The exact bad schedule is: old broker checks epoch 7; another authority activates epoch 8 without fencing epoch 7; old broker submits using v0. This violates the exclusive-owner premise. Therefore a notification or local Boolean alone is insufficient. A safety claim covering actual ownership loss requires a fence/admission mechanism that orders ownership withdrawal against transport entry: an already admitted operation is ordered before withdrawal, or withdrawal wins and the operation is rejected. No new owner or revocation acknowledgement may rely on the old owner being stopped before that fact is enforced. With this premise absent, the specification guarantees rejection only after observed uncertainty/disable, not after an invisible loss. A dead broker performs no new calls, although its previously accepted OS buffers may still drain.

review.rationale: The old-owner trace demonstrates why local belief is insufficient: activating a new owner without fencing leaves the old socket usable. The step correctly identifies this as violation of the ownership premise and narrows any unconditional guarantee to observed disablement. Its stronger result remains conditional on ordering withdrawal against in-flight admission.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Authorization derivation and its edge cases
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially there are no releases, so the invariant holds. Consider the next positive OS acceptance. Complete mediation places it inside FINAL_SUBMIT. Its gate excludes COMMIT throughout final validation and the OS call, and effective ownership enforcement excludes an invalid owner. Therefore the latest policy in this serialization order is exactly the policy used by the final guard, which permits the immutable binding. COMMIT changes policy but accepts no content. Rejected operations and certified zero-acceptance calls add no release. Induction gives the invariant for every finite history satisfying these transition premises. For partial sends only the accepted prefix is released; every later application submission revalidates the remainder. Streaming, tool calls, logs, caches and embeddings require the same treatment wherever they cross a managed boundary. An independently flushing TLS/application queue would invalidate the stated OS-boundary premise. The schedule check(v0), COMMIT(v1), OS-accept(v0) remains a counterexample to separated check-then-send, not to this serialized machine.

review.rationale: For each mediated positive acceptance, the final guard and OS call occupy one policy-excluding interval, so no intervening COMMIT can make the validated policy stale in that order. Partial prefixes and later submissions are treated separately. The induction is valid for finite histories under the explicit mediation, immutable-binding and transport premises.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Proposed oracle for committed versus uncommitted updates
reasoning_steps.argument: Give every update a stable identifier u. A commit receipt must authenticate u, the policy digest/version, ownership epoch and durable commit position; issue it only after the policy transaction is durable. A linearizable status query through the current, fenced authority can establish COMMITTED(u,c), even if the original receipt was lost. If it reports no commit through a query barrier, that establishes only 'not committed as of this barrier', not 'never delivered' or 'will never commit'. If the authority cannot be queried, classify the update UNKNOWN, not revoked and not proven undelivered. In a controlled history-A test, an independent ingress fault injector can deliberately withhold u before broker delivery and record that action; a subsequent authoritative barrier establishes the corresponding uncommitted prefix. A timeout, client send success, packet capture or wall-clock timestamp alone establishes none of these commit facts.

review.rationale: An authenticated durable receipt or linearizable query can establish commitment despite receipt loss. A negative query establishes only an uncommitted prefix, not nondelivery or permanent noncommitment. The proposed fault injector supplies an additional oracle for controlled nondelivery rather than inferring it from timeout.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Proposed independent oracle for the OS-submission boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: For a bounded test, correlate update IDs and immutable envelope IDs with gate-operation ordinals, ownership decisions, durable commit positions, and independently collected host-kernel socket-acceptance events/return lengths. Gate ordinals identify mutually exclusive completed boundary operations; they are not timestamps. For each positive OS acceptance, verify that its operation is authorized by the last preceding committed policy and valid ownership epoch. The independent kernel observation must identify the actual OS socket operation rather than an SDK enqueue or TLS-buffer write. A packet received after COMMIT may belong to an earlier accepted prefix and is not by itself a violation. A write-ahead intent proves neither OS acceptance nor nonacceptance. Missing observations, trace loss, or a crash between acceptance and durable result logging yield UNKNOWN; they must not be counted as a passing test or used to justify replay. This is an oracle design, not a reported measurement.

review.rationale: The proposed check uses operation ordering plus actual kernel socket acceptance rather than packet arrival or SDK enqueue. It expressly requires correct correlation and treats trace loss and crash ambiguity as UNKNOWN. This is a coherent bounded-test design, not a reported observation or proof of every implementation schedule.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Reservation invariant remains separate and intact
reasoning_steps.argument: For every applicable campus/user/project/department account k, let B_k be its cap, F_k its covered fixed commitments, S_k its finally settled charges, and r_ak the reserved upper liability for each open attempt a. Maintain L_k=F_k+S_k+sum_a r_ak <= B_k, beginning from a reconciled initial state. A durable atomic reservation across all applicable accounts succeeds only if each resulting inequality holds; concurrent admissions therefore cannot both spend the same headroom. Every potentially billable attempt must have an enforceable aggregate liability bound within its reservation. Final settlement q_ak<=r_ak replaces r_ak by q_ak in S_k, changing L_k by q_ak-r_ak<=0. Certified nondispatch can release unused coverage. Ambiguous charged timeouts, cancellation and uncertain crash outcomes retain coverage until trustworthy settlement or a valid tighter remaining-liability bound. No outstanding liability disappears at a billing-window boundary. These transitions preserve every cap by induction.

review.rationale: Atomic reservation preserves each account inequality at admission. Replacing r_ak by a trustworthy final q_ak no larger than r_ak changes covered liability by q_ak-r_ak, which is nonpositive. Retaining unresolved liabilities and accounting for fixed commitments closes the stated timeout and billing-window escape paths, conditional on enforceable aggregate bounds and complete spending mediation.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Reservation failure cases and coupling to the histories
reasoning_steps.argument: A revocation or DISABLE does not refund liability from an earlier accepted request. A retry that may incur an additional charge needs additional coverage unless verified billing semantics place it inside the existing aggregate bound; transport identifiers alone do not prove charge deduplication. Counterexample: one open attempt reserves the entire cap B and times out ambiguously; releasing B and retrying permits total charges of 2B. Keeping the reservation instead blocks the retry and may sacrifice availability. At B=0 no attempt with positive possible liability is admissible. Provider rejection or cancellation is not automatically certified zero cost. Thus history B may stop future submissions while reservations remain occupied, and history A's functioning transport still cannot bypass a failed budget guard.

review.rationale: For B greater than zero, an unresolved first attempt can charge B and a separately billable retry can charge another B; releasing coverage merely because of timeout therefore permits 2B liability. Retaining coverage blocks that retry. The zero-cap and cancellation conclusions follow from possible liability rather than optimistic dispatch outcomes.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Peer compatibility and bounded project contribution
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied extract of 1288a55b-8e0b-4b3c-b8a9-e527cd236c17 motivates checking ambiguous-timeout accounting; the reservation proof above is explicitly rederived rather than accepted from that incomplete source. The extract of 8712830f-b69e-476e-b94d-18be7ea7c043 uses controlled handoff H, which may precede OS acceptance; its conditional handoff result cannot be transferred unchanged to this stricter OS boundary. Adopt its question about effective fencing, but leave implementation unverified. The statistical pilot extract 84d10e8b-baaa-498b-9979-b3fa8425883b does not discharge authority, ownership or transport obligations and is not used as safety evidence. This correction applies to managed paths in any of the four baselines; federation adds partner trust boundaries but is not disproven by this local counterexample. It helps specify a safer comparison with baseline 3, without establishing relative usefulness, costs or administrative burden. Novelty and empirical generality are not assessed.

review.rationale: The supplied peer assumptions support the stated scope distinctions: the budget branch uses matching liability premises, controlled handoff H need not coincide with OS acceptance, and statistical pilot claims do not establish authority enforcement. The Investigator does not import truncated proofs, assert independent confirmation or infer federation failure from the local counterexample.

Withdrawal/fencing and admission have a consistent order, including any in-flight operation; Identity, conservative classification, destination authentication and immutable content/destination bindings are trustworthy; ambiguous classification is denied and all covered content paths are mediated; The transport has no independently flushing application-content queue beyond the declared OS boundary; serialization continues through the synchronous nonblocking OS operation; Committed policy, intents and reservations are durable; recovery cannot roll back acknowledged commits, replay uncertain attempts automatically, or enable before ownership and ledger recovery are complete; All spending within each claimed cap is accounted for, every billable attempt has an enforceable aggregate liability bound, hierarchical reservations are atomic, and settlement evidence is trustworthy. Under the Investigator's listed serialization, ownership-enforcement, mediation, transport, durability and bounded-liability premises, the proposed machine authorizes each new OS acceptance using the latest committed policy and preserves covered hierarchical budget caps. Steps 10–11 preserve budget caps through atomic reservation and nonincreasing settlement, while retaining liability after ambiguous outcomes. Step 12 correctly limits transfer from peer results and avoids a deployment or federation-benefit claim.

solution_review.argument_summary: Cycle 3 steps 1–6 distinguish administrator request, durable commit, ownership failure and OS acceptance using two explicit histories. Step 7 proves authorization by induction because the final guard and OS operation exclude policy mutation. Steps 8–9 specify separate commitment and OS-boundary observation oracles, retaining UNKNOWN for missing evidence. argument_steps.title: 1. Scope and the proposed contract
argument_steps.argument: Define COMMIT(u,v) as the durable broker transaction that makes policy version v effective for update identifier u. Define release as the positive-length prefix accepted by the OS transport during a synchronous, nonblocking submission operation. An administrator issuing a request, a broker receiving it, a durable intent record, physical packet transmission and recipient delivery are different events. The proposed contract forbids a new OS acceptance disallowed by the policy committed before that acceptance in the broker's serialization order. It does not recall previously accepted bytes or promise timely processing of an administrator request. These definitions narrow the guarantee; campus acceptance is still required.

review.rationale: Accepted as definitions for an explicitly conditional claim, not as campus policy. Durable commit, positive OS acceptance and later delivery are distinct events, and the stated guarantee consistently excludes request-time revocation and recall.

argument_steps.title: 2. Explicit enabling rule and failure transitions
argument_steps.argument: Use broker state (mode, owner_epoch, committed_policy, durable_ledger), with mode initially DISABLED during recovery. FINAL_SUBMIT(a) may enter the transport only if, under the serialization gate: mode=ENABLED; current exclusive ownership is enforceably valid; recovery is complete; the immutable content/destination/identity binding is permitted by committed_policy; classification is unambiguous; and the attempt has sufficient durable reservation coverage. The broker retains the gate through the OS call and result classification. COMMIT uses the same gate. An observed invalid/uncertain ownership result, unrecoverable state ambiguity, or broker shutdown causes DISABLE before any further transport entry. Failure to reach an administrator is not one of these transitions. This is an explicit specification of the intended narrowed rule, not evidence that cycle 2 or MindRouter implements it.

review.rationale: Accepted as the proposed transition rule under the listed premises. Its guards expressly require enforceable ownership, completed recovery, authorization and reservation coverage; administrator unreachability is not a disabling event. Holding the same gate through the OS call supplies the order used by the later proof.

argument_steps.title: 3. History A: administrator path fails, broker remains authoritative
argument_steps.argument: Initial state A0: broker B is ENABLED in epoch 7; durable v0 permits envelope a to destination D; a has reservation r; B can reach the client and D. A1: administrator X creates update u revoking D, but the request is dropped before B receives it. X observes no commit receipt and eventually a timeout. B observes neither u nor ownership failure; its policy remains v0. A2: B acquires the gate for a, checks the guards against v0, records the required durable intent and invokes the OS adapter while holding the gate. The OS accepts n>0 bytes; this is a permitted release under v0. A3: B releases the gate. Thus administrator unreachability alone does not produce DISABLE. The same release is allowed if u has arrived but remains pending without COMMIT, unless a separate pending-update barrier is specified. Such a barrier is not supplied here.

review.rationale: Dropping u before broker delivery changes neither committed policy nor any enabling guard. Therefore the allowed positive acceptance under v0 is a direct trace of the specified machine. A pending request likewise has no effect without an additional barrier.

argument_steps.title: 4. History A continued: a later committed revocation
argument_steps.argument: A4: X reconnects and submits u. B acquires the gate, durably commits v1 denying D, and only then issues a commit receipt. A5: an unsent suffix of a, another queued envelope, or a new streaming chunk targeting D obtains the gate after that commit and fails policy validation; no OS submission is made for it. Bytes accepted at A2 may still transmit or arrive after A4. If X loses the receipt after A4, the update is nevertheless committed; X's timeout cannot distinguish this case from A1. Receipt loss is an observation ambiguity, not rollback of policy.

review.rationale: After the serialized durable commit of v1, each later submission must validate against v1 and is denied for D. Earlier OS-accepted bytes are outside that new-submission prohibition. Losing the receipt does not undo the durable transaction, so a client timeout cannot determine commitment.

argument_steps.title: 5. History B: observed ownership uncertainty disables submission
argument_steps.argument: Initial state B0 equals A0. B1: before a enters the transport, the trusted ownership check returns UNKNOWN, or the broker receives an ownership-invalid event. B2: at the gate, the broker changes ENABLED to DISABLED and rejects FINAL_SUBMIT(a) before any OS call. Observations are the ownership result, the disable transition and the rejected transport entry, not an administrator timeout. B3: a replacement broker must fence the previous epoch at every managed submission path, recover committed policy and unresolved reservations without rollback, and establish exclusive epoch 8 ownership before enabling. If recovered policy is v1, a is denied; if it is v0 and all other guards pass, a may be admitted as a new authorized submission. Recovery does not automatically replay an uncertain old attempt.

review.rationale: The specified UNKNOWN observation occurs before transport admission and leads to DISABLED, which falsifies an explicit submission guard. Replacement admission is correctly conditioned on effective fencing and complete recovery, with no automatic replay of uncertain attempts.

argument_steps.title: 6. Actual ownership loss is not the same as observing loss
argument_steps.argument: If ownership is withdrawn elsewhere while the old broker still reads a cached owner=true and retains a working socket, a local DISABLE transition need not occur. The exact bad schedule is: old broker checks epoch 7; another authority activates epoch 8 without fencing epoch 7; old broker submits using v0. This violates the exclusive-owner premise. Therefore a notification or local Boolean alone is insufficient. A safety claim covering actual ownership loss requires a fence/admission mechanism that orders ownership withdrawal against transport entry: an already admitted operation is ordered before withdrawal, or withdrawal wins and the operation is rejected. No new owner or revocation acknowledgement may rely on the old owner being stopped before that fact is enforced. With this premise absent, the specification guarantees rejection only after observed uncertainty/disable, not after an invisible loss. A dead broker performs no new calls, although its previously accepted OS buffers may still drain.

review.rationale: The old-owner trace demonstrates why local belief is insufficient: activating a new owner without fencing leaves the old socket usable. The step correctly identifies this as violation of the ownership premise and narrows any unconditional guarantee to observed disablement. Its stronger result remains conditional on ordering withdrawal against in-flight admission.

argument_steps.title: 7. Authorization derivation and its edge cases
argument_steps.argument: Initially there are no releases, so the invariant holds. Consider the next positive OS acceptance. Complete mediation places it inside FINAL_SUBMIT. Its gate excludes COMMIT throughout final validation and the OS call, and effective ownership enforcement excludes an invalid owner. Therefore the latest policy in this serialization order is exactly the policy used by the final guard, which permits the immutable binding. COMMIT changes policy but accepts no content. Rejected operations and certified zero-acceptance calls add no release. Induction gives the invariant for every finite history satisfying these transition premises. For partial sends only the accepted prefix is released; every later application submission revalidates the remainder. Streaming, tool calls, logs, caches and embeddings require the same treatment wherever they cross a managed boundary. An independently flushing TLS/application queue would invalidate the stated OS-boundary premise. The schedule check(v0), COMMIT(v1), OS-accept(v0) remains a counterexample to separated check-then-send, not to this serialized machine.

review.rationale: For each mediated positive acceptance, the final guard and OS call occupy one policy-excluding interval, so no intervening COMMIT can make the validated policy stale in that order. Partial prefixes and later submissions are treated separately. The induction is valid for finite histories under the explicit mediation, immutable-binding and transport premises.

argument_steps.title: 8. Proposed oracle for committed versus uncommitted updates
argument_steps.argument: Give every update a stable identifier u. A commit receipt must authenticate u, the policy digest/version, ownership epoch and durable commit position; issue it only after the policy transaction is durable. A linearizable status query through the current, fenced authority can establish COMMITTED(u,c), even if the original receipt was lost. If it reports no commit through a query barrier, that establishes only 'not committed as of this barrier', not 'never delivered' or 'will never commit'. If the authority cannot be queried, classify the update UNKNOWN, not revoked and not proven undelivered. In a controlled history-A test, an independent ingress fault injector can deliberately withhold u before broker delivery and record that action; a subsequent authoritative barrier establishes the corresponding uncommitted prefix. A timeout, client send success, packet capture or wall-clock timestamp alone establishes none of these commit facts.

review.rationale: An authenticated durable receipt or linearizable query can establish commitment despite receipt loss. A negative query establishes only an uncommitted prefix, not nondelivery or permanent noncommitment. The proposed fault injector supplies an additional oracle for controlled nondelivery rather than inferring it from timeout.

argument_steps.title: 9. Proposed independent oracle for the OS-submission boundary
argument_steps.argument: For a bounded test, correlate update IDs and immutable envelope IDs with gate-operation ordinals, ownership decisions, durable commit positions, and independently collected host-kernel socket-acceptance events/return lengths. Gate ordinals identify mutually exclusive completed boundary operations; they are not timestamps. For each positive OS acceptance, verify that its operation is authorized by the last preceding committed policy and valid ownership epoch. The independent kernel observation must identify the actual OS socket operation rather than an SDK enqueue or TLS-buffer write. A packet received after COMMIT may belong to an earlier accepted prefix and is not by itself a violation. A write-ahead intent proves neither OS acceptance nor nonacceptance. Missing observations, trace loss, or a crash between acceptance and durable result logging yield UNKNOWN; they must not be counted as a passing test or used to justify replay. This is an oracle design, not a reported measurement.

review.rationale: The proposed check uses operation ordering plus actual kernel socket acceptance rather than packet arrival or SDK enqueue. It expressly requires correct correlation and treats trace loss and crash ambiguity as UNKNOWN. This is a coherent bounded-test design, not a reported observation or proof of every implementation schedule.

argument_steps.title: 10. Reservation invariant remains separate and intact
argument_steps.argument: For every applicable campus/user/project/department account k, let B_k be its cap, F_k its covered fixed commitments, S_k its finally settled charges, and r_ak the reserved upper liability for each open attempt a. Maintain L_k=F_k+S_k+sum_a r_ak <= B_k, beginning from a reconciled initial state. A durable atomic reservation across all applicable accounts succeeds only if each resulting inequality holds; concurrent admissions therefore cannot both spend the same headroom. Every potentially billable attempt must have an enforceable aggregate liability bound within its reservation. Final settlement q_ak<=r_ak replaces r_ak by q_ak in S_k, changing L_k by q_ak-r_ak<=0. Certified nondispatch can release unused coverage. Ambiguous charged timeouts, cancellation and uncertain crash outcomes retain coverage until trustworthy settlement or a valid tighter remaining-liability bound. No outstanding liability disappears at a billing-window boundary. These transitions preserve every cap by induction.

review.rationale: Atomic reservation preserves each account inequality at admission. Replacing r_ak by a trustworthy final q_ak no larger than r_ak changes covered liability by q_ak-r_ak, which is nonpositive. Retaining unresolved liabilities and accounting for fixed commitments closes the stated timeout and billing-window escape paths, conditional on enforceable aggregate bounds and complete spending mediation.

argument_steps.title: 11. Reservation failure cases and coupling to the histories
argument_steps.argument: A revocation or DISABLE does not refund liability from an earlier accepted request. A retry that may incur an additional charge needs additional coverage unless verified billing semantics place it inside the existing aggregate bound; transport identifiers alone do not prove charge deduplication. Counterexample: one open attempt reserves the entire cap B and times out ambiguously; releasing B and retrying permits total charges of 2B. Keeping the reservation instead blocks the retry and may sacrifice availability. At B=0 no attempt with positive possible liability is admissible. Provider rejection or cancellation is not automatically certified zero cost. Thus history B may stop future submissions while reservations remain occupied, and history A's functioning transport still cannot bypass a failed budget guard.

review.rationale: For B greater than zero, an unresolved first attempt can charge B and a separately billable retry can charge another B; releasing coverage merely because of timeout therefore permits 2B liability. Retaining coverage blocks that retry. The zero-cap and cancellation conclusions follow from possible liability rather than optimistic dispatch outcomes.

argument_steps.title: 12. Peer compatibility and bounded project contribution
argument_steps.argument: The supplied extract of 1288a55b-8e0b-4b3c-b8a9-e527cd236c17 motivates checking ambiguous-timeout accounting; the reservation proof above is explicitly rederived rather than accepted from that incomplete source. The extract of 8712830f-b69e-476e-b94d-18be7ea7c043 uses controlled handoff H, which may precede OS acceptance; its conditional handoff result cannot be transferred unchanged to this stricter OS boundary. Adopt its question about effective fencing, but leave implementation unverified. The statistical pilot extract 84d10e8b-baaa-498b-9979-b3fa8425883b does not discharge authority, ownership or transport obligations and is not used as safety evidence. This correction applies to managed paths in any of the four baselines; federation adds partner trust boundaries but is not disproven by this local counterexample. It helps specify a safer comparison with baseline 3, without establishing relative usefulness, costs or administrative burden. Novelty and empirical generality are not assessed.

The Investigator does not import truncated proofs, assert independent confirmation or infer federation failure from the local counterexample.

strategy_findings.claim: Conditional on: The formal contract defines effective revocation at durable broker commit and release at positive OS transport acceptance; campus approval of that contract is not presumed; One trusted serialization mechanism orders all covered policy commits and managed OS submission operations; no other authority makes a newer covered policy effective outside that order; Exclusive ownership is enforced at submission admission, not inferred solely from a cached ownership flag. Withdrawal/fencing and admission have a consistent order, including any in-flight operation; Identity, conservative classification, destination authentication and immutable content/destination bindings are trustworthy; ambiguous classification is denied and all covered content paths are mediated; The transport has no independently flushing application-content queue beyond the declared OS boundary; serialization continues through the synchronous nonblocking OS operation; Committed policy, intents and reservations are durable; recovery cannot roll back acknowledged commits, replay uncertain attempts automatically, or enable before ownership and ledger recovery are complete; All spending within each claimed cap is accounted for, every billable attempt has an enforceable aggregate liability bound, hierarchical reservations are atomic, and settlement evidence is trustworthy. Under the Investigator's listed serialization, ownership-enforcement, mediation, transport, durability and bounded-liability premises, the proposed machine authorizes each new OS acceptance using the latest committed policy and preserves covered hierarchical budget caps. Administrator-path loss alone does not disable submission; observed uncertainty or effectively enforced ownership loss does. This is a conditional specification result, not evidence that MindRouter or a federation implements it.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Scope and the proposed contract
reasoning_steps.argument: Define COMMIT(u,v) as the durable broker transaction that makes policy version v effective for update identifier u. Define release as the positive-length prefix accepted by the OS transport during a synchronous, nonblocking submission operation. An administrator issuing a request, a broker receiving it, a durable intent record, physical packet transmission and recipient delivery are different events. The proposed contract forbids a new OS acceptance disallowed by the policy committed before that acceptance in the broker's serialization order. It does not recall previously accepted bytes or promise timely processing of an administrator request. These definitions narrow the guarantee; campus acceptance is still required.

review.rationale: Accepted as definitions for an explicitly conditional claim, not as campus policy. Durable commit, positive OS acceptance and later delivery are distinct events, and the stated guarantee consistently excludes request-time revocation and recall.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Explicit enabling rule and failure transitions
reasoning_steps.argument: Use broker state (mode, owner_epoch, committed_policy, durable_ledger), with mode initially DISABLED during recovery. FINAL_SUBMIT(a) may enter the transport only if, under the serialization gate: mode=ENABLED; current exclusive ownership is enforceably valid; recovery is complete; the immutable content/destination/identity binding is permitted by committed_policy; classification is unambiguous; and the attempt has sufficient durable reservation coverage. The broker retains the gate through the OS call and result classification. COMMIT uses the same gate. An observed invalid/uncertain ownership result, unrecoverable state ambiguity, or broker shutdown causes DISABLE before any further transport entry. Failure to reach an administrator is not one of these transitions. This is an explicit specification of the intended narrowed rule, not evidence that cycle 2 or MindRouter implements it.

review.rationale: Accepted as the proposed transition rule under the listed premises. Its guards expressly require enforceable ownership, completed recovery, authorization and reservation coverage; administrator unreachability is not a disabling event. Holding the same gate through the OS call supplies the order used by the later proof.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. History A: administrator path fails, broker remains authoritative
reasoning_steps.argument: Initial state A0: broker B is ENABLED in epoch 7; durable v0 permits envelope a to destination D; a has reservation r; B can reach the client and D. A1: administrator X creates update u revoking D, but the request is dropped before B receives it. X observes no commit receipt and eventually a timeout. B observes neither u nor ownership failure; its policy remains v0. A2: B acquires the gate for a, checks the guards against v0, records the required durable intent and invokes the OS adapter while holding the gate. The OS accepts n>0 bytes; this is a permitted release under v0. A3: B releases the gate. Thus administrator unreachability alone does not produce DISABLE. The same release is allowed if u has arrived but remains pending without COMMIT, unless a separate pending-update barrier is specified. Such a barrier is not supplied here.

review.rationale: Dropping u before broker delivery changes neither committed policy nor any enabling guard. Therefore the allowed positive acceptance under v0 is a direct trace of the specified machine. A pending request likewise has no effect without an additional barrier.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. History A continued: a later committed revocation
reasoning_steps.argument: A4: X reconnects and submits u. B acquires the gate, durably commits v1 denying D, and only then issues a commit receipt. A5: an unsent suffix of a, another queued envelope, or a new streaming chunk targeting D obtains the gate after that commit and fails policy validation; no OS submission is made for it. Bytes accepted at A2 may still transmit or arrive after A4. If X loses the receipt after A4, the update is nevertheless committed; X's timeout cannot distinguish this case from A1. Receipt loss is an observation ambiguity, not rollback of policy.

review.rationale: After the serialized durable commit of v1, each later submission must validate against v1 and is denied for D. Earlier OS-accepted bytes are outside that new-submission prohibition. Losing the receipt does not undo the durable transaction, so a client timeout cannot determine commitment.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. History B: observed ownership uncertainty disables submission
reasoning_steps.argument: Initial state B0 equals A0. B1: before a enters the transport, the trusted ownership check returns UNKNOWN, or the broker receives an ownership-invalid event. B2: at the gate, the broker changes ENABLED to DISABLED and rejects FINAL_SUBMIT(a) before any OS call. Observations are the ownership result, the disable transition and the rejected transport entry, not an administrator timeout. B3: a replacement broker must fence the previous epoch at every managed submission path, recover committed policy and unresolved reservations without rollback, and establish exclusive epoch 8 ownership before enabling. If recovered policy is v1, a is denied; if it is v0 and all other guards pass, a may be admitted as a new authorized submission. Recovery does not automatically replay an uncertain old attempt.

review.rationale: The specified UNKNOWN observation occurs before transport admission and leads to DISABLED, which falsifies an explicit submission guard. Replacement admission is correctly conditioned on effective fencing and complete recovery, with no automatic replay of uncertain attempts.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Actual ownership loss is not the same as observing loss
reasoning_steps.argument: If ownership is withdrawn elsewhere while the old broker still reads a cached owner=true and retains a working socket, a local DISABLE transition need not occur. The exact bad schedule is: old broker checks epoch 7; another authority activates epoch 8 without fencing epoch 7; old broker submits using v0. This violates the exclusive-owner premise. Therefore a notification or local Boolean alone is insufficient. A safety claim covering actual ownership loss requires a fence/admission mechanism that orders ownership withdrawal against transport entry: an already admitted operation is ordered before withdrawal, or withdrawal wins and the operation is rejected. No new owner or revocation acknowledgement may rely on the old owner being stopped before that fact is enforced. With this premise absent, the specification guarantees rejection only after observed uncertainty/disable, not after an invisible loss. A dead broker performs no new calls, although its previously accepted OS buffers may still drain.

review.rationale: The old-owner trace demonstrates why local belief is insufficient: activating a new owner without fencing leaves the old socket usable. The step correctly identifies this as violation of the ownership premise and narrows any unconditional guarantee to observed disablement. Its stronger result remains conditional on ordering withdrawal against in-flight admission.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Authorization derivation and its edge cases
reasoning_steps.argument: Initially there are no releases, so the invariant holds. Consider the next positive OS acceptance. Complete mediation places it inside FINAL_SUBMIT. Its gate excludes COMMIT throughout final validation and the OS call, and effective ownership enforcement excludes an invalid owner. Therefore the latest policy in this serialization order is exactly the policy used by the final guard, which permits the immutable binding. COMMIT changes policy but accepts no content. Rejected operations and certified zero-acceptance calls add no release. Induction gives the invariant for every finite history satisfying these transition premises. For partial sends only the accepted prefix is released; every later application submission revalidates the remainder. Streaming, tool calls, logs, caches and embeddings require the same treatment wherever they cross a managed boundary. An independently flushing TLS/application queue would invalidate the stated OS-boundary premise. The schedule check(v0), COMMIT(v1), OS-accept(v0) remains a counterexample to separated check-then-send, not to this serialized machine.

review.rationale: For each mediated positive acceptance, the final guard and OS call occupy one policy-excluding interval, so no intervening COMMIT can make the validated policy stale in that order. Partial prefixes and later submissions are treated separately. The induction is valid for finite histories under the explicit mediation, immutable-binding and transport premises.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. Proposed oracle for committed versus uncommitted updates
reasoning_steps.argument: Give every update a stable identifier u. A commit receipt must authenticate u, the policy digest/version, ownership epoch and durable commit position; issue it only after the policy transaction is durable. A linearizable status query through the current, fenced authority can establish COMMITTED(u,c), even if the original receipt was lost. If it reports no commit through a query barrier, that establishes only 'not committed as of this barrier', not 'never delivered' or 'will never commit'. If the authority cannot be queried, classify the update UNKNOWN, not revoked and not proven undelivered. In a controlled history-A test, an independent ingress fault injector can deliberately withhold u before broker delivery and record that action; a subsequent authoritative barrier establishes the corresponding uncommitted prefix. A timeout, client send success, packet capture or wall-clock timestamp alone establishes none of these commit facts.

review.rationale: An authenticated durable receipt or linearizable query can establish commitment despite receipt loss. A negative query establishes only an uncommitted prefix, not nondelivery or permanent noncommitment. The proposed fault injector supplies an additional oracle for controlled nondelivery rather than inferring it from timeout.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Proposed independent oracle for the OS-submission boundary
reasoning_steps.argument: For a bounded test, correlate update IDs and immutable envelope IDs with gate-operation ordinals, ownership decisions, durable commit positions, and independently collected host-kernel socket-acceptance events/return lengths. Gate ordinals identify mutually exclusive completed boundary operations; they are not timestamps. For each positive OS acceptance, verify that its operation is authorized by the last preceding committed policy and valid ownership epoch. The independent kernel observation must identify the actual OS socket operation rather than an SDK enqueue or TLS-buffer write. A packet received after COMMIT may belong to an earlier accepted prefix and is not by itself a violation. A write-ahead intent proves neither OS acceptance nor nonacceptance. Missing observations, trace loss, or a crash between acceptance and durable result logging yield UNKNOWN; they must not be counted as a passing test or used to justify replay. This is an oracle design, not a reported measurement.

review.rationale: The proposed check uses operation ordering plus actual kernel socket acceptance rather than packet arrival or SDK enqueue. It expressly requires correct correlation and treats trace loss and crash ambiguity as UNKNOWN. This is a coherent bounded-test design, not a reported observation or proof of every implementation schedule.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Reservation invariant remains separate and intact
reasoning_steps.argument: For every applicable campus/user/project/department account k, let B_k be its cap, F_k its covered fixed commitments, S_k its finally settled charges, and r_ak the reserved upper liability for each open attempt a. Maintain L_k=F_k+S_k+sum_a r_ak <= B_k, beginning from a reconciled initial state. A durable atomic reservation across all applicable accounts succeeds only if each resulting inequality holds; concurrent admissions therefore cannot both spend the same headroom. Every potentially billable attempt must have an enforceable aggregate liability bound within its reservation. Final settlement q_ak<=r_ak replaces r_ak by q_ak in S_k, changing L_k by q_ak-r_ak<=0. Certified nondispatch can release unused coverage. Ambiguous charged timeouts, cancellation and uncertain crash outcomes retain coverage until trustworthy settlement or a valid tighter remaining-liability bound. No outstanding liability disappears at a billing-window boundary. These transitions preserve every cap by induction.

review.rationale: Atomic reservation preserves each account inequality at admission. Replacing r_ak by a trustworthy final q_ak no larger than r_ak changes covered liability by q_ak-r_ak, which is nonpositive. Retaining unresolved liabilities and accounting for fixed commitments closes the stated timeout and billing-window escape paths, conditional on enforceable aggregate bounds and complete spending mediation.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Reservation failure cases and coupling to the histories
reasoning_steps.argument: A revocation or DISABLE does not refund liability from an earlier accepted request. A retry that may incur an additional charge needs additional coverage unless verified billing semantics place it inside the existing aggregate bound; transport identifiers alone do not prove charge deduplication. Counterexample: one open attempt reserves the entire cap B and times out ambiguously; releasing B and retrying permits total charges of 2B. Keeping the reservation instead blocks the retry and may sacrifice availability. At B=0 no attempt with positive possible liability is admissible. Provider rejection or cancellation is not automatically certified zero cost. Thus history B may stop future submissions while reservations remain occupied, and history A's functioning transport still cannot bypass a failed budget guard.

review.rationale: For B greater than zero, an unresolved first attempt can charge B and a separately billable retry can charge another B; releasing coverage merely because of timeout therefore permits 2B liability. Retaining coverage blocks that retry. The zero-cap and cancellation conclusions follow from possible liability rather than optimistic dispatch outcomes.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Peer compatibility and bounded project contribution
reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied extract of 1288a55b-8e0b-4b3c-b8a9-e527cd236c17 motivates checking ambiguous-timeout accounting; the reservation proof above is explicitly rederived rather than accepted from that incomplete source. The extract of 8712830f-b69e-476e-b94d-18be7ea7c043 uses controlled handoff H, which may precede OS acceptance; its conditional handoff result cannot be transferred unchanged to this stricter OS boundary. Adopt its question about effective fencing, but leave implementation unverified. The statistical pilot extract 84d10e8b-baaa-498b-9979-b3fa8425883b does not discharge authority, ownership or transport obligations and is not used as safety evidence. This correction applies to managed paths in any of the four baselines; federation adds partner trust boundaries but is not disproven by this local counterexample. It helps specify a safer comparison with baseline 3, without establishing relative usefulness, costs or administrative burden. Novelty and empirical generality are not assessed.

review.rationale: The supplied peer assumptions support the stated scope distinctions: the budget branch uses matching liability premises, controlled handoff H need not coincide with OS acceptance, and statistical pilot claims do not establish authority enforcement. The Investigator does not import truncated proofs, assert independent confirmation or infer federation failure from the local counterexample.
