strategy_findings.claim: Conditional on: For the statistical guarantee, paired episode vectors are independent identically distributed draws from a prespecified target task/load mixture, or the analysis uses genuinely independent fixed-size reset blocks as its units; Outcomes, episode enrollment, deadlines, rubrics, multiplicity allocation and the final sample size are fixed before confirmatory outcomes are inspected; missing adjudication counts as failure and favorable optional stopping is prohibited; For economic certification only, all covered costs use a common declared demand scale, nonnegative enforceable bounds M_F and M_B, conservative treatment of unresolved liability, approved fixed-cost allocations and a known positive baseline mean cost; Both service variants can be evaluated within approved domains without unsafe replication or interference invalidating their paired comparison; The proposed numerical gates are adopted only as provisional pilot decision criteria; they are not asserted to be existing university policy or accepted deployment thresholds. Conditional on the Investigator’s listed sampling, preregistration, bounded-cost, approved-domain and provisional-governance assumptions, the fixed-sample confidence construction controls false statistical certification for the probability gates and for economic contrasts formed from exact settled costs. The stated extension to conservatively estimated unresolved costs is not yet justified. No comparative winner, deployment safety or economic advantage has been established.

reasoning_steps.title: 1. Fix the estimand before admissions or routing
reasoning_steps.argument: Define the target population as legitimate research task episodes offered by authenticated pilot users under a prespecified campus/task/load distribution. An episode is one requested useful deliverable, not one model call: an agent workflow and a reproducible batch each retain one episode identifier through all calls, retries and terminal outcomes. Sample episodes before either service admits them. Let B denote baseline 3 and F the hypothetical federation extension, with the same external-access approvals and budget scenario. Baselines 1 and 2 use the same episode definitions, but selecting a winner among all four would require an additional multiplicity plan. The confirmatory comparison here is only F versus B.

review.rationale: Sampling before service admission fixes a common offered-demand population and prevents service-specific selection from defining the estimand. Restricting confirmation to F versus baseline 3 correctly avoids claiming a four-way winner under a two-service multiplicity plan.

reasoning_steps.title: 2. Count refusals without rewarding unsafe behavior
reasoning_steps.argument: For service s and sampled episode i, set Y_si=1 only if the requested deliverable meets the frozen task-quality rubric, finishes within its task-specific end-to-end deadline, supplies required provenance/version information, and follows approved handling rules. Otherwise set Y_si=0. The denominator N includes policy refusals, ambiguous-classification refusals, no-fit jobs, budget exhaustion, overload, outage, provider rejection, deadline expiry, cancellation after enrollment and missing quality adjudication. An appropriate refusal is a safety success but not a useful completion. A late result remains a completion failure. Retries never create new denominator entries. Exclude malformed/nonresearch traffic only through prespecified, outcome-blind eligibility rules; malicious synthetic probes belong in a separate safety suite. Report refusal reasons and both offered-demand and admitted-only rates, but do not substitute the admitted-only rate for the primary outcome.

review.rationale: The binary outcome requires quality, deadline, provenance and approved handling jointly. Retaining refusals, failures, enrolled cancellations and missing adjudication in the denominator prevents admission filtering and retries from inflating useful completion.

reasoning_steps.title: 3. Separate demand coverage from positive-control safety tests
reasoning_steps.argument: Use p_s=E[Y_si] as useful-completion coverage of offered legitimate demand. Restricted or ambiguous legitimate requests remain represented even when refusal is mandatory; this reveals that a service may be safe yet unable to cover the campus’s needs. Report externally eligible and local-only strata as secondary diagnostics rather than redefining the primary denominator after observing results. Synthetic forbidden-egress tests have no legitimate deliverable and are not mixed into p_s. A counterexample to admitted-only reporting is a service that completes 10 easy tasks and refuses 90 difficult ones: admitted completion is 100%, but offered-demand useful completion is 10%. Neither denominator licenses relaxing policy.

review.rationale: The explicit 10-success/90-refusal example independently establishes the difference between admitted-only performance and offered-demand coverage. Separating forbidden-egress probes from legitimate deliverables avoids conflating safety testing with service usefulness.

reasoning_steps.title: 4. Specify the sampling assumptions and pairing controls
reasoning_steps.argument: For the finite-sample bounds below, the N paired vectors must be independent and identically distributed draws from the prespecified target mixture. Each vector contains B and F outcomes for the same task and comparable load condition; dependence within a pair is allowed. Use authorized task copies, blinded assessors and randomized execution order, with isolated/reset budget and queue state where replay is valid. Do not duplicate sensitive work to an unapproved destination merely to form a pair. Shared queues, monthly budget depletion and repeated tasks from the same researcher generally violate episode-level independence. In those cases use independent reset load blocks as sampling units, with a fixed number of enrolled tasks per block, or design a cluster/randomized-period analysis before collection. Bounds on block averages remain valid, but N then means independent blocks, not calls or tasks. Unavailable independent replication makes inference inconclusive rather than permitting an invented effective sample size.

review.rationale: Accepted only as the explicitly conditional sampling premise. Within-pair dependence is compatible with independent paired vectors; genuinely independent fixed-size block averages are also bounded variables. The step correctly excludes ordinary shared-state episodes from an unsupported independence claim.

reasoning_steps.title: 5. Define costs at a common service scale
reasoning_steps.argument: Let c_si be nonnegative cost per offered episode at a declared common annual demand and accounting perspective. Include costs of failed episodes, all billable subcalls and permitted retries, idle capacity, staffing and federation administration. Allocate fixed annual costs over the declared annual offered demand, not over observed successes; keep sunk, incremental and fully loaded analyses separate. Define mu_s=E[c_si], and cost per useful task q_s=mu_s/p_s for p_s>0. The primary economic comparison uses fully loaded cost; repeat incremental analysis as a sensitivity, not a replacement. Cost certification below additionally requires enforceable bounds 0≤c_si≤M_s, settled charges or conservative liability bounds, and a known positive baseline cost floor. Unknown fixed allocations require declared uncertainty ranges; an economic go must survive their approved adverse values. An unsettled charged timeout is not zero cost. No prices, costs or workload observations are supplied here.

review.rationale: The common-demand cost allocation and ratio-of-means estimand are coherent for actual costs. The alternative allowing conservative liability bounds is insufficiently specified to support certification of actual economic cost.
review.objection: Upper bounds on baseline costs are not conservative when those costs later enter the economic contrast negatively. Require settled costs, a clearly labeled liability-surrogate estimand, or signed propagation of lower and upper cost bounds.

reasoning_steps.title: 6. Construct the paired coverage and economic contrasts
reasoning_steps.argument: Let D_i=Y_Fi−Y_Bi, so D_i lies in [−1,1] and Delta=E[D_i]=p_F−p_B. The coverage hurdle is Delta≥0.10. For the economic hurdle q_F/q_B≤0.80, positive denominators give the equivalent inequality K=mu_F p_B−0.80 mu_B p_F≤0. A mean of per-episode cost/success ratios is undefined on failures and is not this estimand. To estimate K without assuming cost and success are independent within a task, partition the N independent pairs into m=floor(N/2) disjoint two-task blocks (i,j), fixed before outcomes. Define Z=(c_Fi Y_Bj+c_Fj Y_Bi−0.80 c_Bi Y_Fj−0.80 c_Bj Y_Fi)/2. Cross-task independence gives E[Z]=K, while arbitrary within-task dependence is retained. Each Z lies in [−0.80 M_B,M_F], and disjoint blocks are independent. Using only these disjoint products sacrifices precision but makes a finite-sample paired rule transparent.

review.rationale: For exact costs and positive denominators, multiplying q_F/q_B≤0.80 gives the stated K inequality. Cross-task independence makes each product’s expectation a product of means without requiring within-task independence. Averaging two terms preserves the stated range, and disjoint task blocks preserve independence.

reasoning_steps.title: 7. Give one simultaneous confidence rule
reasoning_steps.argument: Use one fixed final analysis with family error alpha=0.05. Form two-sided intervals for four quantities: p_F, p_B, Delta and K. Hoeffding’s bounded-variable inequality gives P(|mean−expectation|>w sqrt(log(160)/(2n)))≤0.0125 for range width w, since 2 exp(−2n r²/w²)=0.0125. A union bound therefore gives simultaneous coverage at least 95%, without independence among the four intervals. Write a=sqrt(log(160)/(2N)). The intervals are p_s: mean(Y_s)±a; Delta: mean(D)±2a; K: mean(Z)±(M_F+0.80M_B)sqrt(log(160)/(2m)). Clip probability intervals to [0,1] and the Delta interval to [−1,1]. Denote endpoints L and U. This is deliberately conservative, distribution-free under the listed assumptions, and valid for the prespecified OR between the two benefit pathways.

review.rationale: For each exact bounded mean, the radius gives two-tail error 2 exp(−log(160))=0.0125. Four such errors sum to 0.05, regardless of dependence among intervals. Probability and difference clipping do not reduce coverage.

reasoning_steps.title: 8. State the provisional statistical go rule
reasoning_steps.argument: After all nonstatistical gates pass, require L_pF≥0.90 and either (A) L_Delta≥0.10, or (B) U_K≤0 together with L_Delta≥−0.02. The −2-point completion noninferiority margin is an additional provisional safeguard: lower cost must not hide a materially less useful service. Path B also requires L_pB>0 and a known positive mu_B, so the baseline cost-per-useful-task ratio is meaningful. On the simultaneous-coverage event, each certified inequality holds for its population parameter. Thus a statistical go with any false required parameter inequality can occur only outside that event, with probability at most 5%. This controls statistical false-go risk, not policy, contract, implementation or safety risk. At an exact hurdle, high probability of certification should not be expected; power requires a real margin beyond it.

review.rationale: The simultaneous-event argument correctly controls false certification for exact-cost K and the probability inequalities, including the prespecified OR. It does not cover the settlement bias permitted in step 5.
review.objection: The blanket false-go claim must exclude replacing both services’ actual costs with upper liability estimates. Equal actual costs can then pass the economic pathway with probability one at sufficiently large N; confidence coverage for the surrogate does not establish coverage for actual K.

reasoning_steps.title: 9. Derive completion and paired-coverage sample requirements
reasoning_steps.argument: For completion half-width h, N≥ceil(log(160)/(2h²)): h=0.05 requires 1,016 independent pairs and h=0.03 requires 2,820. For paired Delta half-width h, its range width is 2, so N≥ceil(2 log(160)/h²): h=0.05 requires 4,061 pairs. At N=3,000 the completion half-width is approximately 0.0291 and the Delta half-width approximately 0.0582; certification therefore requires observed F completion at least about 92.91% and observed advantage at least about 15.82 points. These are analytical requirements, not measured rates. The ceiling matters: if B truly exceeds 90% completion, F cannot improve it by 10 points; if B is exactly 90%, that pathway requires perfect population completion. Cost improvement may therefore be the relevant pathway for an already effective baseline.

review.rationale: Solving the stated radii for N gives the reported ceilings 1,016, 2,820 and 4,061. The N=3,000 radii and certification thresholds agree with those formulas. The population ceiling p_F≤1 establishes the stated limitation of the 10-point advantage pathway.

reasoning_steps.title: 10. Distinguish precision from power and expose cost sensitivity
reasoning_steps.argument: For a bounded mean with range width w, a true favorable margin g beyond its hurdle is certified with probability at least 1−beta if N≥w²[ sqrt(log(160)/2)+sqrt(log(1/beta)/2) ]²/g². This follows by adding the confidence radius to the one-sided Hoeffding sampling deviation. With beta=0.20, true p_F=0.95 versus the 0.90 hurdle is certifiable with at least 80% probability at N=2,500; true Delta=0.15 versus 0.10 requires N=10,000 under this conservative bound. These are individual-gate power guarantees, not joint pilot power. For K precision e, require m≥ceil((M_F+0.80M_B)² log(160)/(2e²)). If both cost bounds equal M, half-width 0.10M needs 823 independent two-task blocks, or 1,646 task pairs; half-width 0.02M needs 20,555 blocks, or 41,110 pairs. This is normalized sensitivity, not a dollar scenario. A rare expensive tail can make cost certification impractical in 90 days. Moreover K=(R−0.80)mu_B p_F for R=q_F/q_B, so a 20% saving exactly at R=0.80 supplies no favorable margin at all.

review.rationale: Adding the confidence radius to a one-sided Hoeffding deviation yields the stated individual-gate power bound. The conservative rounded counts and normalized cost-precision counts satisfy their formulas, and K=(R−0.80)mu_B p_F follows algebraically.

reasoning_steps.title: 11. Distinguish safety-stop, no-go and inconclusive
reasoning_steps.argument: Safety-stop: immediately suspend affected routing on a confirmed forbidden controlled handoff, unauthorized derived-artifact disclosure, unreserved paid attempt or verified cap breach; investigate rather than average the incident into a success rate. Missing safety instrumentation blocks go but is not evidence of a breach. Statistical no-go: U_pF<0.90, or both benefit pathways are ruled out—U_Delta<0.10 and either L_K>0 or U_Delta<−0.02. A definite campus contract/security veto or infeasible funding is an administrative no-go, separately labeled. Inconclusive: bounds overlap a required hurdle, sample assumptions fail, evidence is missing, or neither a go nor a no-go condition holds. Failure to reject a hurdle is not evidence that it was met. No paid trial runs after budget exhaustion; resulting service refusals stay in the enrolled denominator. A pilot stopped for safety has no deployment go regardless of favorable completion estimates.

review.rationale: Safety-stop, missing-instrumentation and inconclusive classifications are appropriately separated. For exact K, the no-go Boolean expression is the complement of the two benefit pathways on the simultaneous-coverage event.
review.objection: Economic no-go also needs signed settlement uncertainty: overestimated federation costs can spuriously make L_K positive. Apply a lower confidence bound to a valid lower contrast for actual K, not a contrast containing arbitrary upper cost estimates.

reasoning_steps.title: 12. Make the 90-day collection plan executable without optional stopping
reasoning_steps.argument: Days 1–30: security owns approved domains and fault-test oracles; computing owns load blocks, queues, hardware-fit and independent egress instrumentation; procurement/finance owns liability bounds and cost allocations; faculty and student representatives own task rubrics, deadlines and blinded adjudication; an evaluation lead freezes sampling, N, analysis and exclusions. Include coding, routine analysis, scientific reasoning, multimodal/long-context, agentic, sensitive and reproducible-batch strata, with peak, cold-start and maintenance conditions. Days 31–60: run synthetic safety/fault tests and estimate variance/dependence using a development set excluded from confirmatory analysis. Days 61–90: collect the frozen confirmatory sample under approved hard caps, then analyze once after every episode’s deadline and the declared billing-reconciliation cutoff. Safety monitoring is continuous, but favorable interim estimates do not permit early statistical go. Insufficient independent units by day 90 means inconclusive; extension needs a fresh approved plan or a prespecified sequential method. If the budget cannot support four service executions per episode, prioritize the B–F paired comparison and clearly label reduced descriptive coverage of baselines 1 and 2.

review.rationale: The proposed development/confirmation split, frozen final analysis and prohibition on favorable interim stopping are compatible with the fixed-sample guarantee. Independent-unit and budget shortfalls are explicitly classified as inconclusive rather than quietly reducing the sample or escalating spending.

reasoning_steps.title: 13. Preserve autonomy, fairness and evidence limitations
reasoning_steps.argument: Overall mixture success cannot certify each campus, task class or protected queue. Report campus/task/load-stratum completion, refusal reasons, queue-deadline misses, starvation, throughput, availability, provenance completeness, staff hours and cost attribution. A deployment rule requiring a separate completion floor for every campus needs additional simultaneous intervals and enough independent units per campus; the pooled sample counts above do not establish that. Governance must approve those floors and interactive/batch shares before deployment. Retain the earlier negative constraints: separated check-then-send is not current-policy handoff enforcement, and releasing an unresolved timeout hold can permit overspending. The supplied cycle-2 extract describes conditional models, not implementation evidence; o411 remains recorded as addressed analytically, while its contract and operational duties and the other unresolved ledger entries stay open. Federation and frontier routing remain hypothetical extensions. The brief attributes protocol translation, WDRR, quotas, logging and telemetry to the published campus MindRouter gateway; current source verification, comparative usefulness and deployment readiness are not established here.

review.rationale: A pooled mixture mean cannot entail campus- or stratum-specific floors; additional simultaneous inference is correctly required. The step preserves conditional safety constraints and distinguishes brief-attributed MindRouter descriptions from inspected sources and hypothetical extensions.

strategy_findings.skeptic_response:
The statistical design makes substantial progress on the current question. Its offered-demand denominator, paired comparison, fixed-sample Hoeffding bounds, multiplicity allocation and distinction between safety-stop, no-go and inconclusive are sound under the stated independence assumptions. The sample-size arithmetic checks analytically. No computation or pilot was executed.

One material economic inference needs correction. Conservative upper liability estimates cannot simply replace both services’ actual costs in the contrast K: baseline cost enters with a negative coefficient, so overestimating it can falsely favor federation. For example, let every episode succeed, actual costs equal 1 for both services, federation’s cost be settled at 1, and baseline’s unresolved charge have an upper bound of 2 and a known lower bound of 1. Substituting upper bounds gives K=−0.60 although the actual cost-per-useful-task ratio is 1, not at most 0.80. At N=30,000 identical independent pairs, the proposed completion and noninferiority bounds pass, and the substituted-cost upper confidence bound is approximately −0.566. Thus sampling uncertainty can vanish while settlement uncertainty still produces a false economic conclusion. This refutes that substitution, not the fixed-cost statistical theorem or federation generally.

A direct repair is available without execution. Record charge intervals [l_si,u_si]. In the two-task product, an upper bound on actual K uses federation upper costs and baseline lower costs; a lower bound uses federation lower costs and baseline upper costs. Apply one upper-tail bound to the upper contrast and one lower-tail bound to the lower contrast. Together with the six existing probability/coverage tails, eight tails at 0.00625 each retain the same log(160) allocation and 5% union bound. Economic go uses the upper contrast’s upper confidence endpoint; economic exclusion uses the lower contrast’s lower endpoint. Alternatively, require settled costs for both services and otherwise leave economics inconclusive.

A second important feasibility qualification is that the economic pathway’s proposed −2-point noninferiority safeguard can dominate the advertised sample sizes. With observed paired difference zero, its current Hoeffding rule needs at least ceil(2 log(160)/0.02²)=25,376 independent pairs merely to make its lower endpoint reach −0.02. The 1,646-pair normalized cost example alone therefore cannot support economic go. This is a planning constraint, not evidence that an actual 90-day pilot is infeasible.

The cycle-2 handoff model remains a conditional reference design, not deployment evidence. Its analytical ordering result need not be rewritten. Publications, dated prices, actual campus approvals, independent sampling feasibility, implementation tests and four-baseline measurements remain outstanding. The brief’s 2026-10-31 review date is not an access date established by this review.
objections: Material and recoverable, cycle 3: using upper liability estimates for both services does not conservatively bound actual economic advantage because baseline cost has a negative coefficient in K. The equal-actual-cost example in the response shows false economic certification if that substitution is allowed.

Material and recoverable feasibility limitation: economic-pathway planning must include the −0.02 completion noninferiority gate. At observed equal completion, its current bound needs 25,376 independent pairs, not merely the smaller cost-precision example.

Material and recoverable sampling limitation: reset blocks and representative task pairs are proposed, not demonstrated independent units. Shared queues, budget depletion, maintenance and repeated researchers prevent interpreting raw task counts as the required independent sample.

Material evidence limitation retained from cycle 2: complete mediation, fencing, campus acceptance, recipient obligations, current publications, contracts, prices and operational measurements remain unestablished.

Retained negative constraints: cycle 2 artifact 8712830f-b69e-476e-b94d-18be7ea7c043 supplies the check–revocation–handoff counterexample. It also reports the cycle-1 premature-timeout-release counterexample, whose original artifact is only a pointer here; neither unsafe candidate may be treated as established.

outcome.conclusion:
### Partial finding

Conditional on: The formal contract defines effective revocation at durable broker commit and release at positive OS transport acceptance; campus approval of that contract is not presumed; One trusted serialization mechanism orders all covered policy commits and managed OS submission operations; no other authority makes a newer covered policy effective outside that order; Exclusive ownership is enforced at submission admission, not inferred solely from a cached ownership flag. Withdrawal/fencing and admission have a consistent order, including any in-flight operation; Identity, conservative classification, destination authentication and immutable content/destination bindings are trustworthy; ambiguous classification is denied and all covered content paths are mediated; The transport has no independently flushing application-content queue beyond the declared OS boundary; serialization continues through the synchronous nonblocking OS operation; Committed policy, intents and reservations are durable; recovery cannot roll back acknowledged commits, replay uncertain attempts automatically, or enable before ownership and ledger recovery are complete; All spending within each claimed cap is accounted for, every billable attempt has an enforceable aggregate liability bound, hierarchical reservations are atomic, and settlement evidence is trustworthy. Under the Investigator's listed serialization, ownership-enforcement, mediation, transport, durability and bounded-liability premises, the proposed machine authorizes each new OS acceptance using the latest committed policy and preserves covered hierarchical budget caps. Administrator-path loss alone does not disable submission; observed uncertainty or effectively enforced ownership loss does. This is a conditional specification result, not evidence that MindRouter or a federation implements it.

Cycle 3 steps 1–6 distinguish administrator request, durable commit, ownership failure and OS acceptance using two explicit histories. Step 7 proves authorization by induction because the final guard and OS operation exclude policy mutation. Steps 8–9 specify separate commitment and OS-boundary observation oracles, retaining UNKNOWN for missing evidence. Steps 10–11 preserve budget caps through atomic reservation and nonincreasing settlement, while retaining liability after ambiguous outcomes. Step 12 correctly limits transfer from peer results and avoids a deployment or federation-benefit claim.

The saved review does not establish a complete answer to the project question.

### Findings across strategies
- **Sovereignty and trust boundaries — partial finding.** Conditional on: The formal contract defines effective revocation at durable broker commit and release at positive OS transport acceptance; campus approval of that contract is not presumed; One trusted serialization mechanism orders all covered policy commits and managed OS submission operations; no other authority makes a newer covered policy effective outside that order; Exclusive ownership is enforced at submission admission, not inferred solely from a cached ownership flag. Withdrawal/fencing and admission have a consistent order, including any in-flight operation; Identity, conservative classification, destination authentication and immutable content/destination bindings are trustworthy; ambiguous classification is denied and all covered content paths are mediated; The transport has no independently flushing application-content queue beyond the declared OS boundary; serialization continues through the synchronous nonblocking OS operation; Committed policy, intents and reservations are durable; recovery cannot roll back acknowledged commits, replay uncertain attempts automatically, or enable before ownership and ledger recovery are complete; All spending within each claimed cap is accounted for, every billable attempt has an enforceable aggregate liability bound, hierarchical reservations are atomic, and settlement evidence is trustworthy. Under the Investigator's listed serialization, ownership-enforcement, mediation, transport, durability and bounded-liability premises, the proposed machine authorizes each new OS acceptance using the latest committed policy and preserves covered hierarchical budget caps. Administrator-path loss alone does not disable submission; observed uncertainty or effectively enforced ownership loss does. This is a conditional specification result, not evidence that MindRouter or a federation implements it. (Evidence: Artifact 1, Artifact 5, Artifact 6)
- **Fairness, reliability and pilot — partial finding.** Conditional on: For the statistical guarantee, paired episode vectors are independent identically distributed draws from a prespecified target task/load mixture, or the analysis uses genuinely independent fixed-size reset blocks as its units; Outcomes, episode enrollment, deadlines, rubrics, multiplicity allocation and the final sample size are fixed before confirmatory outcomes are inspected; missing adjudication counts as failure and favorable optional stopping is prohibited; For economic certification only, all covered costs use a common declared demand scale, nonnegative enforceable bounds M_F and M_B, conservative treatment of unresolved liability, approved fixed-cost allocations and a known positive baseline mean cost; Both service variants can be evaluated within approved domains without unsafe replication or interference invalidating their paired comparison; The proposed numerical gates are adopted only as provisional pilot decision criteria; they are not asserted to be existing university policy or accepted deployment thresholds. Conditional on the Investigator’s listed sampling, preregistration, bounded-cost, approved-domain and provisional-governance assumptions, the fixed-sample confidence construction controls false statistical certification for the probability gates and for economic contrasts formed from exact settled costs. The stated extension to conservatively estimated unresolved costs is not yet justified. No comparative winner, deployment safety or economic advantage has been established. (Evidence: Artifact 2, Artifact 3, Artifact 4)

- Campus acceptance of delayed, commit-time revocation and the OS-acceptance boundary is absent.
